title: 嘉靖二十九年進士登科錄
text:
進士出身等第恭依
太祖高皇帝欽定資格第一甲例取三名第一名從
六品第二第三名正七品賜進士及第第二甲
從七品賜進士出身第三甲正八品賜同進士
出身奉
聖旨是欽此
讀卷官
特進光祿大夫柱國少師兼太子太師吏部尚書華蓋殿大學士嚴嵩〔乙丑進士〕
資善大夫禮部尚書兼文淵閣大學士張治〔辛巳進士〕
資政大夫吏部尚書夏邦謨〔戊辰進士〕

punctuated:
進士出身等第，恭依太祖高皇帝欽定資格：第一甲例取三名，第一名從六品，第二、第三名正七品，賜進士及第；第二甲從七品，賜進士出身；第三甲正八品，賜同進士出身。奉聖旨：「是。」欽此。

讀卷官

特進光祿大夫、柱國、少師兼太子太師、吏部尚書、華蓋殿大學士嚴嵩〔乙丑進士〕。
資善大夫、禮部尚書兼文淵閣大學士張治〔辛巳進士〕。
資政大夫、吏部尚書夏邦謨〔戊辰進士〕。
translation_en:
The grades of status conferred upon metropolitan graduates respectfully follow the qualifications imperially established by Emperor Taizu Gao: the first class customarily comprises three men. The first receives lower sixth rank, and the second and third receive upper seventh rank; they are granted metropolitan graduate status with honors. Those in the second class receive lower seventh rank and are granted metropolitan graduate status. Those in the third class receive upper eighth rank and are granted status equivalent to metropolitan graduates. The imperial rescript was received: “Approved.” Respectfully received.

Examination Paper Readers

Yan Song held the titles Grand Master for Special Advancement and Glorious Happiness, Pillar of State, and Junior Preceptor, concurrently serving as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Huagai Hall. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the yichou year.〕

Zhang Zhi held the title Grand Master for Fostering Goodness and served as Minister of Rites, concurrently Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the xinsi year.〕

Xia Bangmo held the title Grand Master for Aiding in Government and served as Minister of Personnel. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the wuchen year.〕

translation_en:
Pan Huang, Grand Master for Fostering Goodness and Minister of Revenue, was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the xinsi year.

Liu Ren, Grand Master for Fostering Goodness and Minister of Justice, was a metropolitan graduate of the dingchou year.

Li Shi'ao, Minister of Works, was a metropolitan graduate of the guiwei year.

Tu Qiao, Grand Master for Aid in Governance and Left Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate, was a metropolitan graduate of the xinwei year.

Ouyang De, Grand Master for Excellent Counsel, in charge of the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent, and Left Vice Minister of Personnel concurrently serving as Academician of the Hanlin Academy, was a metropolitan graduate of the guiwei year.

Sun Hui, Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Transmission Commissioner of the Office of Transmission, was a metropolitan graduate of the jiaxu year.

Luo Yong, Grand Master for Excellent Counsel and Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, was a metropolitan graduate of the guiwei year.

Li Ben, Grand Master for Central Compliance and Junior Supervisor of the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent concurrently serving as Academician of the Hanlin Academy, was a metropolitan graduate of the renchen year.

Wang Yongbin, Junior Supervisor of the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent concurrently serving as Academician Reader-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy, was a metropolitan graduate of the xinsi year.

Min Rulin, Academician Reader-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy and Grand Master for Upright Service, was a metropolitan graduate of the renchen year.

Proctors:

Xu Jie, Grand Master for Fostering Goodness and Minister of Rites concurrently serving as Academician of the Hanlin Academy, was a metropolitan graduate of the guiwei year.

Wang Chongqing, Grand Master for Excellent Counsel and Left Vice Minister of Rites, was a metropolitan graduate of the wuchen year.

Examination Monitoring Officials:

Huang Rugui, Gentleman for Scholarly Service and Investigating Censor for the Shandong Circuit, was a metropolitan graduate of the wuxu year.

Xiao Shiyan, Gentleman for Scholarly Service and Investigating Censor for the Jiangxi Circuit, was a metropolitan graduate of the wuxu year.

Officials Receiving Examination Scripts:

Guo Pu, Reader-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy and Gentleman for Fostering Virtue, was a metropolitan graduate of the yiwei year.

Zhao Zhenji, Hanlin Academy Junior Compiler and Gentleman for Scholarly Service, was a metropolitan graduate of the yiwei year.

正議大夫、資治尹、通政使司通政使兼司經局正字周令，秀才。通議大夫、通政使司通政使張文憲，癸未進士。嘉議大夫、掌鴻臚寺事太常寺卿吳祖乾，官生。亞中大夫、光祿寺卿高澄，己丑進士。中大夫、光祿寺卿談相，儒士。中憲大夫、掌尚寶司事太常寺少卿嚴世蕃，官生。奉政大夫、大理寺右寺丞王槐，生員。奉政大夫、尚寶司卿謝敏行，官生。翰林院修撰、儒林郎茅瓚，戌戌進士。翰林院檢討、徵仕郎林庭機，乙未進士。翰林院檢討、徵仕郎郭盤，乙未進士。承德郎、尚寶司司丞孫墀，監生。承事郎、禮科都給事中楊思忠，辛丑進士。承事郎、兵科都給事中俞鸞，辛丑進士。朝議大夫、山東布政使司右參議李宏，癸酉貢士。翰林院掌典籍事、儒林郎、大理寺左寺左寺副劉鎧，監生。文林郎、協掌典籍事、大理寺右寺右評事吳應鳳，儒士。
translation_en:
Zhang Binghu, Gentleman for Literary Service and Left Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Personnel, was a metropolitan graduate of the year transcribed as 戌戌 [?]. Ye Tang, Gentleman for Rendering Service and Chief Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Revenue, was a metropolitan graduate of the xinchou year (1541).

Sealing Officials:

Zhou Ling, Grand Master for Correct Counsel and Governor for Aid in Governance, was Transmission Commissioner in the Office of Transmission and concurrently Proofreader in the Editorial Service. He was a cultivated talent (xiucai).

Zhang Wenxian, Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Transmission Commissioner in the Office of Transmission, was a metropolitan graduate of the guiwei year (1523).

Wu Zuqian, Grand Master for Excellent Counsel and Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, administered the Court of State Ceremonial. He was a student admitted by virtue of official family status.

Gao Cheng, Grand Master of the Second Rank and Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, was a metropolitan graduate of the jichou year (1529).

Tan Xiang, Grand Master of the Palace and Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, was a Confucian scholar.

Yan Shifan, Grand Master for Constitutional Service and Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, administered the Imperial Seals Office. He was a student admitted by virtue of official family status.

Wang Huai, Grand Master for Fostering Governance and Right Assistant Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, was a government school student.

Xie Minxing, Grand Master for Fostering Governance and Chief Minister of the Imperial Seals Office, was a student admitted by virtue of official family status.

Mao Zan, Senior Compiler in the Hanlin Academy and Gentleman for Confucian Service, was a metropolitan graduate of the year transcribed as 戌戌 [?].

Lin Tingji, Examining Editor in the Hanlin Academy and Gentleman for Meritorious Service, was a metropolitan graduate of the yiwei year (1535).

Guo Pan, Examining Editor in the Hanlin Academy and Gentleman for Meritorious Service, was a metropolitan graduate of the yiwei year (1535).

Sun Chi, Gentleman for Achieving Virtue and Assistant Director of the Imperial Seals Office, was an Imperial University student.

Yang Sizhong, Gentleman for Rendering Service and Chief Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Rites, was a metropolitan graduate of the xinchou year (1541).

Yu Luan, Gentleman for Rendering Service and Chief Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Military Affairs, was a metropolitan graduate of the xinchou year (1541).

Li Hong, Grand Master for Court Counsel and Right Assistant Administration Commissioner in the Shandong Provincial Administration Commission, was a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the guiyou year (1513).

Liu Kai, responsible for the books and records of the Hanlin Academy, held the rank of Gentleman for Confucian Service and served as Left Vice Supervisor in the Court of Judicial Review [the transcription repeats part of the title: 左寺左寺副; ?]. He was an Imperial University student.

Wu Yingfeng, Gentleman for Literary Service, assisted in administering the books and records and served as Right Case Reviewer in the Right Section of the Court of Judicial Review. He was a Confucian scholar.

三月十九日，
translation_en:
Sequence of Imperial Favors and Honors

On the morning of the fifteenth day of the third month of the twenty-ninth year of Jiajing (1550), the Metropolitan Examination graduates proceeded to the inner palace for the Palace Examination. The Emperor took his seat in Fengtian Hall and personally bestowed the policy question.

On the morning of the eighteenth day of the third month, the civil and military officials attended in court dress, standing in their appointed ranks. That day, the Embroidered-uniform Guard arrayed the ceremonial regalia at the vermilion steps and within the vermilion courtyard. The Emperor took his seat in Fengtian Hall. Officials of the Court of State Ceremonial transmitted the imperial decree and proclaimed the candidates’ names. Officials of the Ministry of Rites carried the yellow results placard, led by drums and music, out through the Chang’an Left Gate. After the placard had been posted outside the gate, officials of Shuntian Prefecture escorted the first-place graduate (zhuangyuan) back to his residence with parasols, canopies, and a ceremonial retinue.

On the nineteenth day of the third month…

translation_en:
A banquet was bestowed at the Ministry of Rites. After the banquet, the graduates proceeded to the Court of State Ceremonial to rehearse the ceremonies.
On the twenty-first day of the third month, court robes, a cap, and a belt were bestowed upon the first-ranked graduate (zhuangyuan), and paper currency upon the metropolitan graduates (jinshi).
On the twenty-second day of the third month, the first-ranked graduate led the other metropolitan graduates in submitting a memorial expressing gratitude for the imperial favor.
On the twenty-third day of the third month, the first-ranked graduate led the other metropolitan graduates to the temple of Confucius, the First Teacher, to perform the vegetable-offering rite.
Upon a memorialized request from the Ministry of Rites, the Ministry of Works was ordered to erect a stone stele at the Directorate of Education and inscribe the graduates’ names upon it.

translation_en:
First Class: three men, granted the degree of metropolitan graduate (jinshi) with honors.

Tang Ruji: registered in a civilian household in Lanxi County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang; a student of the Directorate of Education, specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Siji; he ranked twenty-eighth among his brothers and male cousins and was aged thirty-seven, born on the seventh day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather Xian, through the extension of imperial favor, and his grandfather Xue had both received successive posthumous grants of the titles Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of War. His father Long was formerly Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Personnel. His father's former wife, née Xu, had received successive posthumous grants of the title Lady of the First Rank; his mother, née Liu, had also been posthumously granted that title. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Ruqi, a student of the Directorate of Education; his younger brothers were Ruzhou, a tribute scholar, Rumei, Ruxiu, Ruwei, Ruming, Ruyang, Ruli, Ruli (汝澧), Ruhui, and Ruzha. He married a woman née Wu. He placed 103rd in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eleventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lü Tiaoyang: registered in a military household of the Guilin Central Guard, Guangxi, and a native of Lingui County; a student of the Directorate of Education, specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Heqing; he ranked third among his brothers and male cousins and was aged thirty-five, born on the eighteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian, his grandfather Gang, and his father Zhang, a magistrate; his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yingyang, and his younger brothers were Mingyang and Duanyang. He married a woman née Zhu and subsequently a woman née Zhang. He placed twenty-second in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and eighty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Jinhe: registered in a civilian household in Poyang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi; a county government school student, specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Jiezhi; he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins and was aged thirty-six, born on the third day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Xian was Administrator of the household of the Prince of Yi; his grandfather Xin was posthumously granted the title Director in the Ministry of Justice; his father Di was a prefect. His mother, née Fan, was granted the title Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Jinli. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Ji. He placed thirty-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 282nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Second Class: 95 men, granted metropolitan graduate (jinshi) status.

Tian Yang, registered in a military household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an supplementary student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Tinghan; he ranked first in birth order and was thirty-one years old, born on the fifth day of the intercalary eighth month. His great-grandfather was Long, posthumously or honorifically appointed Director of a bureau in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel; his grandfather was Kun, a Department Magistrate; and his father was Wu. His mother was née Yu, and his stepmother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Mei and Tao; his younger brothers were Gui, Nuo, Geng, Zhu, Bang, Qi, Gai, Ting, and Quan. He married a woman née Zhuang and subsequently a woman née Cai. He placed tenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 127th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Jian, registered in a civilian household in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Xinke; he ranked second in birth order and was forty-two years old, born on the eleventh day of the intercalary ninth month. His great-grandfather was Huidi; his grandfather was Li; and his father was Fu, an Assistant Prefect. His father's former wife was née Jin, and his mother was née Xu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Ce, and his younger brother was Jie, a Director of Yin-Yang Studies. He married a woman née Sun. He placed twentieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 300th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zong Chen, registered in a civilian household in Xinghua County, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the county school specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Zixiang; he ranked first in birth order and was twenty-six years old, born on the fourth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Yu; his grandfather was Xianzhang; and his father was Zhou, a District Magistrate. His mother was née Xu. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Yuan. He married a woman née Lu. He placed twenty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 178th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Bao Yinglin, registered in Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Zirui; he ranked third in birth order and was aged twenty-three, born on the seventh day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuanbian, a county Chief Clerk; his grandfather was Xiang, an honorary Longevity Official; his father was Ji, and his mother was née Hu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Duo, and his younger brothers were Yingfang and Yingxi. His wife was née Chen. He placed fiftieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 171st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Lianzhang, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student of the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Jihui; he ranked sixth in birth order and was aged twenty, born on the twenty-third day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yushi; his grandfather was Shiyi, granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Rites and posthumously awarded that of Surveillance Vice Commissioner. His father was Yingbiao, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner; his mother was née Chen, granted the title of Lady of Respect. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Canzhang, a student of the Imperial University, Xuanzhang, Huanzhang, and Yaozhang; his younger brother was Langzhang. His wife was née Hong. He placed fifty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and nineteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jin Lijing, registered in Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Zhongfu; he ranked seventeenth in birth order and was aged thirty-six, born on the tenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was 𨥤 [pronunciation uncertain]; his grandfather was Hong, granted the title of Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice. His father was Benheng, Surveillance Vice Commissioner serving as Education Intendant; his mother was née Zhang, granted the title of Lady of Peace. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Li’ai, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the same examination year; his younger brothers were Lixiang, a student of the Imperial University, and Lichang. His wife was née Chen; he subsequently married a woman née Wang. He placed twenty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 295th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Shiguan, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Guoguang; he ranked fifth in birth order and was aged twenty-seven, born on the thirteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sili; his grandfather was Shun; his father was Zhu, a Magistrate; and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shiming, and his younger brothers were Shiyu and Shizhi. His wife was née Chen. He placed first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fifty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Fang Hongjing, registered in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Dingzhi; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the eighteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Maofu; his grandfather, Taisun; his father, Hu; his mother, née Hu; and his stepmother, née Zheng. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Xuanjing and Yijing, and his younger brothers were Wujing, Benjing, and Shoujing. He married a woman née Zheng. He placed tenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fu Xiaqi, registered in Nan’an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Tinghuang; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged forty-two, and was born on the second day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Liang; his grandfather, Gui; his father, Ling; and his mother, née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shangqi, Zhouqi, and Xianqi. He married a woman née Wu. He placed sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Yidao, registered in Dongguan County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a military household and was an additional student at the county school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Guanqing; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-six, and was born on the seventeenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zusheng; his grandfather, Jizhen; his father, Guangui; and his mother, née Feng. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Yida, Yisui, and Yitong. He married a woman née Li. He placed thirty-ninth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 266th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Yuanyan, registered in Huai’an County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Zhongwen; he ranked sixth among his brothers, was aged thirty-nine, and was born on the seventeenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongtan; his grandfather, Cong; his father, Liangce, who had been granted the honorary title of Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; and his mother, née Wu, who had been granted the title of Lady of Peace (anren). Both parents were living. His elder brother Yuanke was a Prefect. He married a woman née Lan and subsequently a woman née Li. He placed forty-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 146th in the Metropolitan Examination.

陸綸〔貫浙江湖州府歸安縣民籍，府學生，治春秋，字理之，行三，年四十一，四月十九日生〕。曾祖坦，祖肇，父瑞，母卞氏。永感下，兄經、墀，弟科〔監生〕、崑、紳、稷、絃、紘，娶卞氏。浙江鄉試第九名，會試第八十四名。

游天廷〔貫福建鎮海衛銅山所軍籍，歲貢生，治詩經，字士達，行二，年三十七，十二月初三日生〕。曾祖存凱，祖洪珍，父晃，前母楊氏，母高氏。慈侍下，兄天衢，娶劉氏。順天府鄉試第二十二名，會試第二十九名。

黃憲卿〔貫直隸常州府武進縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字弘度，行一，年四十，八月二十六日生〕。曾祖孟瓛〔南京太常寺典簿，贈刑部員外郎〕，祖俊〔運使，進階資治少尹〕，父誥〔七品散官〕，母徐氏。具慶下，弟懋卿，娶李氏。應天府鄉試第四十二名，會試第四十九名。
translation_en:
Qin Gongji 欽拱極 was registered in an artisan household in Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, and was a native of Taicang Subprefecture; he was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes, with the courtesy name Zichen, fourth in family order, aged forty-three, and born on the eleventh day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather Xuan, his father Tai, and his mother née Li; his father was living and his mother deceased; his younger brothers were Huiji, Fuji 敷極, Fuji 福極, Xiji, Taiji, Shouji, and Youji; his wife was née Wang; he placed sixteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fiftieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Lun 陸綸 was registered in a civilian household in Gui’an County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang; he was a prefectural school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, with the courtesy name Lizhi, third in family order, aged forty-one, and born on the nineteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Tan, his grandfather Zhao, his father Rui, and his mother née Bian; both parents were deceased; his elder brothers were Jing and Chi, and his younger brothers were Ke (a National University student), Kun, Shen, Ji, Xian, and Hong; his wife was née Bian; he placed ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eighty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

You Tianting 游天廷 was registered in a military household of the Tongshan Battalion, Zhenhai Guard, Fujian; he was an annual tribute student specializing in the Book of Odes, with the courtesy name Shida, second in family order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the third day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Cunkai, his grandfather Hongzhen, and his father Huang; his father’s former wife was née Yang and his mother née Gao; his mother was living and his father deceased; his elder brother was Tianqu; his wife was née Liu; he placed twenty-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Xianqing 黃憲卿 was registered in a civilian household in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili; he was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, with the courtesy name Hongdu, first in family order, aged forty, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Menghuan (Registrar in the Nanjing Court of Imperial Sacrifices, posthumously granted the title of Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice), his grandfather Jun (Transport Commissioner, advanced to the prestige title Zizhi shaoyin), his father Gao (holder of a seventh-rank prestige title), and his mother née Xu; both parents were living; his younger brother was Maoqing; his wife was née Li; he placed forty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

魏裳〔貫湖廣武昌府蒲圻縣，軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字順甫，行九，年三十一，十月初八日生〕。曾祖碧，祖溶〔知縣〕，父正蒙，母李氏。具慶下，兄表、頃，弟製、裘、袤、裁、襄、袗、褫、褒，娶劉氏。湖廣鄉試第十二名，會試第六十五名。

胡膏〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字來霑，行六，年四十二，十月二十六日生〕。曾祖世澤，祖溥，父珩，母項氏。永感下，兄朝明〔巡檢〕、靑〔封翰林院編修〕、𦚢，弟能、龍、肬、寵、脩、脭、胄、肖，娶俞氏。浙江鄉試第八十三名，會試第二十二名。
translation_en:
Zhang Shouzong, registered in Shuide Native Office, Sinan Prefecture, Guizhou, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Jixian; he ranked first in his family and was twenty-five years old, born on the fifth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Jin, his grandfather Yiling, and his father Wei; his mother was née Xiang. Both parents were living. His wife was née Xiong. He placed sixth in the Guizhou Provincial Examination and seventy-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Guangchen, registered in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student at the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhongxi; he ranked second in his family and was twenty-four years old, born on the twenty-first day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Xian, his grandfather Qi, and his father Shaomin; his mother was née Liang. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Guangzhou, a tribute scholar (gongshi); his younger brothers were Guangzhai, Guangzai, Guangning, Guangcai, Guangshi, and Guang’an. His wife was née Xu. He placed sixty-first in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and one hundred twenty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wei Shang, registered in Puqi County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shunfu; he ranked ninth in his family and was thirty-one years old, born on the eighth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Bi, his grandfather Rong, a district magistrate, and his father Zhengmeng; his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Biao and Qing [?]; his younger brothers were Zhi, Qiu, Mao, Cai, Xiang, Zhen, Chi, and Bao. His wife was née Liu. He placed twelfth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and sixty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Gao, registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Laizhan; he ranked sixth in his family and was forty-two years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Shize, his grandfather Pu, and his father Heng; his mother was née Xiang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Chaoming, a police chief; Qing, granted the honorary title of Hanlin Academy Compiler; and 𦚢 [name reading uncertain]. His younger brothers were Neng, Long, You, Chong, Xiu, Cheng, Zhou, and Xiao. His wife was née Yu. He placed eighty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and twenty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

李淑〔貫湖廣承天府京山縣民籍，江西安仁縣人，國子生，治詩經，字師孟，行一，年三十四，二月初七日生〕。曾祖九淵，祖珏，父景瑞，母楊氏。具慶下，娶王氏，繼娶陳氏。湖廣鄉試第三十九名，會試第一百二十五名。

熊桴〔貫湖廣武昌府武昌縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字元乗，行三，年四十四，正月初九日生〕。曾祖友信〔知縣〕，祖鐩〔壽官〕，父清〔縣丞〕，前母周氏，母萬氏。永感下，兄極〔衛經歷〕、栻〔陰陽訓術〕，娶陳氏。湖廣鄉試第七十七名，會試第二百五十三名。

白啓常〔貫錦衣衛官籍，直隸武進縣人，縣學附學生，治詩經，字伯倫，行一，年二十二，三月初三日生〕。曾祖昂〔光禄大夫、柱國、太子太傅、刑部尚書，贈太保，謚康敏〕，祖圻〔通議大夫、都察院右副都御史〕，父悅〔尚寶司司丞〕，嫡母鄒氏〔封孺人〕，繼母楊氏〔封孺人〕，生母陳氏。具慶下，兄啓京〔刑部主事〕、仲儒、應震、應䝉〔監生〕、啓東、啓明、啓業、應尾、應翼、應奎、應星、啓髙，娶富氏。應天府鄉試第一百名，會試第五十一名。

translation_en:
Li Shu 李淑, registered in a civilian household in Jingshan County, Chengtian Prefecture, Huguang, was a native of Anren County, Jiangxi, and a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shimeng. He ranked first in birth order, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the seventh day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jiuyuan, his grandfather Jue, and his father Jingrui; his mother was née Yang. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed thirty-ninth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 125th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiong Fu 熊桴 was registered in a civilian household in Wuchang County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yuancheng. He ranked third in birth order, was aged forty-four, and was born on the ninth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Youxin, a Magistrate; his grandfather was Sui, an honorary official recognized for longevity; and his father was Qing, a Vice Magistrate. His father's former wife was née Zhou, and his mother was née Wan. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Ji, a Registrar in a Guard, and Shi, an Instructor in a School of Yin and Yang. He married a woman née Chen. He placed seventy-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 253rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bai Qichang 白啓常 was registered in an official household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Wujin County in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was an additional student of the county school and specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Bolun. He ranked first in birth order, was aged twenty-two, and was born on the third day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ang, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Pillar of the State, Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Justice, posthumously awarded the title Grand Guardian and the name Kangmin. His grandfather was Qi, Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Censor-in-chief of the Censorate. His father was Yue, Assistant Director of the Office of Imperial Seals. His legal mother was née Zou and his stepmother née Yang, each granted the title Lady; his birth mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qijing, a Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; Zhongru; Yingzhen; Yingmeng, a student of the Directorate of Education; Qidong; Qiming; Qiye; Yingwei; Yingyi; Yingkui; Yingxing; and Qigao. He married a woman née Fu. He placed one hundredth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Dai 李玳 was registered in a civilian household in Bazhou, Shuntian Prefecture, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Tingshi. He ranked second in birth order, was aged forty-three, and was born on the twenty-second day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Da and his grandfather Ming, both honorary officials recognized for charitable service; his father was Shao, a Registrar, and his mother was née Yang. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His elder brother was Pei, and his younger brothers were Hu and Zhu. He married a woman née Xu. He placed sixty-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Ren Minwang, courtesy name Zizhong, was registered in a civilian household in Linfen County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-three, born on the fifth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ben; his grandfather, Ji, was an Assistant Instructor; his father was Min, and his mother was née Fan. His grandparents and parents were living. His younger brothers were Minjing and Minfu, and his wife was née An. He placed ninth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 205th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Rong, courtesy name Renqing, was registered in a military household of Dengzhou Guard, Shandong, and was a native of Yin County, Zhejiang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first in his family and was aged forty-one, born on the eighteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lian; his grandfather, Quan; and his father, Xian. His father's principal wife was née Wang, and his birth mother was née Peng. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Xiu, Qi, Lin, and Cheng, and his wife was née Yang. He placed forty-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 189th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fan Jia, courtesy name Zimei, was registered in a civilian household in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An attached student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked twenty-fifth in his family and was aged thirty-four, born on the twelfth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather, Lu, was a District Magistrate; his grandfather was Yuan; his father, Qi, was a Chief Clerk; and his mother was née Huang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Xiang, Nan, Wu, Chun, Ji, and Ben; his younger brothers were Mu and Zhang, the latter a provincial sacrificial official (shengji guan). His wife was née Shen. He placed thirtieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Shu, courtesy name Shimei, was registered in a civilian household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the prefectural school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked tenth in his family and was aged forty-three, born on the eleventh day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shiqing; his grandfather, Lin, was a District Magistrate; his father was Jue, and his mother was née Lin. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Zao, and his wife was née Chen. He placed fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 256th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Bingshu 吳炳庶 was registered in a military household in Xianju County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Chaozheng and ranked third among his brothers. He was thirty-one, born on the fifteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bangqing; his grandfather, Shushen, was a prefectural registrar, posthumously granted the title Gentleman of Literary Service; and his father, Ronghe, was a county magistrate. His mother, née Wang, was granted the title Lady. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Bingxi, an Imperial University student, and Bingpao, a clerk in a battalion office. He married a woman née Zhu. He placed seventy-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and twenty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Sizan 何思贊 was registered in a military household in Shunde County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. An supplementary student of the county government school specializing in the Book of Rites, he had the courtesy name Shaoxiang and ranked third among his brothers. He was thirty-one, born on the third day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Chang, was a county magistrate; his grandfather, Kui, was posthumously granted the title Gentleman of Literary Service and the office of Investigating Censor; and his father, Ao, was Left Provincial Administration Commissioner. His father's former wife, née Liang, was posthumously granted the title Lady; his mother, née Pan, was granted the same title. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Sicun and Siyi, and his younger brothers were Sishen and Sixu. He married a woman née Liang. He placed twenty-second in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and fifty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yun 張蘊 was registered in a military household in Gaochun County, Yingtian Prefecture. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Yizhen and ranked fifth among his brothers. He was thirty-seven, born on the twenty-third day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu; his grandfather was Xun; and his father, Jie, was an assistant prefect. His mother was née Rui, and his stepmothers were née Zhu and née Chen. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Qin, Xun, Jin, and Dao, and his younger brother was Chang. He married a woman née Yu. He placed forty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred ninety-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Jia 黃甲 was registered in a military household of the Xingwu Guard in Nanjing and was a native of Shangyou County, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Shouqing and ranked fourth among his brothers. He was thirty-two, born on the eleventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cheng; his grandfather was Run; his father was Zhong; and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xuan, Wan, and Yu. He married a woman née Xu. He placed one hundred thirty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred fifty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Ruxiang. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty-six and was born on the twenty-first day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Mian; his grandfather, Yourang; his father, Rong, a clerk in an office (suo); and his mother, née Huang. Both parents were living. He ranked thirty-third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and twentieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Xueshi, registered in Jiading County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was an attached student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ziyan. Second in birth order, he was aged twenty-nine and was born on the sixth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Jie; his grandfather, Jing; his father, Fu; and his mother, née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Xueli. His wife was née Ou; he subsequently married a woman née Wang. He ranked twenty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 194th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liang Youyu, registered in Panyu County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Gongshi. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-two and was born on the sixteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Xin; his grandfather, Zhao, posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor for the Henan Circuit at Nanjing; his father, Shibiao, an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; and his mother, née Zhang, granted the title of Lady (ruren). His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His younger brothers were Youfu, Youzhao, and Youzhen. His wife was née Zhou. He ranked eleventh in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and eighty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Yingpin, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Junbin. Third in birth order, he was aged thirty-one and was born on the eighth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Zongxun; his grandfather, Boyu, granted the title of Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue; and his father, Tuan, an Assistant Prefect. His father's former wife was née Huang, and his mother was née Zhuo. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His elder brothers were Yingke and Yingzheng, and his younger brothers were Yingzhong and Yingquan. His wife was née Yu. He ranked twelfth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 250th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xiantu, registered in Ningling County, Guide Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Yingxiang; he ranked second in his family and was aged twenty-two [?], born on the seventh day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yi, his grandfather Yue, his father Guan, and his mother née Zheng. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Xianshu, Xianqi, Xianke, Xiance, Xianshi, Xianwen, and Xianyan. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed sixty-second in the Henan Provincial Examination and 101st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Tianyou, registered in Fuliang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Youqing; he ranked eighth in his family and was aged forty, born on the tenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bangren; his grandfather Jing received the honorary title of District Magistrate; his father Yu was an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner. His legal mother, née Li, was granted the title of Lady (ruren), and his birth mother was née Hu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Tianxiang and Tiande, both Imperial University students, and Tianmin, a county school student. His younger brothers were Tianxian, a Vice Director in the Ministry of War; Tianzhang; Tianfeng, a tribute scholar; Tianzhi; Tianqiu; Tianheng; Tianpu; Tianchong; and Tianyin. He married a woman née Wang. He placed seventy-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and twenty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wan Zhong, registered in Jinxian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Yanhe; he ranked third in his family and was aged thirty-six, born on the second day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongxi, his grandfather Kongwu, and his father Hu. His legal mother was née Fu, his stepmother née Deng, and his birth mother née Deng. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Bo and his younger brother Chou. He married a woman née Wang. He placed twenty-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 157th in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Kuan, registered in Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Rusu; he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty-seven, born on the first day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yunzhi, his grandfather Kan, and his father Congliang, a Local Office Clerk; his mother was née Wang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother Chong was a tribute scholar, and his younger brother was Cai. He married a woman née Yu. He placed twenty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Zhao, registered in a civilian household in Yanjin County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Ruoshi; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-third day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Liang; his grandfather, Zhen, held an honorary office conferred for longevity; his father, Mi, was an Assistant Prefect; and his mother was née Yang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Xun, a Magistrate, and Gao, an Imperial University student; his younger brothers were Lun, Hui, Yan (an Imperial University student), Shi (an Imperial University student), Zhi, Zou, Ping, Zan, and Cheng. He married a woman née Ren and subsequently a woman née Wang. He ranked eighteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 252nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Sanjie, registered in a military household in Tong'an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yunkang; he was second in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the fourteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Qinzhi, his grandfather Cen, his father Ji, and his mother née Ye. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Sanxi and his younger brother Sanpin. He married a woman née Ye. He ranked twenty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 221st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Daoxing, registered in a civilian household in Yangqu County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, was an attached student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Mingfu; he was first in birth order, aged twenty, and born on the seventh day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Ju; his grandfather, Ding, held an honorary office conferred for longevity; his father, Shangzhi, was a Police Chief; and his mother was née Mi. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Daoming. He married a woman née Yang. He ranked ninth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 291st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Yinghe, registered in a military household in Gui'an County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Wenxiang; he was third in birth order, aged forty-seven, and born on the nineteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather, Qi, held a seventh-rank prestige title; his grandfather, Xiao, was posthumously appointed Magistrate; his father, Ke, was Minister of the Court of Judicial Review; and his mother, née Zhu, was invested with the title of Senior Lady of Purity. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yingqi, Superintendent of a Salt Tax Office, and Yingkui, a Prefectural Judge. He married a woman née Pan. He ranked second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

胡庭蘭〔貫廣東廣州府增城縣，民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字伯賢，行一，年四十，十月十五日生〕。曾祖通，祖璋〔知縣〕，父鳳虞，前母湯氏，母單氏。永感下，弟庭萼，娶張氏，繼娶莫氏、鄧氏。廣東鄉試第一名，會試第三百十三名。

沈應魁〔貫直隸蘇州府常熟縣，民籍，國子生，治禮記，字仲文，行二，年三十七，七月二十三日生〕。曾祖達〔贈刑部主事〕，祖海〔知府〕，父虞〔兵馬司指揮〕，母張氏，繼母程氏。慈侍下，兄應元〔貢士〕，弟應麒〔監生〕、應聘，娶盧氏。應天府鄉試第八十五名，會試第一百五十二名。

柯本〔貫福建興化府莆田縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字正之，行二，年三十四，五月二十八日生〕。曾祖暄〔贈大理寺評事〕，祖英〔知府〕，父維羆〔知縣〕，母盧氏。永感下，兄檀、栻、樞、梡〔俱貢士〕、楠、檟、棐、集、渠、案、礎、檯，弟弟、梃、樸、榦、大蘧、大棱、大栟，娶黃氏。福建鄉試第三十六名，會試第五十四名。
translation_en:
Lü Yao, courtesy name Sihui, was registered in a civilian household in Xian County, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-eight years old, born on the twentieth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Zhi, his grandfather Lin, his father Pai, and his mother Lady Niu; his parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Can and Huang, and he married Lady Tang. He placed twenty-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 223rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Tinglan, courtesy name Boxian, was registered in a civilian household in Zengcheng County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was forty years old, born on the fifteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Tong; his grandfather Zhang served as a magistrate; his father was Fengyu. His father's former wife was Lady Tang, and his mother was Lady Shan. Both his parents were deceased. His younger brother was Ting'e. He married Lady Zhang and subsequently Ladies Mo and Deng. He placed first in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 313th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Yingkui, courtesy name Zhongwen, was registered in a civilian household in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-seven years old, born on the twenty-third day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather Da was posthumously appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Justice; his grandfather Hai served as a prefect; his father Yu served as commander of a Ward-inspecting Office. His mother was Lady Zhang, and his stepmother Lady Cheng. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother Yingyuan was a tribute scholar (gongshi); his younger brothers were Yingqi, an Imperial University student, and Yingpin. He married Lady Lu. He placed eighty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 152nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ke Ben, courtesy name Zhengzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-four years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather Xuan was posthumously appointed a case reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review; his grandfather Ying served as a prefect; his father Weipi served as a magistrate. His mother was Lady Lu, and both his parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Tan, Shi, Shu, and Kuan, all tribute scholars (gongshi), followed by Nan, Jia, Fei, Ji, Qu, An, Chu, and Tai. His younger brothers were Di [?; the transcription repeats the character for “younger brother”], Ting, Pu, Gan, Daqu, Daleng, and Dabing. He married Lady Huang. He placed thirty-sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fifty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

楊一和〔貫雲南雲南府昆明縣，民籍，大理府太和縣人，國子生，治易經，字貞甫，行二，年四十三，八月十五日生〕。曾祖鑑，祖斌〔遇例冠帶〕，父鼐，母陽氏。具慶下，兄一中。娶李氏。雲南鄉試第二十五名，會試第二百六十七名。

高岱〔貫湖廣承天府京山縣，軍籍，鍾祥縣人，國子生，治易經，字伯宗，行一，年四十三，九月初一日生〕。曾祖讓，祖鎮，父節〔教諭〕，母李氏。具慶下，弟嵩、啓〔貢士〕、𡼡〔貢士〕。娶李氏。湖廣鄉試第三名，會試第一百六十七名。

李春芳〔貫福建泉州府同安縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字實夫，行一，年二十六，九月二十三日生〕。曾祖賢〔戶部郎中〕，祖栟〔歲貢生〕，父伯成，母林氏，生母翁氏。慈侍下，弟春菲、春華。娶葉氏。福建鄉試第五十六名，會試第七十六名。
translation_en:
Jin Li’ai 金立愛 was registered in a civilian household in Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Yuanfu; he ranked fifteenth among his brothers and male cousins and was thirty years old, born on the eighth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Ju; his grandfather, Hong, received the honorary title of Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice; his father, Benheng, was an Education Intendant serving as Vice Commissioner of the Provincial Surveillance Commission. His mother, née Zhang, received the title Lady of Peace. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Lijing, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the same examination year; Lixiang, a tribute scholar; and Lichang. He married a woman née Yu and subsequently a woman née Cai. He placed forty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Yihe 楊一和 was registered in a civilian household in Kunming County, Yunnan Prefecture, Yunnan, and was a native of Taihe County, Dali Prefecture. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhenfu; he ranked second among his brothers and male cousins and was forty-three years old, born on the fifteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Jian; his grandfather, Bin, had been granted the privilege of wearing official cap and girdle under an applicable regulation. His father was Nai, and his mother was née Yang 陽. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yizhong. He married a woman née Li. He placed twenty-fifth in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and 267th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Dai 高岱 was registered in a military household in Jingshan County, Chengtian Prefecture, Huguang, and was a native of Zhongxiang County. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Bozong; he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins and was forty-three years old, born on the first day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Rang; his grandfather was Zhen; his father, Jie, was a School Instructor; and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Song; Qi, a tribute scholar; and 𡼡 [name reading uncertain], also a tribute scholar. He married a woman née Li. He placed third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 167th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Chunfang 李春芳 was registered in a civilian household in Tong’an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shifu; he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins and was twenty-six years old, born on the twenty-third day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather, Xian, was a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather, Bing, was an annual tribute student. His father was Bocheng; his mother was née Lin, and his birth mother was née Weng. His father was deceased, and he attended his living mother. His younger brothers were Chunfei and Chunhua. He married a woman née Ye. He placed fifty-sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and seventy-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xu Zhongxing, registered in Changxing County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ziyu; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twentieth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Henglu, his grandfather Li, and his father Jian, an honorary official for longevity; his mother was née Xu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhongfu and Zhonghe, and his wife was née Yang. He ranked thirtieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 126th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Xizhe, registered in Weiyuan County, Jiading Subprefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shuyu; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twenty-second day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Borui, his grandfather Xiang, and his father Zongjiang; his mother was née Wei. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Xishan and his younger brother Xitai; his wife was née Luo. He ranked ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 147th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Yanzuo, registered in Luoyang County, Henan Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shusi; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the sixth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Ji, his grandfather Bian, an honorary official for longevity, and his father Run, a District Magistrate. His mother was née Wang and his stepmother née Zhou. He had living grandparents and parents. His younger brother was Yanchou, and his wife was née Zhang. He ranked sixtieth in the Henan Provincial Examination and thirty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Yue, registered in Qiantang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zijun; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-first day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Chang, his grandfather Jian, an honorary official for longevity, and his father Gui, an official awaiting selection for appointment. His father's former wife was née Shen, and his mother was née Gu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shan and Song, the latter a student of the Directorate of Education; his wife was née Zhu. He ranked sixty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 195th in the Metropolitan Examination.

章懋〔貫四川瀘州衞官籍，浙江長興縣人，國子生，治書經，字世功，行三，年四十三，三月初六日生〕。曾祖旺〔正千戶〕，祖能，父旅，母同氏。具慶下，兄勛〔指揮僉事〕、德、憲，弟愈，娶苟氏。四川鄉試第五十九名，會試第一百六十六名。

朱天球〔貫福建漳州府漳浦縣軍籍，縣學附學生，治禮記，字君玉，行四，年二十三，十月十七日生〕。曾祖德〔壽官〕，祖魯〔壽官〕，父琯，母陳氏。具慶下，兄鴻漸，弟天申，娶涂氏。福建鄉試第三十八名，會試第八十名。

莫如善〔貫龍驤衞軍籍，廣東恩平縣人，國子生，治易經，字子明，行一，年四十，九月初二日生〕。曾祖寅，祖牛，父疑〔錦衣衞冠帶總旗〕，母朱氏〔旌表節婦〕。慈侍下，兄如爵〔監察御史〕，弟如士〔監察御史〕，娶凌氏。順天府鄉試第十四名，會試第二百十七名。

馮臯謨〔貫浙江嘉興府海鹽縣民籍，縣學生，治書經，字明卿，行一，年三十一，十月二十日生〕。曾祖璿〔衞經歷〕，祖金，父乾，母吳氏。具慶下，弟詔、訓、誥、嘉言、昌言、正言，娶朱氏。浙江鄉試第十八名，會試第二百名。
translation_en:
Zhang Mao, registered in an officer household of Luzhou Guard, Sichuan, was a native of Changxing County, Zhejiang, and a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Shigong, and he ranked third in his family. He was forty-three, born on the sixth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wang, a full Battalion Commander; his grandfather was Neng; his father was Lü; and his mother was née Tong. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xun, an Assistant Commander, De, and Xian; his younger brother was Yu. His wife was née Gou. He placed fifty-ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and one hundred sixty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Tianqiu was registered in a military household in Zhangpu County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, and was an attached student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Junyu, and he ranked fourth in his family. He was twenty-three, born on the seventeenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather De and grandfather Lu both held honorary offices conferred for longevity. His father was Guan, and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Hongjian, and his younger brother was Tianshen. His wife was née Tu. He placed thirty-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and eightieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mo Rushan, registered in a military household of Longxiang Guard, was a native of Enping County, Guangdong, and a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ziming, and he ranked first in his family. He was forty, born on the second day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yin; his grandfather was Niu; and his father was Yi, a Company Commander of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard entitled to wear the official cap and belt. His mother, née Zhu, had received an official commendation as a chaste widow. His mother alone was living. His elder brother Rujue and younger brother Rushi were both Investigating Censors. His wife was née Ling. He placed fourteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred seventeenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Gaomo was registered in a civilian household in Haiyan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Mingqing, and he ranked first in his family. He was thirty-one, born on the twentieth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuan, a Guard Registrar; his grandfather was Jin; his father was Qian; and his mother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhao, Xun, Gao, Jiayan, Changyan, and Zhengyan. His wife was née Zhu. He placed eighteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and two hundredth in the Metropolitan Examination.

吳一儒〔貫浙江湖州府歸安縣民籍，嘉興府崇德縣人，國子生，治書經，字望魯，行一，年四十七，九月二十二日生〕。曾祖琛，祖正，父悅，母徐氏。具慶下，弟一民、一相、一臣，娶錢氏。浙江鄉試第十七名，會試第一百六十二名。

陳茂禮〔貫浙江寧波府慈谿縣民籍，縣學附學生，治詩經，字履卿，行三，年二十四，七月二十五日生〕。曾祖志，祖倫，父安，前母馮氏，繼母丘氏，生母王氏。慈侍下，兄茂仁〔國子生〕、茂義〔布政使司左參政〕，弟茂智，娶王氏。浙江鄉試第八十六名，會試第二十一名。

閻光潛〔貫山東兖州府東平州軍籍，州學生，治書經，字孔昭，行二，年三十三，六月初八日生〕。曾祖宏，祖昂〔義官〕，父儒，母趙氏。具慶下，兄光著，弟光含、承構，娶靳氏。山東鄉試第二十三名，會試第七十四名。

李纘〔貫福建泉州府晉江縣民籍，國子生，治禮記，字存孝，行二，年三十九，十月十七日生〕。曾祖文采，祖朝機，父興仁，母陳氏，繼母張氏、謝氏。具慶下，兄續，娶吳氏。福建鄉試第十名，會試第四名。
translation_en:
Wu Yiru, courtesy name Wanglu, was registered in a civilian household in Gui’an County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a native of Chongde County, Jiaxing Prefecture. He was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents, first in birth order, aged forty-seven, and born on the twenty-second day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chen, his grandfather Zheng, his father Yue, and his mother née Xu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yimin, Yixiang, and Yichen; his wife was née Qian. He ranked seventeenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 162nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Maoli, courtesy name Lüqing, was registered in a civilian household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. He was an additional student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Odes, third in birth order, aged twenty-four, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhi, his grandfather Lun, and his father An. His father’s former wife was née Feng, his stepmother née Qiu, and his birth mother née Wang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Maoren, a student of the Imperial University, and Maoyi, Left Administration Vice Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission; his younger brother was Maozhi. His wife was née Wang. He ranked eighty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and twenty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yan Guangqian, courtesy name Kongzhao, was registered in a military household in Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong. He was a student of the subprefectural Confucian school specializing in the Book of Documents, second in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the eighth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hong, his grandfather Ang, an honorary official recognized for philanthropy, his father Ru, and his mother née Zhao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Guangzhu, and his younger brothers were Guanghan and Chenggou; his wife was née Jin. He ranked twenty-third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and seventy-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Zuan, courtesy name Cunxiao, was registered in a civilian household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. He was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Rites, second in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the seventeenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wencai, his grandfather Chaoji, and his father Xingren. His mother was née Chen, and his stepmothers were née Zhang and née Xie. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Xu; his wife was née Wu. He ranked tenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Shen, courtesy name Kenian, was registered in a civilian household in Hui’an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was third in birth order, aged forty-three, and born on the twenty-second day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qin; his grandfather was Pu; his father was Jing, posthumously granted the title of Magistrate; and his mother, née Zeng, was granted the title of Lady (ruren). Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Kai, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner, and Ti, a titular official; his younger brothers were Huan 懽 and Huai 懐. He married a woman née Wu. He placed fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 161st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tian Rulin, courtesy name Ziren, was registered in a civilian household in Zhuozhou, Shuntian Prefecture, and was a native of Laishui County in the Metropolitan Region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was seventh in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the eleventh day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather Kuan received successive posthumous grants of the titles Grand Master for Aid in Governance and Minister of Rites. His grandfather Jingxian held the titles Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Pillar of State, Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Rites, and was posthumously granted the title Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent. His father Sui was an Office Assistant in the Directorate of Imperial Parks, and his mother was née Zhai. He placed 102nd in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 214th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shao Ling, courtesy name Ruren, was registered in a civilian household in Xiuning County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged forty-two, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiwu; his grandfather Yangde and father Tingwan both held the honorary designation of Official for Righteousness. His mother was née Cheng, and his stepmother was née Jin. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brother was Chang 倀 [?]; his younger brothers were Jue 爵, Qu 齲 [?], and Chen 齔 [?]. He married a woman née Wu. He placed 107th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 135th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ou Pei, courtesy name Shengfu, was registered in a postal-relay household in Tongchuan Subprefecture, Sichuan, and was a native of Wu County in the Metropolitan Region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the eighteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shijie; his grandfather was Feng; and his father Daqin was granted the title of Investigating Censor. His father’s former wife, née Liu, was posthumously granted the title of Lady (ruren); his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Zhu, formerly an Investigating Censor, and Ke; his younger brother was Jie. He married a woman née Wu. He placed twelfth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 311th in the Metropolitan Examination.

張選〔貫直隸揚州府高郵州軍籍，浙江寧海縣人，國子生，治書經，字士直，行二，年四十四，正月初七日生〕。曾祖忠〔壽官〕，祖鎧，父湧〔封工部郎中〕，母宣氏〔封宜人〕。永感下，兄道〔知州〕，弟遜〔知府〕、遵、逵〔七品散官〕。娶林氏，繼娶徐氏。應天府鄉試第七十九名，會試第一百五十三名。

蒙大賚〔貫廣西柳州府賓州民籍，國子生，治禮記，字善卿，行一，年三十二，十一月初九日生〕。曾祖贊，祖瑋，父仲元〔訓導〕，母韋氏。具慶下，弟大惠、大化、大有。娶周氏。廣西鄉試第三十一名，會試第三十五名。

余應舉〔貫江西南昌府南昌縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字德甫，行一，年三十七，六月二十二日生〕。曾祖子良，祖泰，父敘，母萬氏，繼母蔣氏。具慶下，弟應期、應兆。娶李氏。江西鄉試第九十一名，會試第二百四十八名。

王叔果〔貫浙江溫州府永嘉縣竈籍，國子生，治禮記，字育德，行一，年三十，二月初七日生〕。曾祖封，祖鉦〔封通政司右通政〕，父澈〔兵部郎中〕，母潘氏〔封宜人〕，繼母張氏。具慶下，弟叔杲〔貢士〕。娶林氏。浙江鄉試第五十四名，會試第二百六十五名。
translation_en:
Zhang Xuan, registered in a military household in Gaoyou Subprefecture, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was originally from Ninghai County, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Shizhi and ranked second among his brothers. He was forty-four years old, born on the seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhong, an honorary longevity official; his grandfather was Kai; his father was Yong, posthumously granted the title of Director in the Ministry of Works; and his mother, née Xuan, was granted the title of Lady of Suitability. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother Dao was a Subprefect; his younger brothers were Xun, a Prefect, Zun, and Kui, a seventh-rank titular official. He married a woman née Lin and subsequently a woman née Xu. He placed seventy-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred fifty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Meng Dalai was registered in a civilian household in Bin Subprefecture, Liuzhou Prefecture, Guangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he had the courtesy name Shanqing and ranked first among his brothers. He was thirty-two years old, born on the ninth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zan; his grandfather was Wei; his father was Zhongyuan, an Assistant Instructor; and his mother was née Wei. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Dahui, Dahua, and Dayou. He married a woman née Zhou. He placed thirty-first in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and thirty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Yingju was registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Defu and ranked first among his brothers. He was thirty-seven years old, born on the twenty-second day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ziliang; his grandfather was Tai; his father was Xu; his mother was née Wan; and his stepmother was née Jiang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yingqi and Yingzhao. He married a woman née Li. He placed ninety-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and two hundred forty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Shuguo was registered in a salt-producing household in Yongjia County, Wenzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he had the courtesy name Yude and ranked first among his brothers. He was thirty years old, born on the seventh day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Feng; his grandfather was Zheng, granted the title of Right Vice Commissioner of the Office of Transmission; his father was Che, a Director in the Ministry of War; his mother, née Pan, was granted the title of Lady of Suitability; and his stepmother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brother Shugao was a tribute scholar (gongshi). He married a woman née Lin. He placed fifty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and two hundred sixty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

李伸〔貫江西南昌府南昌縣，民籍，縣學生，治禮記，字道卿，行三，年二十八，八月二十四日生〕。曾祖綸，祖嵩，父時濟，母姜氏。具慶下，兄健、鑰，娶喻氏。江西鄉試第二十九名，會試第一百三十八名。

周後叔〔貫直隸蘇州府崑山縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字胤昌，行一，年三十四，八月十八日生〕。曾祖賢，祖永年，父慈，前母徐氏，母陳氏。永感下，弟之程、之甫、之申、之翰、之稼，娶鄒氏，繼娶戴氏。應天府鄉試第五十三名，會試第一百六十五名。

陳柯〔貫福建福州府閩縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字君則，行三，年三十四，正月十六日生〕。曾祖紳，祖瑩〔壽官〕，父源清〔教諭〕，母馬氏。永感下，兄桂，弟模、相、梅、杞，娶林氏，繼娶林氏。福建鄉試第六十名，會試第二百七十四名。

translation_en:
Li Shen, registered in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Daoqing; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged twenty-eight, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lun, his grandfather Song, his father Shiji, and his mother née Jiang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jian and Yue, and his wife was née Yu. He placed twenty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 138th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Houshu, registered in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yinchang; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the eighteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian, his grandfather Yongnian, and his father Ci; his father's former wife was née Xu, and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Zhicheng, Zhifu, Zhishen, Zhihan, and Zhijia. His wife was née Zou; he subsequently married a woman née Dai. He placed fifty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 165th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Ke, registered in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Junze; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the sixteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shen, his grandfather Ying (holder of an honorary official title for longevity), his father Yuanqing (a School Instructor), and his mother née Ma. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Gui, and his younger brothers were Mo, Xiang, Mei, and Qi. His wife was née Lin; he subsequently married another woman née Lin. He placed sixtieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 274th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Xianzhong was registered in a military household under Haining Guard, Zhejiang, and was a native of Haiyan County. He was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Wencheng; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-seven, and was born on the seventeenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jihai, his grandfather Hong, his father Yan, and his mother née Yan. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brother was Maoshu, and his wife was née Wang. He placed fifty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wu Song, courtesy name Zhongwang, was registered in a military household of Yongchang Guard, Yunnan, and was a native of Jiaxing County, Zhejiang. A student of the Yongchang Prefectural School specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the seventeenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cheng, his grandfather Li, his father Lan, and his mother née Hua. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Chong, Qi, and Yan; he married a woman née Wang. He placed ninth in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and 320th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Bangqing, courtesy name Yixian, was registered in a civilian household of Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the fourteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenzuan, who held honorary rank for longevity; his grandfather was Shiming, his father Zhao, and his mother née Cheng. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jiaqing and his younger brothers Puqing and Keqing; he married a woman née Luo. He placed twenty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 115th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Zongkui, courtesy name Gongxian, was registered in a civilian household of Hejian County, Hejian Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the fourteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiang, his grandfather Feng, his father Zhixue, who held an imperially bestowed honorary office, and his mother née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Zongxun; he married a woman née Wei and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed 128th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 174th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fan Daru, courtesy name Zishi, was registered in a military household of Zhanhua County, Binzhou, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the seventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jun, his grandfather Kui, his father Shaoyi, and his mother née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Daxun, Dalun, Dazuo, and Bei; he married a woman née Sun. He placed thirty-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and ninety-first in the Metropolitan Examination.
