translation_en:
Xue Tianhua, courtesy name Sisu, was registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-eight, born on the twentieth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chong, his grandfather Chen, and his father Shitong; his father's former wife was née Fan, and his mother was née Wei. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His elder brother was Tianrong, and his younger brothers were Tianfu, Tianmin, and Tianshen. He married a woman née Wu and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed forty-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and sixty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Dajie, courtesy name Kewan, was registered in Nan'an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty-one, born on the third day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tian, his grandfather Yi, and his father Cunshi; his legal mother was née Zhang, his stepmother was also née Zhang, and his birth mother was née Wang. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His younger brothers were Dafan, Dali, Dayue, Darun, and Dafang. He married a woman née Dai and subsequently a woman née Xie. He placed forty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and three hundred fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Meng Yuzheng, courtesy name Zhongyu, was registered in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the second day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Quan, his grandfather Yuan, and his father Yong; his mother was née Shen, and his stepmother was née He. His mother was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving father. His elder brother was Yuru, and his younger brothers were Yuzhong, Yuzhi, Yuming, Yuye, Yuji, Yuwen, and Yuxiang. He married a woman née Dong. He placed eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred twenty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Jiong, courtesy name Yanzhang, was registered in Sheng County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked tenth among his brothers and was aged forty-one, born on the fourteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yifu, his grandfather Yuan, and his father Yi; his mother was née Hu. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Gun, Xi, and Xiang, and his younger brother was Biao. He married a woman née Wang. He placed eighty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and twenty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Cui Xuelü, courtesy name Bohe, was registered in a civilian household in Changping Subprefecture, Shuntian Prefecture, and was a native of Wu County, Zhili. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twentieth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather Zhong was Director of the Imperial Manufactories under the Ministry of Works and, apparently by imperial command [?], posthumously awarded the title of Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; his grandfather Jie was Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; his father Zicai was an Assistant Prefect; and his mother, née Wu, held the title of Lady (Ruren). Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Xueqian, an annual tribute student, and Xueguan. He married a woman née Ma. He placed 124th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 158th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Tian, courtesy name Shungeng, was registered in a military household in Chongde County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the ninth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Xuan; his grandfather Xi was a County Registrar; his father was Huaizhong; and his mother was née Zhao. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Ji and Jiang. He married a woman née Hu. He placed 68th in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 181st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Nie Ying, courtesy name Rudeng, was registered in an artisan household in Xinhe County, Ji Subprefecture, Zhending Prefecture, Zhili, and was a native of Yangqu County, Shanxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was third in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the ninth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Xiang; his grandfather Fu held an honorary official title for longevity; his father was Jun; and his mother was née Miao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Lian, an Imperial University student, and Ting, a tribute scholar (gongshi); his younger brothers were Lin, Luo, Wei, Zhu, Xun, Qia, Ming, Lan, Bin, and Huan. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently women née Lu and née Li. He placed 110th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 95th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hao Shouye, courtesy name Zishu, was registered in a military household in Jun Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. A subprefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the seventh day of the intercalary twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Liang; his grandfather was Xiu; his father was Song; his mother was née Liu; and his stepmother was née Guo. Parents and grandparents were living. His younger brother was Shouping. He married a woman née Wang. He placed 42nd in the Henan Provincial Examination and 209th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Ruilong, registered in Chaoyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Tiqian. He ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the twenty-seventh day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hong, his grandfather Wanling, and his father Chengzhou; his mother was née Yang. His mother alone was surviving. His younger brother was Ruihe, and his wife was née Xiao. He placed twenty-fifth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 243rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yingshi, registered in Yongfu County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a native of Houguan County. He was a county government school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Maoxing. He ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty-three, and was born on the eighteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dan, his grandfather E, and his father Rong, who held an honorary longevity title; his mother was née Chen. His father alone was surviving. His elder brothers were Yingzhong, an Investigating Censor, and Yingzeng; his younger brothers were Yingqi, Yingyu, Yingmin, and Yingpin. His wife was née Lin. He placed fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yanshi, registered in Yuci County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Weipin. He ranked fourth among his brothers, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the nineteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mao, his grandfather Gongming, and his father Yue; his mother was née Liu. Both parents were surviving. His elder brothers were Yanbao, Yanxun, and Yanchen. His wife was née Yan, and his subsequent wife was née An. He placed forty-seventh in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 142nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ding Zishen, registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a salt-producing household and was an attached student of the prefectural government school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Pengyue. He ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty, and was born on the twenty-first day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Quan, his grandfather De, who held an honorary longevity title, and his father Yi; his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were surviving. His wife was née Zhang. He placed thirty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 238th in the Metropolitan Examination.

His great-grandfather was Mian, officially commended as a righteous commoner; his grandfather was Zan, his father Pan, and his mother née Wu, with both parents living; his elder brothers were Zi, Qi (a student of the Directorate of Education), and Song (also a student of the Directorate of Education), and his younger brothers were Li, Nan, Zha, Ge (a student of the Directorate of Education), Ying, Zhu, Shu, Pu, and Fei; he married a woman née Ren and placed seventy-sixth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 170th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jian Laiyu 蹇來譽, registered in an official household of Chongqing Guard, Sichuan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zixiu, he ranked first in his family, and he was thirty-two years old, born on the fifteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yingquan, a Company Commander; his grandfather was Hong, his father Tingxiang, and his mother née Jiang, with his father deceased and his mother living; his younger brothers were Laipeng, Laishuo, and Lailian; he married a woman née Wang and placed third in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and forty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Zhang 諸暲, registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zicheng, he ranked twenty-ninth in his family, and he was forty years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Huize, his grandfather Lun, his father Yongzhen, and his mother née Shu, with both parents deceased; his elder brother was Shi and his younger brothers were Hui and Ying; he married a woman née Zhou and subsequently a woman née Xu, and placed forty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 130th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Tang 孫塘, registered in a military household of the Rear Battalion of Hangzhou Right Guard, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ziyuan, he ranked first in his family, and he was thirty-eight years old, born on the twenty-third day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mao, his grandfather Yu, his father Jingzhao (an honorary official recognized for public benefaction), and his mother née Guo, with his father deceased and his mother living; his elder brother was Tai and his younger brother Jiao; he married a woman née Sheng and subsequently a woman née Jiang, and placed sixty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 103rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Third Class: 222 men, granted the status of metropolitan graduates (jinshi) by association.

Cui Du, courtesy name Minji, was registered in a military household in Puzhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents, he was third in family order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Heng; his grandfather, Lian; his father, Jing; and his mother, née Li. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Zhou and Xian, and his younger brother was Ming. He married a woman née Li. He placed fortieth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 231st in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Tingyu, courtesy name Runfu, was registered in an artisan household in Shaowu County, Shaowu Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in family order, aged thirty-six, and born on the first day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Qiong; his grandfather, Kuan; his father, Hong; his mother, née Yu; and his stepmother, née Wu. His father alone was living. His elder brother was Tingjin, and his younger brothers were Tingxian, Tingming, Tingrui, and Tingzhong. He married a woman née Zheng. He placed sixty-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 219th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lü Yang, courtesy name Diaoyang, was registered in an official household of Pingyang Guard, Shanxi, and was a native of Cao County, Shandong. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in family order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the twenty-third day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather Ying and grandfather Jing were both Vice Commanders of a Guard, each posthumously awarded the title General Who Cherishes Those from Afar. His father, Chen, was a Vice Commander of a Guard serving as Commandant. His father's former wife, née Deng, was posthumously awarded the title Lady of Gentility; his mother, née Wang, was awarded the same title. His mother alone was living. His younger brother was Kun. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed twenty-sixth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 317th in the Metropolitan Examination.

A county government school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the seventeenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Yongren, his grandfather Tingcheng, his father Wenxi, and his mother née Bao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Gong, and his younger brothers were Ling, Bin, and Huang. He married a woman née Fang. He placed sixty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Qiang, courtesy name Zizhen, was registered in a civilian household in Yizhou, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A subprefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was seventh in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the sixth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was You; his grandfather Wen was a prefectural clerk; and his father Jingrong held the honorary designation of Official for Righteousness. His father’s former wife was née Qin, and his mother was née Wang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Pan, a director of foodstuffs; Ao, a county registrar; Yue; Xi; Tang, an Imperial University student; and Xuan. He married a woman née Xu. He placed seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 268th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jie, courtesy name Weifan, was registered in a banner household of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard and was a native of Jiaozhou, Shandong. An additional student of the Shuntian prefectural government school specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-three, and born on the tenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Ang; his grandfather Jin was a vice battalion commander in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard; his father was Jian; and his mother was née Fang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhong, Bi, He, You, and Quan. He married a woman née Dai. He placed forty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 207th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Bangzhen, courtesy name Ziyu, was registered in a civilian household in Feicheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the fifteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather Zeng was a sacrificial official [?]; his grandfather Zhang held the honorary designation of Official for Righteousness; his father was Di; and his mother was née Wu. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Bangru and Bangshi. He married a woman née Hu. He placed sixty-sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 245th in the Metropolitan Examination.

王輿〔貫陝西西安府涇陽縣民籍，國子生，治春秋，字仲任，行四，年三十八，四月二十二日生〕。曾祖敬，祖幹，父鼎〔贈縣丞〕，嫡母張氏〔贈孺人〕，生母張氏。慈侍下，兄輅〔知縣〕，娶吳氏，繼娶李氏。陝西鄉試第五十六名，會試第八名。

丘鵬〔貫直隸蘇州府長洲縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字志弘，行一，年三十九，八月二十八日生〕。曾祖芳，祖雲，父鏜，母沈氏。慈侍下，兄山，弟鯨、龍、麒、鶚、淵，娶楊氏。應天府鄉試第十八名，會試第四十三名。
translation_en:
Yan Wangyun, courtesy name Daji, was registered in a military household in Anyi County, Jiezhou Subprefecture, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second in birth order and was twenty-nine sui, born on the sixth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gan, his grandfather Li, his father Zong, and his mother née Zhang; both parents were living. His elder brother was Lingyun, and he married a woman née Wei. He placed twentieth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 273rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Shu, courtesy name Guozheng, was registered in a civilian household in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third in birth order and was thirty-four sui, born on the twenty-second day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian, his grandfather Jin, and his father Si; his legal mother was née Xu and his birth mother née Hou. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Sheng and Hao; his younger brother Zhixuan was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the same examination year. He married a woman née Yuan and subsequently a woman née Xu. He placed 135th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 203rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yu, courtesy name Zhongren, was registered in a civilian household in Jingyang County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked fourth in birth order and was thirty-eight sui, born on the twenty-second day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing, his grandfather Gan, and his father Ding, posthumously awarded the title of County Vice Magistrate. His legal mother, née Zhang, was posthumously awarded the title of Lady (ruren); his birth mother was also née Zhang. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brother Lu was a County Magistrate. He married a woman née Wu and subsequently a woman née Li. He placed fifty-sixth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qiu Peng, courtesy name Zhihong, was registered in a civilian household in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first in birth order and was thirty-nine sui, born on the twenty-eighth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fang, his grandfather Yun, his father Tang, and his mother née Shen. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brother was Shan; his younger brothers were Jing, Long, Qi, E, and Yuan. He married a woman née Yang. He placed eighteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Fu Minghui 傅鳴會, registered in the guard-officer category in Lingshou County, Zhending Prefecture, Zhili, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Rujia; he was third in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the ninth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Kuan; his grandfather, Qian, held an honorary longevity title; his father was Wei; his legal mother was née Li and his birth mother née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Mingshi and Mingyuan, the latter an Imperial University student, and his younger brother was Mingyun. He married a woman née Luo. He placed ninety-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 218th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Fengmao 李鳳毛, registered in the civilian category in Peng County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yuxiang; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the fourteenth day of the intercalary fourth month. His great-grandfather was Sui, a School Instructor; his grandfather was Yue, a Prefectural School Professor; his father was Pei and his mother née Deng. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Fengge. He married a woman née Chen. He placed sixty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 289th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao He 高鶴, registered in the civilian category in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ruoling; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the sixteenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Lian; his grandfather was Yue; his father was Benzhong and his mother née Hu. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Peng and Yuan. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Guobin 吳國賓, registered in the civilian category in Wuwei Subprefecture, Luzhou Prefecture, Zhili, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Maoxian; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the twenty-second day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Xin, who held an honorary longevity title; his grandfather was Jingzhao, posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Personnel; his father was Tinghan, Left Administrative Assistant in a Provincial Administration Commission; and his mother, née Li, had been granted the title of Lady of Peace. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Guobao 國寶, Guobin 國賔, Guoshang 國賞, and Guoyin 國寅. He married a woman née Xie. He placed eighty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

王極〔貫順天府薊州，官籍，直隸無為州人，國子生，治書經，字伯準，行一，年三十五，九月二十日生〕。曾祖臣〔正千戶〕，祖銳〔正千戶〕，父濟〔正千戶〕，母張氏。重慶下，弟棟、桂、檜、楹、柱，娶邢氏。順天府鄉試第七十八名，會試第二百二十七名。
translation_en:
Li Fangzhi, registered in Fushun County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Ruchuan, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged forty-two, born on the twelfth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather Ben was Minister of Rites at Nanjing; his grandfather Wenchang was posthumously appointed Investigating Censor; his father Feng was Vice Commissioner of the Provincial Surveillance Commission; and his mother, née Yan, was granted the title of Lady (ruren). His father alone was living. His elder brother was Fang’en, a tribute scholar; his younger brothers were Fanghua, Fangshi, Fangjin, Fangzheng, Fangxun, Fangtai, Fangbao, Fangyin, Fanglin, and Fangjie. He married a woman née Gan. He placed thirty-sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 244th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fu Yunzhong, registered in Yongqing County, Shuntian Prefecture, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Ruzhi, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-one, born on the fourteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rang; his grandfather Qin was a Professor in a garrison school; his father was Cunxin; and his mother was née Hu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Meizhong and Jianzhong, and he married a woman née Shi. He placed ninetieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 216th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yuan Rushi, registered in Shishou County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Gongru, he ranked fourth among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-nine, born on the twenty-ninth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dun; his grandfather was Zongji; his father was Qi; and his mother was née Zeng. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ruchang, a tribute scholar, Ruxing, and Ruzui. He married a woman née Liu. He placed twenty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and thirty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ji, registered in Jizhou, Shuntian Prefecture, belonged to an official household and was originally from Wuwei Subprefecture in Zhili; he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, his courtesy name was Bozhun, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the twentieth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather Chen, grandfather Rui, and father Ji each held the post of Battalion Commander; his mother was née Zhang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Dong, Gui, Hui, Ying, and Zhu, and he married a woman née Xing. He placed seventy-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 227th in the Metropolitan Examination.

湯日新〔貫浙江嘉興府秀水縣匠籍，國子生，治書經，字懋昭，行一，年三十七，六月十八日生〕。曾祖澄，祖宗遠，父誥，母何氏。慈侍下，娶倪氏，繼娶張氏。浙江鄉試第三名，會試第二名。

translation_en:
Liu Yilin, courtesy name Ziren, was registered in a civilian household in Changping Subprefecture, Shuntian Prefecture. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Tai, a magistrate; his grandfather was Sirong, a Right Administrator, promoted to the prestige rank of Yazhong dafu; his father was Xiang, an honorary official for public benefaction; and his mother was née Wang. His mother alone was still living. His wife was née Wang. He placed first in the Shuntian Provincial Examination and 106th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Mao, courtesy name Zipei, was registered in a civilian household in Jiading County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the tenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Fan; his grandfather was Kai; and his father was Yun, an annual tribute student. His father's principal wife was née Li, and his birth mother was née Shao. Both parents were still living. His elder brother was Zi, an Office Assistant in the Court of State Ceremonial, and his younger brothers were Chu and Lu. His wife was née Li. He placed fifty-second in the Yingtian Provincial Examination and 100th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tang Rixin, courtesy name Maozhao, was registered in an artisan household in Xiushui County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the eighteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Cheng; his grandfather was Zongyuan; his father was Gao; and his mother was née He. His mother alone was still living. His wife was née Ni; he subsequently married a woman née Zhang. He placed third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Yilong, courtesy name Yutian, was registered in a civilian household in Hui'an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Mingjue; his grandfather was Hongde; his father was Zhao; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were still living. His younger brothers were Yilin and Yifeng. His wife was née Liu. He placed fifty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 228th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Yi, registered in a civilian household in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Shunqing, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the fifth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dingyong, his grandfather Xianneng, and his father Meiheng; his father's former wife was née Chen, and his mother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Kui and his younger brother Lai; his wife was née Xu. He placed fifty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 298th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye En, registered in a military household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and a native of Shanyang County in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Record of Rites; his courtesy name was Siguang, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-eight, born on the twenty-ninth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yang, posthumously awarded the title of Right Censor-in-chief of the Censorate; his grandfather was Bao, his father Ce, a student of the Imperial University, and his mother née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Ke, Jia, and Ru, and his younger brothers Si, Ji, Yu, Shu, and Yuan. His wife was née Sheng; he subsequently married a woman née Liu. He placed thirty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 121st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao He, registered in a military household in Chang'an County, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a prefectural government student specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Bohong, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the sixteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shou, his grandfather Rui, and his father Shan; his father's former wife was née Sun, and his mother was née Xiao. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Luo and his younger brother Lian; his wife was née Li. He placed twenty-sixth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 139th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Daoji, registered in a civilian household in Tong'an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a prefectural government student specializing in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Yizhong, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the tenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was An, his grandfather Cai, his father Guangjie, and his mother née Lin. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Daoyin; his wife was née Jiang. He placed sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and twenty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

王希堯〔貫陝西慶陽府安化縣，民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字汝仁，行一，年二十六，十一月二十八日生〕。曾祖允，祖懷〔典史〕，父守正，母劉氏。重慶下，弟希舜、希禹，娶王氏。陝西鄉試第三名，會試第一百五十四名。

鄭存仁〔貫山東東昌府臨清州衛河提舉司，匠籍，州學增廣生，治詩經，字子義，行一，年三十二，四月初五日生〕。曾祖榮，祖貴〔壽官〕，父璽，母黃氏。慈侍下，弟存禮，娶孫氏。山東鄉試第二十四名，會試第一百八十八名。
translation_en:
Huang Chaopin, registered in Shunde County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Xiyin, and he ranked second among his brothers. He was thirty-four, born on the twenty-fourth day of the intercalary twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Yuan, his grandfather Pei, and his father Chen; his father’s former wife was née Tan, and his mother was née Ou. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Chaomeng, Chaojin, and Chaozai. He married a woman née Ou and subsequently another woman née Ou. He placed fifty-fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and seventeenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Shijie, registered in Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a county-school student. He specialized in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Boyuan, and he ranked fifth among his brothers. He was thirty-four, born on the twenty-eighth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather Qing was Left Provincial Administration Commissioner in the Provincial Administration Commission; his grandfather Xiangshu was a District Magistrate; his father Zeng had been granted the privilege of wearing official cap and belt under the applicable regulations. His mother, née Luo, was living, and his father was deceased. His elder brothers were Shilun, Shiji, Shibi, a District Magistrate, and Shiti; his younger brother was Shichu. He married a woman née Yue. He placed fifty-seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and two hundred fifteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xiyao, registered in Anhua County, Qingyang Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a county-school student. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Ruren, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was twenty-six, born on the twenty-eighth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Yun, his grandfather Huai was a Chief Clerk, and his father was Shouzheng; his mother was née Liu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Xishun and Xiyu. He married a woman née Wang. He placed third in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and one hundred fifty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Cunren was registered in an artisan household under the Weihe Superintendency in Linqing Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, and was an additional-quota student of the subprefectural school. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Ziyi, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was thirty-two, born on the fifth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Rong, his grandfather Gui held an honorary title granted for longevity, and his father was Xi; his mother was née Huang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Cunli. He married a woman née Sun. He placed twenty-fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and one hundred eighty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Cui Jinsi, registered in a military household in Binzhou, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Xirui; he ranked first in his family and was aged forty-three, born on the second day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Jin; his grandfather, Duan, was posthumously granted the title of Prefectural Judge; his father, Wei, was an Associate Prefect; and his mother, née Mu, was granted the title of Lady for Service. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jinli, Jinchen, and Jinxing, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed thirteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 141st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Jian, registered in a civilian household in Xiangfu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was a native of Jinhua County, Zhejiang, and a county-school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Daohan; he ranked seventh in his family and was aged forty-one, born on the twenty-second day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather, Gui, was an Instructor; his grandfather, Jian, held an honorary rank for longevity; and his father, Qing, was an Assistant Instructor. His father's former wives were née Chen and née Yang, and his mother was née Li. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Lan and Dong. He married a woman née Yuan, and subsequently women née Pu and née Liu. He placed eighth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 175th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Jun, registered in a military household in Xuancheng County, Ningguo Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zongyu; he ranked third in his family and was aged twenty-nine, born on the fourth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Bokai, his grandfather was Lun, his father was Xiang, and his mother was née Xu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Huai, Han, and Chao; his younger brother was Jiang; and his wife was née Gong. He placed seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Yao, registered in a civilian household in Baling County, Yuezhou Prefecture, Huguang, was an additional student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Guohua; he ranked first in his family and was aged twenty-eight, born on the twelfth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather, Feng, was an Instructor; his grandfather, Chuyan, was a Station Master; his father was Ruli; his mother was née Yan; and his stepmother was née Yi. His father alone was living. His younger brothers were Yu and Ying, and his wife was née Xu. He placed thirteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and sixtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lü Zhuo, courtesy name Wenhua, was registered in an artisan household in Xiushui County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An additional student of the county school, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He ranked sixth in his family and was aged twenty-one, born on the seventeenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Ying, his grandfather Tingrui, and his father Chun; his father's principal wife was née Yang, and his birth mother was née Lu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ye, Hui, Zhao (an Imperial University student), Can (an Imperial University student), and Ke; his younger brother was Yue. His wife was née Shen. He placed sixty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eighty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yingbi, courtesy name Binzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Liaocheng County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong. An Imperial University student, he specialized in the Record of Rites. He ranked fourth in his family and was aged thirty-eight, born on the eleventh day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Yi; his grandfather Jian was an Assistant Instructor, posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor. His father Lu was a Salt Distribution Commissioner, advanced in rank to Grand Master for Excellent Counsel. His mother, née Li, was posthumously granted the title of Lady; his stepmothers were née Zhu, granted the title of Lady, and née Xu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yingyuan, Yingkui, and Yingxiang; his younger brothers were Yingcan, Yinglin, and Yingfeng. He married a woman née Xia and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed thirty-eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and two hundred and sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Hui, courtesy name Shifang, was registered in a civilian household in Pingyuan County, Dezhou Subprefecture, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. A county-school student, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked fourth in his family and was aged thirty, born on the twenty-seventh day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather Shou was posthumously granted the title of Assistant Office Director in the Court of Imperial Entertainments; his grandfather Fu held that office. His father Bangjie was a prefectural Clerk. His father's former wives were née Ren and née Wu; his mother was née Wu, and his stepmother was née Qi. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Heng, Lan, and Qin. His wife was née Shao. He placed twenty-second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and one hundred and sixty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

You Lie, courtesy name Ziwei, was registered in a civilian household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An Imperial University student, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He ranked second in his family and was aged forty-four, born on the seventh day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Ren; his grandfather Libao held an honorary title conferred for longevity. His father was Ming, his mother née Hong, and his stepmother née Lin. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shouci and Ziqing (an official awaiting selection for appointment); his younger brothers were Mo, Gao, Wu, and Ran [the transcription and division of the brothers' names are uncertain: 壽賜子卿 and 默羔嘸然, ?]. His wife was née Cai. He placed seventy-sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhu Jingxian, registered in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was an supplementary student of the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Fanzhi. He ranked second in his family, was aged thirty-seven, and was born on the seventeenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Ying 纓; his grandfather, Ying 瑩, had been granted the cap and girdle of official status under the applicable regulations. His father was Xibo, and his mother was née Sun. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Jinggu, Office Manager in the Nanjing Front Chief Military Commission; Jingyi, a student of the Imperial University; Jingyan; and Jingfu. His younger brothers were Jingchen; Jingcheng, a student of the Imperial University; and Jingxi. He married a woman née Gong and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed thirteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 241st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Bo, registered in Renqiu County, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zhong'an. He ranked second in his family, was aged twenty-eight, and was born on the first day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Fu, a Granary Commissioner; his grandfather was Jing; and his father was Zhen. His father's former wife was née Fang, and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Dong, and his younger brothers were Xu and Shao. He married a woman née Zhang 章. He placed twenty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 294th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zha Jiang, registered in Jing County, Ningguo Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Rusu. He ranked first in his family, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the twentieth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Lin, his grandfather was Tong, his father was Biao, and his mother was née Sheng. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jing and Wei. He married a woman née Wang. He placed thirty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 148th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Guang, registered in Pinghu County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Yuanshi. He ranked first in his family, was aged twenty-nine, and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Qi; his grandfather was Shen, who held honorary official status conferred for longevity; his father was Xiao, a student of the Imperial University; and his mother was née Shen. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Wei. He married a woman née Gu. He placed tenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventy-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Zhengguo, registered in Yiyang County, Henan Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zuozhi; he ranked first among his brothers, was twenty-nine years old, and was born on the seventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chen, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather was Mo, posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Upright Service and Director of the Bureau of Personnel Appointments in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel. His father was Bangrui, Grand Master for Excellent Counsel and Left Vice Minister of Personnel. His mother, née Gong, was granted the title Lady of Suitability; his stepmother was née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhengzhi, Zhengfang, and Zhengda, and his wife was née Lin. He placed forty-fourth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 163rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yijing, registered in Sui Subprefecture, Guide Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Ziyuan; he ranked first among his brothers, was thirty-one years old, and was born on the second day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong, his grandfather was Peng, and his father was Tingsui, a County Vice Magistrate; his mother was née Ren. Both parents were deceased. His wife was née Han, and his subsequent wife was née Tang. He placed thirty-second in the Henan Provincial Examination and 145th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Yuanji, registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Laizhen; he ranked fourth among his brothers, was thirty-nine years old, and was born on the twenty-sixth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather was Shizhong, and his father was Tingyi; his mother was née Zhang, and his stepmother was née Chai. His father was deceased and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Yuanxun, Yuanren, and Yuanmeng, and his wife was née Wang. He placed forty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 123rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Liangbin, registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Yijie; he ranked first among his brothers, was thirty-four years old, and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qing, his grandfather was Yun, and his father was Chun; his mother was née Wang. His father was living and his mother was deceased. His younger brother was Liangcai, and his wife was née Chen. He placed twenty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 212th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Zhengse, registered in Guangshan County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zezheng. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-six and was born on the seventeenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Shitong; his grandfather, Feng; his father, Jia, a student of the Directorate of Education; and his mother, née Xu. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brother was Zhongse, and his wife was née Wang. He ranked seventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and 144th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Kuang Shuqi, registered in Gao'an County, Ruizhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Jifu. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty and was born on the ninth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Wanmou; his grandfather, Jing, a Bureau Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice; and his father, Yijing, a Department Magistrate. His father's former wife was née Wu, and his mother was née Huang. His mother alone survived. His younger brother was Shuchu, and his wife was née Wu. He ranked fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 242nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qiao Si, registered in Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shutong. Fourth in birth order, he was aged forty-five and was born on the ninth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Lin; his grandfather, Yinglong; and his father, Zhu, a Police Chief. His father's former wife and his mother were both née Huang. Both his parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Zhong, a District Magistrate; Shu; and Mao, an Assistant Prefect. His younger brother was Yu, and his wife was née Wang. He ranked thirty-first in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 284th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Dian, registered in Baoding Central Guard under the Daning Regional Military Commission, belonged to an official household and was a student at the Regional Military Commission's school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zihou. First in birth order, he was aged thirty and was born on the twentieth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Ning; his grandfather, Dagang; and his father, Shichang, an Assistant District Magistrate. His mother was née Li, and his stepmother was née Liu. His father alone survived. His younger brother was Ao, and his wife was née Song. He ranked eleventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 143rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Tang Shilong, registered in Xian County, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Deheng; he ranked second among his brothers, was thirty-five years old, and was born on the third day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Feng; his grandfather, Min, served as a subprefectural Clerk; his father, Xian, served as an Instructor; and his mother was née Chen. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Shixun, and his younger brother was Shixian. His wife was née Liu. He placed thirty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 222nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yongxian, registered in Qizhou, Baoding Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Bochun; he ranked first among his brothers, was thirty-six years old, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the intercalary fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wei; his grandfather was Zilu; his father was Yao; his mother was née Zhang; and his stepmother was née Li. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Shangxian, Jinxian, and Mengxian. His wife was née Liu. He placed forty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 128th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mao Ruqi, registered in Longyou County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was an added-quota student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Boxiang; he ranked third among his brothers, was thirty-eight years old, and was born on the third day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongfu; his grandfather was Zuicheng; his father was Wenying; his mother was née Jiang; and his stepmother was née Yao. His mother was living, and his father was deceased. His younger brothers were Ruxie and Rupi. His wife was née Yu. He placed thirty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 182nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Jibang, registered in Suide Subprefecture, Yan’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a military household and was originally from Shizhou, Shanxi. He was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zizhong; he ranked fourth among his brothers, was thirty-three years old, and was born on the thirteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather, Zheng, served as a District Magistrate; his grandfather, Jing, and his father, Lan, both served as county Registrars; and his mother was née Huo. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jimin, Jishi, and Jishang; his younger brothers were Jishi, Jiren, Jizhou, and Jizhong. His wife was née Huo. He placed fourteenth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 117th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Song Deng, registered in a civilian household in Dingxing County, Baoding Prefecture, Zhili, was a county school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Zixian, and he was second in birth order. His age is recorded as “至十五” [?]; he was born on the fifteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, his grandfather Chen, and his father Shihua; his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Zhao. He placed tenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 286th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tang Bin, registered in a military household in Nanpi County, Cangzhou, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Jiyin, and he was first in birth order, aged twenty-seven, born on the seventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fuchun; his grandfather Cheng held the honorary title of Official for Righteousness; and his father Yin was a County Vice Magistrate. His father's former wife was née Li, and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Xie. He placed 219th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 108th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Shaoqing, registered in a civilian household in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zishan, and he was second in birth order, aged thirty-seven, born on the fifteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather Cun was a County Magistrate; his grandfather Zhen was posthumously awarded the titles of Grand Master for Governance and Bureau Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel; and his father Danan was a Prefect. His mother, née Sheng, was invested with the title of Lady of Suitability. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Sizhong and Shaosun, and his younger brothers were Juqing, Yanqing, and Zhengqing. He married a woman née Gu and subsequently a woman née Shi. He placed first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Yang, registered in a civilian household in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, Zhili, was originally from Jiading County, Suzhou Prefecture. He was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Fuqing, and he was third in birth order, aged thirty-three, born on the eighteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhou; his grandfather Yue held a seventh-rank prestige title; and his father was Long. His mother was née Yan. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Jie, an Imperial University student, and Sui; his younger brothers were Tao, Ling 陵, and Ling 𨹧. He married a woman née Qu. He placed 116th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 247th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Dong Sui 董遂, registered in Song County, Henan Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shuliang. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-three and was born on the nineteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shixin; his grandfather was Ang; his father was Xiang, Vice Commissioner of the Provincial Surveillance Commission; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Xun 遜, Xuan 選, Xun 塤, and Shi 适. His wife was née Li. He placed twelfth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 211th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Yingqian 沈應乾, registered in Wuhe County, Fengyang Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to an artisan household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Weishun. First in birth order, he was aged forty-one and was born on the seventeenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Li, a student of the Imperial University; his grandfather was Han, Chief Judicial Officer, advanced in rank to Grand Master for Court Discussion; his father was Cai; and his mother was née Ou. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yingshi and Yingzhen. His wife was née Chen. He placed twenty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 310th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Ji 鄭佶, registered in Huangpi County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to an official household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yuanjian. Third in birth order, he was aged thirty-eight and was born on the tenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zizhang; his grandfather was Qian; his father was Luan, an annual tribute student; and his mother was née Zhou. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Wei and Jun, and his younger brother was Shi. His wife was née Yu. He placed sixty-fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 276th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiao Kejiao 蕭可教, registered in Jiangdu County, Yangzhou Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zixiu. First in birth order, he was aged forty-four and was born on the eighteenth day of the intercalary first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kai, Medical Instructor; his grandfather was Shen; his father was Ding; and his mother was née Ma. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Kewei and Kejin. His wife was née Zhang. He placed fifteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 200th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wei Dongwu, registered in Ye County, Yuzhou, Nanyang Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Shujing; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-one [?—the age formula is garbled], and born on the fifteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather Xu was a county magistrate, posthumously granted the title of Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud at Nanjing; his grandfather Yue was an annual tribute student, posthumously granted the title of Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Works and subsequently that of Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud at Nanjing. His father Dao was Right Vice Minister of Justice at Nanjing, and his mother, née Jiao, was invested with the title of Lady of Virtue. Both parents were living. His elder brother Dongchu was a tribute scholar. He married a woman née Kang. He placed seventy-seventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and one hundred sixteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tu Zhonglü was registered in the Yingzhou Central Garrison Guard in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household, and was originally from Pinghu County, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he had the courtesy name Zongyu, was second in birth order, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the eighth day of the second month. His great-grandfather Ji was posthumously granted the title of Minister of Justice; his grandfather Xun was Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Justice, posthumously granted the title of Grand Guardian and the name Kangxi. His father Yingjun was Right Admonisher in the Right Secretariat of the Heir Apparent, and his mother was née Xiang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers Mengxuan, Zhongqi, Zhongchou, and Zhongxi were all Imperial University students; his younger brothers were Shufang, Shuming, and Shu□, all Imperial University students; Jihou, a government student; and Zhongzhen, Zhongqiao, Shudu, Shuzhang, and Shuyi. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Shen. He placed forty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred forty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gou Ying, registered in Langzhong County, Baoning Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Xiyan; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the seventh day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Zhiying; his grandfather Chang held an honorary official title conferred for longevity; his father was Liangbi, and his mother was née Yan. His parents and a grandparent or grandparents were living. His younger brother was Yu. He married a woman née Bai. He placed fortieth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and ninety-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Daozhi, registered in Xianyang County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Zisheng; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Zheng; his grandfather Cai was granted the titles of Gentleman of the Forest of Literature and Investigating Censor, and posthumously those of Grand Master of Constitutional Service and Surveillance Vice Commissioner. His father Xian was Left Administration Vice Commissioner, and his mother, née Feng, was invested with the title of Lady and subsequently that of Lady of Respect. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother Daozheng was an Imperial University student; his younger brothers were Daoping, Daokuan, Daochun, Daocheng, and Daogong. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Liu. He placed third in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and one hundred seventy-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Luo Wei, registered in Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Sufu, he was first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-one, born on the eighteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chaoli, his grandfather Zhongyuan, his father Wenkui, and his mother née Zhao; both parents were living, his younger brother was Jin, and he married a woman née Wei and subsequently a woman née Chen; he ranked seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 156th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Liyan, registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military salt-service household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ruxuan, he was second in birth order, and he was aged thirty-eight, born on the thirtieth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zuanbi, his grandfather Jin, his father Tong, and his mother née Wang; both parents were deceased, his elder brother was Liyan (立言), his younger brothers were Litong and Libiao, and his wife was née You; he ranked seventy-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and seventy-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gu Honglu, registered in Xianju County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Jingwen, he was third in birth order, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-second day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chi, his grandfather Jing, his father Zhao, his mother née Wang, and his stepmother née Song; both parents were living, his elder brothers were Hongbo and Hongyuan, his younger brothers were Hongbian and Honggan, and his wife was née Du; he ranked sixty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninety-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Qing, registered in Yongfeng County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a Confucian scholar household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Lüxuan, he was second in birth order, and he was aged forty-one, born on the twenty-ninth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tingchong, his grandfather Wenbin, his father Yi'e, and his mother née Liu; his father was deceased and his mother living, his elder brother was Gai, his younger brother Gui, and his wife was née Peng; he ranked thirty-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 255th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Cao Shoujing, registered in a civilian household in Fuliang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhongquan; he ranked third in his family, was aged twenty-seven, and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Shikuan; his grandfather was Ruxie, posthumously granted the title of Vice Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Works; his father was Bai; and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shouren and Shoulian, and his younger brothers were Shoujie and Shoujie (守介 and 守潔, respectively). His wife was née Zheng. He placed twenty-eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 134th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pan Jixun, registered in a civilian household in Gui’an County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and a native of Wucheng County, was a county-school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Shiliang; he ranked tenth in his family, was aged thirty, and was born on the twenty-third day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Xuan; his grandfather was Xiao, a Departmental Judge; his father was Kui, an Imperial Academy student; and his mother was née Min. Both parents were living. His elder brothers are listed as Jiyou, Jida, and Jijian, all Imperial Academy students; Jixun [?], a Prefectural Judge; Jixian and Jilin, both Associate Prefects; Jifu [?], Jijun, Jixun [?], Jixian (季賢), and Jibin. His younger brothers were Jijiao, Jitang, and Jixi. His wife was née Shi. He placed ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 113th in the Metropolitan Examination. [The elder-brother list repeats the candidate’s own name twice and appears inconsistent with his stated family rank.]

Chen Jing, registered in a banner household of the Zhuolu Left Guard in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an Imperial Academy student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Ruji; he ranked first in his family, was aged forty-five, and was born on the tenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Jingchun; his grandfather was Xin; his father was Song, who held the honorary title of Longevity Official; and his mother was née Gong. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Lun, and his wife was née Gu. He placed fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Li, registered in a civilian household in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and a native of Shanyin County, was an Imperial Academy student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Xingfu; he ranked seventh in his family, was aged thirty-one, and was born on the eighteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Lü; his grandfather was Yi; his father was Hong, a Steward of Food; and his mother was née Zhou. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Shan, Lin, and Cheng, and his wife was née Liu. He placed sixty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 264th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Weng Mengli, registered in a civilian household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was a supplementary student at the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Xideng; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the sixteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shao, his grandfather Yi, his father Zidi, and his mother née Chen. His mother was living and his father deceased. He married a woman née Xie. He placed forty-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 133rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Qian, registered in a salt-producing household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Hengfu; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather Hua was an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; his grandfather Jiugao held the rank of Battalion Commander, acquired through a grain contribution; his father Bida was a County Magistrate, and his mother was née Zhou. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Yi, Hui, Cui, Mi, Yinbin, and Jin. He married a woman née Yao and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 107th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Kexue, registered in a civilian household in Shifang County, Hanzhou, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, was a county-school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zixing; he was second in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the nineteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather Qinfu, his father Jun, a student of the Imperial University, and his mother née Yang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Kexiao, and his younger brothers were Kefu and Kezi. He married a woman née Wang. He placed twenty-second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and fifty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Anqi, registered in a military household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zihe; he was second in birth order, aged forty, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather Xuan and grandfather Xuan each held a seventh-rank prestige title. His father was Qian; his father's former wife was née Zhao, and his mother was née Zhang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Changqi, and his younger brothers were Wu, a County Magistrate, Yingqi, Fengqi, and Pengqi. He married a woman née Li. He placed ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 198th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Zhengyi, courtesy name Dexu, was registered in a military household in Baling County, Yuezhou Prefecture, Huguang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-first day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuandao, his grandfather Biyong, his father Xiang, and his mother née Yu; both parents were living. His elder brother was Zhengren, a provincial sacrificial official, and his younger brother Zhengxin. His wife was née Zhao. He placed sixteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 260th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zheng, courtesy name Zixiao, was registered in a civilian household in Zhushan County, Yunyang Prefecture, Huguang, and was a native of Yongjia County, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the eighteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Binggui, his grandfather Lu, his father Lian, a prefectural school instructor, and his mother née Shao; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xun, Gao, and Cheng. His wife was née Lan. He placed 114th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 196th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yongkang, courtesy name Yunjing, was registered in a military household in Wenshang County, Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the nineteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Liang, his grandfather Xuan, his father Shangzhong, and his mother née Du; both parents were living. His wife was née Feng. He placed forty-first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 251st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Chuance, courtesy name Yuanhan, was registered in a civilian household in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, Zhili. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked sixth among his brothers and was aged twenty-one, born on the twenty-seventh day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yi, a subprefect promoted in prestige rank to Grand Master for Court Discussion; his grandfather was Jifang, his father Tiren, an annual tribute student, and his mother née Song. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chuanxing, Chuanmo, Chuanjiao, Chuanshi, Chuandi, Chuanzhang, Chuanke, Chuanshi, Chuanyin, Chuansheng, Chuanxi, and Chuanyi. His wife was née Li. He placed fifty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
崔棟〔貫順天府薊州衛軍籍，州學生，治禮記，字孔材，行一，年三十六，二月十五日生〕。曾祖富，祖繼英，父江，前母盧氏，母盧氏。重慶下，弟楊、榛、檳、接、檢、榆，娶尹氏。順天府鄉試第三十六名，會試第一百五名。

傅汝礪〔貫陝西寧羌衛軍籍，西安府長安縣人，國子生，治詩經，字若金，行五，年四十二，十月初九日生〕。曾祖安，祖本，父琄〔壽官〕，嫡母丁氏，生母王氏。慈侍下，兄鐸〔知縣〕、汝霖〔知縣〕、汝舟、汝楫、汝和，娶何氏。陝西鄉試第三十一名，會試第三百四名。

丘橓〔貫山東青州府諸城縣民籍，國子生，治禮記，字懋實，行四，年三十五，九月三十日生〕。曾祖能，祖玘，父讓，母張氏。具慶下，兄先、賢、瑶，弟桴，娶范氏。山東鄉試第二名，會試第一百六十九名。

丘文學〔貫山東東昌府博平縣民籍，江西永豐縣人，國子生，治易經，字子晉，行一，年三十七，十一月二十五日生〕。曾祖一信，祖公玉，父明，母孫氏。重慶下，弟懋學，娶尹氏。山東鄉試第四十七名，會試第四十一名。
translation_en:
Cui Dong, courtesy name Kongcai, was registered in a military household of Jizhou Guard, Shuntian Prefecture. A student of the department school, he specialized in the Book of Rites. He ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the fifteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fu; his grandfather, Jiying; and his father, Jiang. His father's former wife and his mother were both née Lu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Yang, Zhen, Bin, Jie, Jian, and Yu. He married a woman née Yin. He placed thirty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 105th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fu Ruli, courtesy name Ruojin, was registered in a military household of Ningqiang Guard, Shaanxi, and was a native of Chang'an County, Xi'an Prefecture. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked fifth among his brothers and was aged forty-two, born on the ninth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was An; his grandfather, Ben; and his father, Xuan, who held an honorary official title conferred for longevity. His legal mother was née Ding, and his birth mother was née Wang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Duo, a Magistrate; Rulin, a Magistrate; Ruzhou; Ruji; and Ruhe. He married a woman née He. He placed thirty-first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 304th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qiu Shun, courtesy name Maoshi, was registered in a civilian household of Zhucheng County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Rites. He ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the thirtieth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Neng; his grandfather, Qi; his father, Rang; and his mother, née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xian 先, Xian 賢, and Yao; his younger brother was Fu. He married a woman née Fan. He placed second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 169th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qiu Wenxue, courtesy name Zijin, was registered in a civilian household of Boping County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, and was a native of Yongfeng County, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yixin; his grandfather, Gongyu; his father, Ming; and his mother, née Sun. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brother was Maoxue. He married a woman née Yin. He placed forty-seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and forty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.
