紀鳳鳴〔貫錦衣衛旗籍，陝西榆林衛人，國子生，治詩經，字明瑞，行一，年三十六，九月十三日生〕。曾祖濼〔贈承德郎、太常寺寺丞〕，祖世梁〔太常寺寺丞〕，父汴〔七品散官〕，母陳氏。嚴侍下，弟鳳儀，娶于氏，繼娶王氏、茹氏。順天府鄉試第八十八名，會試第二百九十名。

柳希玭〔貫直隸廬州府廬江縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字子敬，行一，年四十五，九月初五日生〕。曾祖廣，祖萬，父琪，母王氏。永感下，弟希禮、希渾、希儒，娶劉氏。應天府鄉試第七十八名，會試第四十四名。

王潺〔貫錦衣衛官籍，直隸長垣縣人，國子生，治易經，字公沛，行四，年四十一，正月十一日生〕。曾祖斌〔正千戶，封武德將軍〕，祖宇〔正千戶，封武德將軍〕，父鉞〔正千戶，封武德將軍〕，母陳氏〔封宜人〕。慈侍下，兄洧〔正千戶〕、沂〔副千戶〕、澤，弟洋，娶萬氏，繼娶季氏。順天府鄉試第一百二十九名，會試第二百八十八名。

袁世榮〔貫直隸松江府華亭縣軍籍，國子生，治書經，字子仁，行一，年三十二，三月十四日生〕。曾祖凱〔布政使司左布政使〕，祖佩〔中書舍人〕，父讚〔前鴻臚寺少卿〕，母周氏〔封孺人〕。永感下，弟世華、世孝，娶潘氏。應天府鄉試第一百名，會試第二百七十一名。
translation_en:
Ji Fengming, registered in the bannerman category of the Embroidered Uniform Guard and a native of Yulin Guard, Shaanxi, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Mingrui; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the thirteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather Luo was posthumously granted the titles of Gentleman for Receiving Virtue and Assistant in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; his grandfather Shiliang was Assistant in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; his father Bian held a seventh-rank prestige title; and his mother was née Chen. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brother was Fengyi. He married a woman née Yu and subsequently women née Wang and Ru. He placed eighty-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 290th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Xipin, registered in a civilian household in Lujiang County, Luzhou Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zijing; he was first in birth order, aged forty-five, and born on the fifth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Guang, his grandfather Wan, his father Qi, and his mother née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Xili, Xihun, and Xiru. He married a woman née Liu. He placed seventy-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Chan, registered in an officer household of the Embroidered Uniform Guard and a native of Changyuan County, Zhili, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Gongpei; he was fourth in birth order, aged forty-one, and born on the eleventh day of the first month. His great-grandfather Bin, grandfather Yu, and father Yue were each Battalion Commanders and each received the title General of Military Virtue; his mother, née Chen, received the title Lady of Suitability. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Wei, a Battalion Commander, Yi, a Vice Battalion Commander, and Ze; his younger brother was Yang. He married a woman née Wan and subsequently a woman née Ji. He placed 129th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 288th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yuan Shirong, registered in a military household in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Ziren; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the fourteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather Kai was Left Provincial Administration Commissioner; his grandfather Pei was a Secretariat Drafter; his father Zan was formerly Vice Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial; and his mother, née Zhou, received the title Lady of Service. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Shihua and Shixiao. He married a woman née Pan. He placed one hundredth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 271st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Xiaozu, registered with the Wuxiang Left Guard and a native of Binzhou, Shandong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Zhongxiu; he ranked second in his family and was twenty-nine years old, born on the fifth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather Neng was posthumously appointed Left Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate; his grandfather was Tong; his father, Yu, was a student admitted by virtue of official family status; and his mother was née Peng. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Xizu, and his younger brothers were Jizu, Shengzu, Tongzu, and Shunzu. He married a woman née Du. He placed 132nd in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 48th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Ying, of civilian registration in Lanxi County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shunshu; he ranked sixteenth in his family and was forty-four years old, born on the eighteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Yuanjun; his grandfather, Shan; his father, Zhu; his father's former wife was née Chen, and his mother was née Hong. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Shu, and his younger brother was Jing. He married a woman née Zheng and subsequently a woman née Shao. He placed 36th in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 204th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Zhou, of civilian registration in Taihe County, Dali Prefecture, Yunnan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Ziyu; he ranked fourth in his family and was thirty-nine years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Wenyi; his grandfather, Yongying; his father, Qing; and his mother was née Li. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Ren, a County Vice Magistrate; Kai, a Subprefectural Clerk; and Heng. He married a woman née Yang. He placed 33rd in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and 314th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yingxian, of military registration in Zhangpu County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Weimo; he ranked first in his family and was forty years old, born on the tenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Xide; his grandfather, Heng; his father, Qiong; and his mother was née Ruan. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yingji and Yingcong. He married a woman née Zheng. He placed 58th in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 172nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

謝教〔貫直隸常州府武進縣，民籍，縣學增廣生，治詩經，字敬敷，行一，年三十五，七月十九日生〕。曾祖貴〔壽官〕，祖晟，父緯，母浦氏，繼母杜氏。具慶下，弟孜、徵、敕，娶許氏。應天府鄉試第七十三名，會試第四十六名。

許公高〔貫四川保寧府南部縣，軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字德升，行一，年三十四，九月二十七日生〕。曾祖瓚〔義官〕，祖正奇，父重本〔斷事〕，母龐氏，繼母劉氏、任氏。重慶下，弟公亨、公大、公進、公清、公廉，娶沈氏。四川鄉試第三十九名，會試第六十八名。

尹庭〔貫山東濟南府肥城縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字子紹，行一，年三十七，二月初九日生〕。曾祖綱，祖鳳，父天民〔知縣〕，母孟氏，繼母張氏。嚴侍下，弟進、遴，娶傅氏。山東鄉試第三十七名，會試第四十三名。

林兆金〔貫福建興化府莆田縣，軍籍，國子生，治書經，字懋南，行一，年三十六，五月二十四日生〕。曾祖環〔文林郎、大理寺評事，贈通議大夫、兵部右侍郎兼都察院右僉都御史〕，祖富〔通議大夫、兵部右侍郎兼都察院右僉都御史〕，父萬仞〔官生〕，母李氏。慈侍下〔弟兆恩〔官生〕、兆憲、兆龍、兆復、兆瓊、兆芳、兆登、兆舉、兆臻、兆坤、兆文、兆麟，娶丘氏，繼娶吳氏〕。福建鄉試第六十三名，會試第二百四十名。
translation_en:
Xie Jiao, registered in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student of the county school. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Jingfu. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-five and was born on the nineteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Gui, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his grandfather was Sheng; and his father was Wei. His mother was née Pu, and his stepmother was née Du. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zi, Zheng, and Chi, and his wife was née Xu. He ranked seventy-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Gonggao, registered in Nanbu County, Baoning Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Desheng. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-four and was born on the twenty-seventh day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Zan, an honorary official recognized for public beneficence; his grandfather was Zhengqi; and his father was Chongben, a Judicial Officer. His mother was née Pang, and his stepmothers were née Liu and née Ren. His grandparents and parents were living. His younger brothers were Gongheng, Gongda, Gongjin, Gongqing, and Gonglian, and his wife was née Shen. He ranked thirty-ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and sixty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yin Ting, registered in Feicheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Zishao. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-seven and was born on the ninth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Gang; his grandfather was Feng; and his father was Tianmin, a District Magistrate. His mother was née Meng, and his stepmother was née Zhang. His father alone was living. His younger brothers were Jin and Lin, and his wife was née Fu. He ranked thirty-seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and forty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Zhaojin, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Maonan. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-six and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Huan, Gentleman of Literary Service and Case Reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review, posthumously granted the titles of Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Minister of War concurrently serving as Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His grandfather was Fu, Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Minister of War concurrently serving as Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His father was Wanren, a student admitted by virtue of official family privilege, and his mother was née Li. His mother alone was living. His younger brothers were Zhao'en, likewise a student admitted by virtue of official family privilege, Zhaoxian, Zhaolong, Zhaofu, Zhaoqiong, Zhaofang, Zhaodeng, Zhaoju, Zhaozhen, Zhaokun, Zhaowen, and Zhaolin. His wife was née Qiu, and his subsequent wife was née Wu. He ranked sixty-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and two hundred fortieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

卓爾〔貫福建福州府長樂縣，民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字見可，行一，年三十八，五月十一日生〕。曾祖誠，祖仕英，父廷紳，母林氏。具慶下，弟有為，娶陳氏，繼娶陳氏。福建鄉試第八十九名，會試第三百十五名。

馬斯臧〔貫河南開封府鈞州，民籍，國子生，治禮記，字遠謨，行一，年三十六，六月二十一日生〕。曾祖文麟〔知縣〕，祖安〔封知府〕，父紀〔布政使司右參政〕，母連氏〔封恭人〕。慈侍下，弟斯才、斯作、斯徂〔貢士〕，娶王氏。河南鄉試第五名，會試第三百三名。

楊惟平〔貫直隸真定府冀州南宮縣，民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字君正，行一，年三十六，正月十三日生〕。曾祖輔〔縣丞〕，祖懋，父崙，母李氏。慈侍下，弟惟聰、惟中、惟一，娶張氏。順天府鄉試第十九名，會試第一百九十名。
translation_en:
Zhuo Er, registered in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government student. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Jianke; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-eight, born on the eleventh day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Cheng, his grandfather Shiying, his father Tingshen, and his mother née Lin. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Youwei. He married a woman née Chen and subsequently another woman née Chen. He placed eighty-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 315th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Liao, registered in Haiyan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Yuanbai; his recorded family birth-order rank was sixty-seven, and he was aged twenty-eight, born on the tenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Fan; his grandfather Pang received the honorary title of Magistrate. His father Shu 术 [?] was a Secretary in the Ministry of Works, and his mother, née Zheng, received the title of Lady (Ruren). His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Yi, a county school Instructor, Jun, Lian, and Xiao; his younger brother was Yao. He married a woman née Qian. He placed thirty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Sizang, registered in Jun Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Record of Rites. His courtesy name was Yuanmo; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-first day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather Wenlin was a Magistrate; his grandfather An received the honorary title of Prefect. His father Ji was a Right Administration Vice Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission, and his mother, née Lian, received the title of Lady (Gongren). His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Sicai, Sizuo, and Sicu, the last a tribute scholar (gongshi). He married a woman née Wang. He placed fifth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 303rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Weiping, registered in Nangong County, Ji Subprefecture, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government student. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Junzheng; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the thirteenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather Fu was a County Vice Magistrate, his grandfather was Mao, his father Lun, and his mother née Li. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Weicong, Weizhong, and Weiyi. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed nineteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 190th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhou Guoqing, courtesy name Taizhong, was registered as a guardsman of the Embroidered Uniform Guard and was a native of Haining County, Zhejiang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second in his family and was twenty-six years old, born on the first day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Jing; his grandfather Zhen and father Jing both held the honorary title of Philanthropic Official. His mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Guoxiang, Guozhu, and Guoliang, and his wife was née Chen. He placed second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Bangyan, courtesy name Chaoxuan, was registered in a civilian household in Suizhou, Guide Prefecture, Henan. An added-quota student of the department school specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first in his family and was twenty-three years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Cheng, his grandfather Duo, and his father Qin; his mother was née Xi. His mother was living and his father deceased. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Huangfu. He placed first in the Henan Provincial Examination and twelfth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hou Donglai, courtesy name Ruzong, was registered in a military household in Ye County, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second in his family and was twenty-nine years old, born on the second day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Xin, his grandfather Xing, and his father Siyi. His father's former wife was née Song, and his mother was née Bian. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Donglu and his younger brother Dongfang; his wife was née Li. He placed sixty-first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 164th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Chongzeng, courtesy name Canbo, was registered in a military household in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked forty-second in his family and was thirty-four years old, born on the tenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather Mi was Right Administration Vice Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission and received the additional posthumous titles of Grand Master of the Great Center and Junior Governor for Aid in Governance. His grandfather De was a Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; his father was Zhou and his mother née He. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Chongshan, an Imperial University student, Chongzu, Chongnan, Chongji, Chongyi, Chongke, and Chonglu; his wife was née Yang. He placed seventieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninety-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Sun Jia, registered with the Embroidered Uniform Guard and a native of Yuyao County, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhiwan; he ranked fifty-sixth among his brothers and male cousins and was aged thirty-eight, born on the seventh day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Menghong, posthumously granted the title of Minister of Rites; his grandfather was Bin, a County School Instructor; his father was Lian, and his mother was née Zheng. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Kan, Assistant Commissioner-in-Chief of the Front Chief Military Commission; Chi, Assistant Director of the Office of Imperial Seals; Sheng, Chancellor of the Directorate of Education; and Jie, a student admitted by virtue of official family status. His younger brothers were Fang, a Secretary in the Ministry of Justice, and Jiong. His wife was née Wang. He placed tenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 160th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ru’an, of military household registration in Xiong County, Baoding Prefecture, Northern Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Zile; he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins and was aged forty-one, born on the first day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Ming, his grandfather was Lun, his father was Ju, and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Runing, Ruyi, Ruchong, and Rucai. His wife was née Li. He placed fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 187th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Ben, of military household registration in Chao County, Wuwei Subprefecture, Luzhou Prefecture, Southern Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Zizhong; he ranked second among his brothers and male cousins and was aged forty-three, born on the twentieth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Heng, a County Magistrate; his grandfather was Guang, a County School Instructor posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his father was Hu, a Prefect posthumously granted the title of Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; and his mother was née Zhang, granted the title of Lady of Respect (gongren). Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Cai, and his younger brothers were Nie and Cheng. He married a woman née Yang and subsequently a woman née Yao. He placed 123rd in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 104th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Ding, of civilian household registration in Zhangpu County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Sizhong; he ranked second among his brothers and male cousins and was aged twenty-nine, born on the first day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Shigeng, his grandfather was Tirui, and his father was Zongzhi. His legal mother, his father’s principal wife, was née Cheng; his birth mother was née Su. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His elder brother was Zui, and his younger brothers were Xian, Ben, and Hao. His wife was née Zhang. He placed fifty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 110th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xue Ruh uai 薛如淮, courtesy name Dongqing, was registered in a civilian household in Jiangyin County, Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged forty-five, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ting; his grandfather, Ting, held an honorary official title for longevity; his father, Ao, was a subprefectural judge; and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Ruyuan, and his younger brothers were Ruyi, Ruluo, Rulan, Ruchun, Ruru, and Rusheng. His wife was née Peng. He ranked ninety-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 291st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Liangpu 郭良璞, courtesy name Bianyu, was registered in a military household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qi, his grandfather Tiyu, his father Gong, and his mother née Sun. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Liangchen, Liangmin, and Liangjin. His wife was née Xue. He ranked fifty-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and thirty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Duan Guyan 段顧言, courtesy name Ruxing, was registered in a military household in Zunhua County, Ji Subprefecture, Shuntian Prefecture, and was originally from Linfen County, Shanxi. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing, his grandfather Jing, and his father Yongchang, a county magistrate. His father's former wife was née Guo, and his mother was née Zhang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His wife was née Li. He ranked thirty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 230th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Ruqi 周汝器, courtesy name Zicai, was registered in a civilian household in Luoshan County, Xinyang Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan. An attached student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twentieth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tong; his grandfather, Mengxian, held an honorary official title for longevity; his father was Ji; and his mother was née Peng. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Rugong, Ruluo, Ruguang, Ruming, and Rudi. His wife was née Hu. He ranked forty-sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and thirtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

任良貴〔貫江西撫州府臨川縣，民籍，縣學增廣生，治詩經，字汝爵，行七，年三十四，九月二十九日生〕。曾祖啓邦，祖希勝，父錦膺，母饒氏。具慶下，兄良善、良仁、良義、良秉、良彝、良富，弟良壽、良龍，娶黃氏。江西鄉試第四十四名，會試第二百七十九名。

馬濂〔貫直隸常州府無錫縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字濬卿，行一，年三十七，十月初一日生〕。曾祖綬，祖珮〔壽官〕，父鈍，母呂氏。具慶下，弟懰，娶□氏。應天府鄉試第三名，會試第二百三十五名。
translation_en:
Shi Yaochen, registered in Qingyang County, Chizhou Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was a county-school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Qinfu, he ranked second in family order, and he was aged thirty-one, born on the tenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yan, his grandfather Hong, his father Zongde, and his mother née Bao; both parents were living, his elder brother was Gongchen, his younger brothers were Shunchen, Wenchen, and Renchen, and his wife was née Xu; he placed 109th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 307th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Wentong, registered in Jing’an County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Yizhong, he ranked fifty-eighth in family order, and he was aged thirty-eight, born on the eleventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zibin, his grandfather Lian, his father Xian, his mother née Xiang, and his stepmother née Yu; both parents were living, his younger brothers were Zhi and Geng, and his wife was née Tu; he placed 26th in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination, while his Metropolitan Examination rank is partly illegible: □十八 [?].

Ren Lianggui, registered in Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an added-quota county-school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Rujue, he ranked seventh in family order, and he was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-ninth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qibang, his grandfather Xisheng, his father Jinying, and his mother née Rao; both parents were living, his elder brothers were Liangshan, Liangren, Liangyi (良義), Liangbing, Liangyi (良彝), and Liangfu, his younger brothers were Liangshou and Lianglong, and his wife was née Huang; he placed 44th in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 279th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Lian, registered in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Junqing, he ranked first in family order, and he was aged thirty-seven, born on the first day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shou, his grandfather Pei (holder of an honorary official title conferred for longevity), his father Dun, and his mother née Lü; both parents were living, his younger brother was Liu, and his wife’s surname is illegible (□); he placed third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 235th in the Metropolitan Examination.

張燈〔貫江西饒州府浮梁縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字文輝，行十七，年四十，九月十九日生〕。曾祖仕寧，祖滸，父樂，母鄭氏。永感下，兄炫、嫺、焸、羙、熾，弟焰、爟，娶朱氏。順天府鄉試第一百二十九名，會試第三百八名。

translation_en:
Zhang Jiefu, registered in a military household in Xinhui County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Chaobo; he ranked second in his family and was thirty-four years old, born on the twentieth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shizhong, his grandfather Rujian, and his father Qing; his mother was née Li. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Junfu, Jifu, and Houfu, and his wife was née Deng. He placed thirty-fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and ninetieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wei Xin, registered in a civilian household in Yangcheng County, Zezhou, Shanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhizheng; he ranked first in his family and was forty years old, born on the second day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wan, his grandfather Chengde, and his father Jin〔a government student granted the privilege of wearing official cap and girdle〕; his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His wife was née Wang. He placed seventh in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 183rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Deng, registered in a civilian household in Fuliang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Wenhui; he ranked seventeenth in his family and was forty years old, born on the nineteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shining, his grandfather Hu, and his father Le; his mother was née Zheng. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Xuan, Xian, Gu (焸) [?], Mei, and Chi; his younger brothers were Yan and Guan. His wife was née Zhu. He placed 129th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 308th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Zhengxiu, registered in a civilian household in Tongchuan Subprefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Record of Rites. His courtesy name was Zhong’an; he ranked second in his family and was thirty-three years old, born on the sixteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ce, his grandfather Zizhong, and his father Gong. His father’s former wife was née Ye, and his mother was née Cheng. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Zhengyi, Zhengming, and Zhengchuan. He married a woman née Zhou and subsequently a woman née Fu. He placed fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 249th in the Metropolitan Examination.

姚世熈〔貫貴州新添衛官籍，直隸舒城縣人，國子生，治易經，字思載，行一，生二十八，十月十一日生〕。曾祖信，祖鑑〔百戶〕，父璋，母胡氏。具慶下，弟世泰、世和，娶潘氏。貴州鄉試第四名，會試第一百四十九名。
translation_en:
Shi Tong, courtesy name Ruifu, was registered in an artisan household of the Embroidered Uniform Guard and was a native of Shangyuan County, Yingtian Prefecture. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-five [?], and born on the twenty-ninth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Liang, his grandfather Lun, and his father Duo; his father's former wife was née Zhang, and his mother was née Shan. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Kui, and his younger brothers were Da, Feng, and Qian. He married a woman née Sun. He placed ninetieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 254th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Minxue, courtesy name Xizeng, was registered in a civilian household in Baodi County, Shuntian Prefecture. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-two [?], and born on the twelfth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Jun, his grandfather Sheng, and his father Qi, a Patrol Inspector [?]; his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brother Wenxue was a Subprefectural Judge; his younger brothers were Zhixue and Jingxue. He married a woman née Wang. He placed seventieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 159th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Kai, courtesy name Zizhong, was registered in a civilian household in Wenshang County, Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-nine [?], and born on the second day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather Jue was posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate, and subsequently Left Vice Minister of War. His grandfather Ming was granted the title Secretary in the Ministry of War, posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate, and subsequently granted the posthumous title Left Vice Minister of War. His father Ying was Minister of War. His father's former wife, née Li, was posthumously titled Lady of Respect (gongren), subsequently elevated to Lady of Virtue (shuren); his mother, née Zheng, was granted the title Lady of Respect, subsequently elevated to Lady of Virtue. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Shi; his younger brothers were Zhu, an Imperial University student; Huai, a tribute scholar; and Gui and Geng, both students admitted by virtue of official family status. He married a woman née Xu. He placed eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and sixty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yao Shixi, courtesy name Sizai, was registered in an official household of Xintian Guard, Guizhou, and was a native of Shucheng County in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-eight [?], and born on the eleventh day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Xin, his grandfather Jian, a Company Commander, and his father Zhang; his mother was née Hu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shitai and Shihe. He married a woman née Pan. He placed fourth in the Guizhou Provincial Examination and 149th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Mou Zhen, courtesy name Yideng, was registered in a military household in Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan. A National University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was third in birth order, aged fifty-eight, and born on the first day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather Yongying was posthumously appointed Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate; his grandfather Feng was Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate; his father Zhengda was a department magistrate, advanced in rank to Grand Master for Governance; and his mother, née Yang, was granted the title of Senior Lady of Suitability. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Tai, a prefect, and Chun. His wife was née Chen. He placed twenty-seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 180th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Yi, courtesy name Junwan, was registered in a civilian household in Xianning County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. A National University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the fifth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mao; his grandfather was You; and his father, Wei, was a clerk in a Salt Distribution Commission. His mother was née Liu, and his stepmothers were née Yang and née Ge. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were E, Zhong, Tian, and Yong. His wife was née Sang. He placed twenty-eighth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 150th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Yingshi, courtesy name Ziyi, was registered in a military household of Henan Guard, Henan. A National University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the twenty-first day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hong; his grandfather was Lan; his father was Ji; and his mother was née Xin. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Suishi, Chengshi, and Jishi. His wife was née Li. He placed sixty-eighth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 293rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Rongren, courtesy name Weishan, was registered in a civilian household in Zhengzhou, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. A National University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the nineteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiang; his grandfather was Qi; his father was Dao; and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Anren and Yiren. His wife was née Yang. He placed third in the Henan Provincial Examination and 262nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yao Bangcai, a native of Gui’an County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was registered in a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Lunbo. He ranked first among his brothers and was forty-five years old, born on the third day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kai, a county clerk; his grandfather was Zhen, a county magistrate; his father was Shunchen; and his mother was née Wu. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Bangrong and Bangyan, and his wife was née Ye. He placed sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 297th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Sixian, a native of Wuling County, Changde Prefecture, Huguang, was registered in a military household and was a prefectural government school student. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Mingqing. He ranked sixth among his brothers and was thirty-one years old, born on the twenty-second day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian, chief of a Transport Office; his grandfather was Xiang, a guard registrar; his father was Wenxiang, a commandant of a Military Police Office; and his mother was née Yang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Siqing, his younger brother was Sizhong, and his wife was née Wang. He placed eighth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and eighty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Rulun, a native of Anping County, Jinzhou Subprefecture, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was registered in a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ruyan. He ranked first among his brothers and was forty years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian; his grandfather was Zhao; his father was Jie, a prestige official; and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His wife was née Li. He placed sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 190th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Ying, a native of Xuancheng County, Ningguo Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was registered in a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Dengzhi. He ranked second among his brothers and was forty-one years old, born on the first day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Taishi; his grandfather was Yuer; his father was Wei; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zi, Han, Ji, Zhu, and Ya. His wife was née Ma, and he subsequently married a woman née Tang. He placed 117th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 182nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Fan Zhongdai, registered in a civilian household in Qingyuan County, Baoding Prefecture, Zhili, was a prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Dongwang; he ranked first in his family and was thirty-five years old, born on the sixth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lian; his grandfather, Bing, was a magistrate; and his father, Yan, was an assistant instructor. His mother was née Hao, and his stepmother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Zhongheng. He married a woman née Chang and subsequently a woman née Zhang. He placed twenty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 236th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Wen, registered in a military household of the Chengdu Left Escort Guard in Sichuan, was an additional student of the prefectural government school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zixing; he ranked first in his family and was thirty-five years old, born on the twenty-first day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cong, his grandfather was Ji, and his father was Jing. His mother was née Pu, and his stepmother was née Wei. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Wen (問). He married a woman née Zhang. He placed fifty-sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 319th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Hanci, registered in a civilian household in Yingshan County, Sui Subprefecture, De'an Prefecture, Huguang, and originally from Jinxi County, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zixiu; he ranked twenty-first in his family and was thirty-seven years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bozhong, his grandfather was Xitai, and his father was Shan. His mother was née Li. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Hanlin, Hanzhang, and Hanzhi, and his younger brother was Hanshu. He married a woman née Ying and subsequently a woman née Min. He placed seventy-fifth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 232nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Ji, registered in a civilian household in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, was a prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Chaozong; he ranked first in his family and was forty-two years old, born on the thirteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Hu, held the rank of Gentleman for Rendering Service; his grandfather, Tong, was a magistrate; and his father, Dian, was an official in charge of the prefectural School of Yin and Yang (yinyang zhengshu). His mother was née Chen, and his stepmother was née Du. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Fang and Kan. He married a woman née Qian. He placed fiftieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 312th in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
岑遠〔貫廣東廣州府南海縣，軍籍，國子生，治易經，字昂霄，行四，年三十五，五月初一日生〕。曾祖桂清，祖觀全，父妙安，母梁氏。慈侍下，兄逵、貴逵，娶梁氏，繼娶喬氏。廣東鄉試第二十八名，會試第一百四十名。

錢鑄〔貫順天府大興縣，匠籍，直隸山陽縣人，國子生，治書經，字宗顏，行二，年三十八，十月二十四日生〕。曾祖通，祖昭，父洪，母張氏，繼母于氏。慈侍下，兄鐸，弟鏞、鎬、錄、鉉，娶閻氏。順天府鄉試第六十五名，會試第一百七十六名。

黃垣〔貫江西南昌府南昌縣，民籍，縣學附學生，治詩經，字拱辰，行四，年二十九，三月二十六日生〕。曾祖子厚，祖橙，父鍾〔歲貢生〕，母張氏，繼母熊氏。重慶下，兄圻，弟埏，娶萬氏。江西鄉試第二十名，會試第二百八十七名。

王守充〔貫廣東惠州府歸善縣，軍籍，縣學生，治易經，字美中，行三，年二十八，三月十五日生〕。曾祖璽，祖鳳翥，父密，母李氏。具慶下，兄守立、守高，娶集氏。廣東鄉試第十九名，會試第三百二十九名。
translation_en:
Cen Yuan, registered in a military household in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Angxiao; he ranked fourth in his family and was thirty-five years old, born on the first day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guiqing, his grandfather Guanquan, his father Miao’an, and his mother née Liang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Kui and Guikui [the division of these names is uncertain: 逵貴逵]. He married a woman née Liang and subsequently a woman née Qiao. He placed twenty-eighth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 140th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Zhu, registered in an artisan household in Daxing County, Shuntian Prefecture, and a native of Shanyang County in Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zongyan; he ranked second in his family and was thirty-eight years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tong, his grandfather Zhao, his father Hong, his mother née Zhang, and his stepmother née Yu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Duo, and his younger brothers were Yong, Gao, Lu, and Xuan. He married a woman née Yan. He placed sixty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 176th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Yuan, registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an additional student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Gongchen; he ranked fourth in his family and was twenty-nine years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zihou, his grandfather Cheng, his father Zhong〔an annual tribute student〕, his mother née Zhang, and his stepmother née Xiong. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Qi and his younger brother Shan. He married a woman née Wan. He placed twentieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 287th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Shouchong, registered in a military household in Guishan County, Huizhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Meizhong; he ranked third in his family and was twenty-eight years old, born on the fifteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xi, his grandfather Fengzhu, his father Mi, and his mother née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shouli and Shougao. He married a woman née Ji. He placed nineteenth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 329th in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
秦鈁〔貫浙江寧波府慈谿縣民籍，府學附學生，治《詩經》，字鳴和，行七十一，年二十九，十一月二十四日生〕。曾祖木，祖惇，父垠，前母楊氏，母劉氏，繼母王氏。慈侍下，兄鐸、鉅，弟銳，娶華氏。浙江鄉試第五十名，會試第十三名。

張雲霖〔貫遼東廣寧左衛官籍，山東歷城人，國子生，治《詩經》，字子潤，行一，年四十二，正月二十六日生〕。曾祖端，祖銘，父春，母郭氏，繼母吳氏。慈侍下，弟雲瑞，娶鄭氏，繼娶陳氏。順天府鄉試第六十二名，會試第三十三名。

紀公巡〔貫山東東昌府高唐州恩縣民籍，縣學增廣生，治《易經》，字恒甫，行二，年三十一，三月初七日生〕。曾祖綸〔監生〕，祖存仁〔知縣〕，父鶴〔醫官〕，母劉氏。具慶下，兄公遇，弟公遜、公迪、公述，娶馬氏。山東鄉試第五十八名，會試第二百七十九名。

陳宗虞〔貫四川保寧千戶所軍籍，國子生，治《春秋》，字于韶，行二，年二十八，四月初九日生〕。曾祖政，祖敏，父信，前母邢氏，母楊氏，繼母陸氏。具慶下，兄吉、宗周〔千戶〕，娶徐氏，繼娶楊氏。四川鄉試第二名，會試第二百一名。
translation_en:
Qin Fang 秦鈁, registered in a civilian household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an supplementary student of the prefectural school specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Minghe; he ranked seventy-first in family birth order and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mu, his grandfather Dun, and his father Yin; his father's former wife was née Yang, his mother née Liu, and his stepmother née Wang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Duo and Ju, and his younger brother Rui. His wife was née Hua. He placed fiftieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yunlin 張雲霖 was registered in an official household of Guangning Left Guard, Liaodong, and was a native of Licheng, Shandong. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he had the courtesy name Zirun, ranked first in family birth order, and was aged forty-two, born on the twenty-sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Duan, his grandfather Ming, and his father Chun; his mother was née Guo and his stepmother née Wu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Yunrui. His wife was née Zheng; he subsequently married a woman née Chen. He placed sixty-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ji Gongxun 紀公巡, registered in a civilian household in En County, Gaotang Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, was an added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Hengfu; he ranked second in family birth order and was aged thirty-one, born on the seventh day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lun, an Imperial University student; his grandfather was Cunren, a County Magistrate; and his father was He, a Medical Officer. His mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Gongyu, and his younger brothers were Gongxun 公遜, Gongdi, and Gongshu. His wife was née Ma. He placed fifty-eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 279th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Zongyu 陳宗虞, registered in a military household of the Baoning Battalion, Sichuan, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Yushao; he ranked second in family birth order and was aged twenty-eight, born on the ninth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zheng, his grandfather Min, and his father Xin; his father's former wife was née Xing, his mother née Yang, and his stepmother née Lu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ji and Zongzhou, the latter a Battalion Commander. His wife was née Xu; he subsequently married a woman née Yang. He placed second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 201st in the Metropolitan Examination.

宋繼先〔貫山東萊州府濰縣，軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字子孝，行三，年二十九，正月十九日生〕。曾祖英〔巡檢〕，祖鐸，父大強，母唐氏。具慶下，兄豹、繼商，弟繼魯，娶王氏。山東鄉試第十九名，會試第二百十名。

張峯〔貫福建泉州府惠安縣，民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字維直，行四，年四十一，正月二十七日生〕。曾祖茂〔縣丞〕，祖綸〔知縣，贈通議大夫、都察院右副都御史〕，父忱，母蔡氏。永感下，兄岳〔都察院右都御史〕、嵩、崑，弟嶢、崶、嵓，娶何氏。福建鄉試第二十名，會試第五十七名。

羅元禎〔貫江西饒州府鄱陽縣，匠籍，府學生，治詩經，字汝符，行八，年三十一，十一月初七日生〕。曾祖清，祖瑄，父容，母黃氏。慈侍下，兄元祐、元吉，弟元勳、元良、元氣、元齡、元和、元季、元亨，娶胡氏。江西鄉試第七十名，會試第二百六十九名。

欒尚約〔貫山東萊州府膠州，軍籍，國子生，治禮記，字孔源，行四，年二十四，十月二十日生〕。曾祖鳴，祖滋〔問官，贈文林郎、知縣〕，父麐〔代府右長史〕，母張氏〔贈孺人〕，繼母劉氏〔封孺人〕。具慶下，兄尚絅、尚忠、尚簡，弟尚縝、尚純，娶匡氏。山東鄉試第六十二名，會試第二百二十五名。
translation_en:
Song Jixian, registered in Wei County, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zixiao, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the nineteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying, a Police Chief; his grandfather was Duo; his father was Daqiang; and his mother was née Tang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Bao and Jishang, and his younger brother was Jilu. His wife was née Wang. He placed nineteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 210th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Feng, registered in Hui'an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Weizhi, he ranked fourth among his brothers, and he was aged forty-one, born on the twenty-seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mao, a County Vice Magistrate; his grandfather was Lun, a County Magistrate posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate; his father was Chen; and his mother was née Cai. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yue, Right Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate, Song, and Kun; his younger brothers were Yao, Feng, and Yan. His wife was née He. He placed twentieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fifty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Yuanzhen, registered in Poyang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to an artisan household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Rufu, he ranked eighth among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-one, born on the seventh day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qing; his grandfather was Xuan; his father was Rong; and his mother was née Huang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Yuanyou and Yuanji; his younger brothers were Yuanxun, Yuanliang, Yuanqi, Yuanling, Yuanhe, Yuanji, and Yuanheng. His wife was née Hu. He placed seventieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 269th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luan Shangyue, registered in Jiaozhou, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Kongyuan, he ranked fourth among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-four, born on the twentieth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ming; his grandfather was Zi, an official whose title is transcribed as wen guan [?], posthumously granted the titles Gentleman for Cultivated Service and County Magistrate; his father was Lin, Right Administrator in the household of the Prince of Dai; his mother was née Zhang, posthumously granted the title Lady; and his stepmother was née Liu, granted the title Lady. His father and stepmother were living. His elder brothers were Shangjiong, Shangzhong, and Shangjian; his younger brothers were Shangzhen and Shangchun. His wife was née Kuang. He placed sixty-second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 225th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Fang Youji, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student of the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Junjing. Third in family order, he was aged thirty-nine and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather, Chaozong, received successive honorary appointments culminating in Director of a Bureau in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites and was posthumously appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His grandfather, Liangjie, was Left Provincial Administration Commissioner; his father, Chongxi, was a tribute scholar. His father's former wife was Lady Lin, and his mother was Lady Weng. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were You𨌆 [name reading uncertain], a physician granted the privilege of wearing official cap and girdle, and Youchi, an Imperial University student. His younger brothers were Youning, Youyi, Youju (an Imperial University student), Youxu, Youchou, and Youbin. He married Lady Liu. He placed seventy-seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and one hundred eighty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Dai, registered in Taixing County, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a salt-producing household and was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Bozong. Second in family order, he was aged thirty-two and was born on the seventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tingzhang, his grandfather Yi, his father Shun, and his mother Lady Yu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yue; his younger brothers were Chong, Feng, Xue, Ye, and Jun. He married Lady He. He placed eighty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred thirty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Rushu, registered in Jinhua County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Chaoming. Forty-eighth in family order, he was aged thirty-six and was born on the fifteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kehou; his grandfather, Kun, received an honorary appointment as Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; his father, Quan, was an Assistant Provincial Surveillance Commissioner. His legal mother was Lady Zhu, who was granted the title Lady of Repose (anren), and his birth mother was Lady Huang. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Ruqian, Rujia, Ruzhou, Ruguang and Ruyao (both Imperial University students), Ruli (a Steward of Food), and Ruwei (a Registrar). His younger brothers were Rujing, Rulun, Ruyi, Rudao, Ruxin, and Ruzhi. He married Lady Chen. He placed second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and one hundred ninety-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Xiu, registered in Yongkang County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shiqing. Twenty-eighth in family order, he was aged thirty-five and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lun, his grandfather Lang, his father Qiang, and his mother Lady Hu. Both parents were living. His elder brother, Jun, was an Imperial University student; his younger brother was Hong. He married Lady Chen. He placed thirty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and one hundred second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Tao Tianzhong, registered in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was a prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shunzuo; he ranked sixth in family order, was aged thirty-three, and was born on the tenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yong, his grandfather Min, his father Yue, and his mother née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Tianjue and Tianchong. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Weng. He placed forty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 186th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Shouyu, registered in Daming County, Daming Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zifa; he ranked second in family order, was aged forty-five, and was born on the nineteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was An, his grandfather Lu (a prestige official), his father Xizhe, and his mother née Li. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Shouzhi; his younger brothers were Shoulu, Shouchun, Shouyue, Shouque, Shouguang, Shoumu, and Shoumo. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed 128th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 236th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wen Xiru, registered in Quanzhou, Guilin Prefecture, Guangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhenqing; he ranked third in family order, was aged thirty-three, and was born on the ninth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Keyu, his grandfather Junpin, his father Youlan, and his mother née Wu. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Xixiu (an Instructor). He married a woman née Wu and subsequently a woman née Tang. He placed seventh in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 261st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Yaowen, registered in Queshan County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Huibo; he ranked first in family order, was aged twenty-seven, and was born on the sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ren (an annual tribute student), his grandfather Wanyan (a Guard Registrar), his father Weijing, and his mother née Zhang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Yaowu, Yaoxun, Yaoru, and Yaode. He married a woman née Li. He placed fifteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 132nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Zhi, registered in an artisan household in Luoyang County, Henan Prefecture, Henan, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zili; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-eight, born on the thirteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hao, his grandfather Jiang, and his father Xiang, an Assistant Instructor; his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Dai, Guan, and Shen, and his wife was née Yang. He placed fifteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and sixty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yuanchun, registered in a civilian household in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Menghe; he ranked ninth among his brothers and was aged forty-two, born on the twenty-ninth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Min, his grandfather Zhe, and his father Zi; his mother was née Lou and his stepmother née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Di, and his younger brothers were Yuanmo, Cai, Yuandao, and Yuanjing, a tribute scholar (gongshi). His wife was née Chen. He placed forty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eighteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yao Shaozu, registered in a military household of the Dezhou Guard in Zhili, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Jingfang; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty-four, born on the tenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kang, his grandfather Yu, a Companion Reader advanced to the rank of Assistant Gentleman for Attendance, and his father Ning; his mother was née Jiang, and his stepmothers were née Yuan and née Jian [?]. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Jixian and Shengwu, and his wife was née Xu. He placed thirty-sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 263rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Yilan, registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ruguan; he ranked fifth among his brothers and was aged twenty-eight, born on the twelfth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qi, a County Vice Magistrate, his grandfather Yun’e, and his father Xianwei; his mother was née Xu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yihong and Yichao, and his wife was née Yu. He placed thirty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 275th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chang Yingshi, of a military household registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was an attached student of the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Tingzuo. He ranked third in his family and was aged twenty-seven, born on the second day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Menghe, an honorary official honored for longevity; his grandfather was Tijing; his father was Zaitong; and his mother was née Zhu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yingrui, Yingfu, and Yinghui (a tribute student), and his younger brothers were Yingke and Yingji. He married a woman née Luo and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed fifteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 277th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Yichuan, of an official household registered in Duchang County, Nankang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Tixing. He ranked thirtieth in his family and was aged forty-one, born on the seventeenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ling; his grandfather was Shanhui; his father was Xun; his mother was née Li; and his stepmother was née Shu. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Yifei. He married a woman née Wang. He placed fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and eighty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wan Minying, of a military household registered in the Right Battalion of Maoshan Guard under the Daning Regional Military Commission, was a native of Jiangxia County, Huguang, and a student of the Yizhou departmental school in the metropolitan region. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zicai. He ranked fourth in his family and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuan; his grandfather was Jing, an honorary official recognized for public beneficence; and his father was Kui, a county registrar. His legal mother was née Zhou, and his birth mother was née Zhao. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Minhe (an honorary official recognized for public beneficence), Minjun, and Minjie; his younger brothers were Minping and Minfan (a tribute student). He married a woman née Yue. He placed sixty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 136th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Guangyuan, of a civilian household registered in Qi County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, and designated a wealthy household in Pingyin County, was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zixu. He ranked first in his family and was aged forty-six, born on the fourth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian; his grandfather was Cong; his father was Chijing, a student of the Imperial University; his mother was née Li; and his stepmother was also née Li. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Guangyun (a ninth-rank titular official), Guangsui, Guangying (a tribute student), and Guangxuan. He married a woman née Xu. He placed thirty-first in the Henan Provincial Examination and seventy-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Tan Nie 譚臬, courtesy name Chaoxian, was registered in a civilian household in Fuzhou, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the departmental school, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He ranked second in his family and was thirty-one years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Benfang; his grandfather, Zongxue, held an honorary longevity title; his father, Wei, was granted the title of Case Reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review; and his mother, née Shen, was granted the title of Lady (Ruren). His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Qi, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission, Rong, and Jiang; his younger brothers were Qu and Liang. He married a woman née Hu. He placed sixty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 213th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yan Hui 顏會, courtesy name Liqing, was registered in a military household in Longxi County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He ranked first in his family and was thirty-seven years old, born on the sixteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Guangli; his grandfather, Zijing; his father, Fuyong; and his mother, née Yang. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. He married a woman née He. He placed twenty-seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 155th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pei Tianyou 裴天祐, courtesy name Shunzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Ganyu County, Haizhou, Huai'an Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked third in his family and was forty-one years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Sheng; his grandfather, Tong, was a County Vice Magistrate; his father, Zhang, was a student of the Imperial University; and his mother was née Zhong. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Tianlun and Tianzuo; his younger brothers were Tianni and Tianze. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed seventy-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 239th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Rui 孫銳, courtesy name Xichun, was registered in a military household in Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Book of Rites. He ranked fourth in his family and was forty years old, born on the fifth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Wenze; his grandfather, Kai; and his father, Zan. His father's principal wife was née Wang, his stepmother was née Huang, and his birth mother was née Ding. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Jian, Ju, who held an honorary longevity title, and Keng, an Assistant Prefect. He married a woman née Zhou. He placed ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 193rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

牛輓〔貫山西澤州高平縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字伯行，行三，年四十二，四月二十六日生〕。曾祖睿，祖拳，父璉，母李氏。永感下，兄輔、軒，弟軏，娶秦氏，繼娶李氏。山西鄉試第十一名，會試第三百二名。

趙時舉〔貫廣東潮州府饒平縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字存晦，行一，年四十一，七月十三日生〕。曾祖權，祖試，父通〔知州〕，母張氏。永感下，娶陳氏，繼娶周氏。廣東鄉試第十七名，會試第二百八十五名。
translation_en:
Jian Yingqi 蹇應祺, registered in Jingyang County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Boji, he was seventh in birth order, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the fourth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen; his grandfather, Luan; his father, Xian, a district magistrate; and his mother, née Liu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Yongkang, Yongning (Assistant Surveillance Commissioner in the Shaanxi Provincial Surveillance Commission), Yingxiang, Yingchen, and Yongheng; his younger brothers were Yingsu and Yinghu. He married a woman née Liu. He ranked fifty-ninth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 233rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Peng Jiye 彭繼業, registered in the Jiaozhou Guard Battalion, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was originally from Longquan County, Jiangxi; he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, with the courtesy name Dafang, second in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the third day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuan, posthumously appointed a secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice; his grandfather, Zan, a secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice; his father, Heling, an assistant instructor; and his mother, née Ji. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Jizu, a tribute scholar (gongshi). He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Li. He ranked seventieth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and ninety-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Niu Wan 牛輓, registered in Gaoping County, Zezhou, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Boxing, he was third in birth order, and he was aged forty-two, born on the twenty-sixth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rui; his grandfather, Quan; his father, Lian; and his mother, née Li. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Fu and Xuan; his younger brother was Yue. He married a woman née Qin and subsequently a woman née Li. He ranked eleventh in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 302nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Shiju 趙時舉, registered in Raoping County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Cunhui, he was first in birth order, and he was aged forty-one, born on the thirteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Quan; his grandfather, Shi; his father, Tong, a department magistrate; and his mother, née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. He married a woman née Chen and subsequently a woman née Zhou. He ranked seventeenth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 285th in the Metropolitan Examination.

陶應龍〔貫直隸真定府冀州棗強縣，軍籍，縣學生，治詩經，字文化，行一，年四十二，十一月二十日生〕。曾祖源，祖全，父明，母楊氏。具慶下，弟應麒，娶高氏，繼娶李氏。順天府鄉試第一百十八名，會試第二百四十六名。

translation_en:
Zheng Fengyang, registered in Gu’an County, Shuntian Prefecture, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Daoheng; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-seven, and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Sigong, his grandfather Chun, his father Shu, and his mother Lady Pang; his mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother Fengshi was a tribute scholar. He married Lady Fang. He placed 132nd in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 36th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Chun, registered in Xianling Guard, Huguang, belonged to an official household and was an added student at the Jingzhou Prefectural School specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Mingshu; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged twenty-six, and was born on the ninth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Tong, his grandfather Kang, his father Ning, and his mother Lady Zhao; his mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Zhu 銖 and Zhi 鋕. He married Lady Jiang. He placed 38th in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 173rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tao Yinglong, registered in Zaoqiang County, Jizhou Subprefecture, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was a county-school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Wenhua; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged forty-two, and was born on the twentieth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Yuan, his grandfather Quan, his father Ming, and his mother Lady Yang; both parents were living. His younger brother was Yingqi. He married Lady Gao and subsequently Lady Li. He placed 118th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 246th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Guobin, registered in Lanxi County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Rujia; his family birth-order rank is recorded as ninetieth [?], he was aged thirty-two, and he was born on the twenty-seventh day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Qi, a District Magistrate; his grandfather was Beng and his father Zuan. His father’s former wife was Lady Zhao, and his mother was Lady Chen; his father was living and his mother deceased. He married Lady Shao. He placed 89th in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 301st in the Metropolitan Examination.

□ Wenhan (surname illegible), courtesy name Zeye, was registered in a military household of Fenzhou Guard, Shanxi, and was a native of Mengcheng County, directly administered territory. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the twenty-second day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Quan; his grandfather, Lin; and his father, Ji, held an honorary title for longevity. His father's former wife was née Wu, and his mother was née Huang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Wenzong, Wenxuan, Wenrong (an honorary official recognized for charitable contributions), and Wenhua. His wife was née Han. He placed twenty-third in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 151st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Dounan, courtesy name Ziyi, was registered in a salt-producing household of Yancheng County, Huai'an Prefecture, directly administered territory. A county government student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the fourth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongmei; his grandfather, Lun; and his father, Xun, a District Magistrate. His mother was née Liu, and his stepmother was née Ji. His father was living, and his mother was deceased. His elder brothers were Doujue and Douji; his younger brothers were Doubi, Doushu, Douxiang, Douke, and Yinan. His wife was née Xia. He placed fifteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Jixian, courtesy name Zongchen, was registered in a civilian household of Guangde Subprefecture, directly administered territory. An Imperial University student specializing in the Record of Rites, he was sixth in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-third day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ci; his grandfather, Hao; and his father, Wei. His mother was née Ge, and his stepmother was née Hou. His mother was living, and his father was deceased. His elder brother was Shangwen; his younger brothers were Shangzhi, Shangyou, and Shangshi. His wife was née Bu. He placed 109th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 278th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Jiayin, courtesy name Xiaofu, was registered in a military household of Tongliang County, He Subprefecture, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan. A county government student specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-four, and born on the fifth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jiong; his grandfather, Yueyi; and his father, Wenjin. His mother was née Shen. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Zongyin, and his younger brother was Xiyin. His wife was née Xiang. He placed fifteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and eighty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.
