translation_en:
…and acts as Heaven’s son. If Heaven’s heart has not been satisfied, his conduct as a son is deficient. He governs the people and acts as their father and mother. If the people’s livelihood has not been secured, his duties as their parent remain unfulfilled. His responsibility is truly no light one, and his task truly no easy one. Yet his efforts have a foundation: the heart. They also have a practical expression: government. When his heart can move Heaven and transform the people, the foundation of inner sagehood is established; when his government can serve Heaven and cherish the people as his children, the practical expression of outward kingliness is realized. In governing all under Heaven, a ruler need only cultivate these two things.

Yet, considered more deeply, Heaven and the people differ in their respective positions, but the principle underlying them is interconnected. Reverence and diligence differ as activities, but their effects depend upon one another. Thus, one who knows how to revere Heaven will surely also diligently care for the people; one who knows how to labor for the people may indeed be one who serves Heaven well. The Book of Documents says: “Heaven bestows kindness upon the people; the sovereign serves Heaven.” It also says: “Heaven aids the people below, providing them with rulers and teachers.” Heaven therefore has compassion for the people: what the people desire, Heaven will surely follow. If the ruler can truly devote greater care to the people, could the means of winning Heaven’s favor lie anywhere beyond this?

Examining the historical course of decline and flourishing, rise and fall, we find that it has generally proceeded from this. People know that Yao revered Heaven and Shun attended reverently to Heaven’s commands, but they do not know that bringing order and harmony, cherishing those afar and winning over those nearby, were the actual substance of their reverence for Heaven. People know that Yu scrupulously heeded Heaven’s warnings and Tang obediently followed Heaven’s mandate, but they do not know that making the land habitable and enabling the people to eat grain, and being generous and benevolent, were the actual substance of their reverence for Heaven. People know that King Wen reverently upheld Heaven’s awe-inspiring authority and King Wu honored Heaven’s settled mandate, but they do not know that issuing measures of government and practicing benevolence, and extending aid throughout the four quarters, were the actual substance of their reverence for Heaven. punctuated:
數聖人者善承天道，故直體其陰隲惠愛之意，而代終其事。是以上則當乎天心，下則協乎人心，唐虞三代之治於今為烈也。降而春秋，君德寖衰，如日食、星隕、雨雹、地震之類，告戒甚明，而迄不聞其修省之實。獨楚莊王以天無災異為天且忘我，似足以語天人之際矣。然而虐用其民，殆無虛日，豈知事天之道者哉？漢唐宋之世，或素服避殿，議賑蠲租；或謫見日月，寢兵罷事；或徹樂减膳，遣使勸農；或星孛營室，求言釋囚。是皆英君誼辟勵精圖治，固足以消回天變，而奠安民社矣。然惜其天德未純，王道弗究，雖能行之於一時，而不能持之以悠久。說者謂其倖福而為善，懼禍而不為惡，律以帝王誠心直道之事，槩乎未之有得也。
洪惟我太祖高皇帝，本天授聖人之資，當拯溺亨屯之任，規為燕貽，以開萬世之太平者，慮至遠矣。而於敬天勤民二者，尤汲汲焉。如《洪範》庶徵之應，語博士許存仁；祈天永命之道，語縣令許好問。因冬
translation_en:
…These several sages were adept at carrying out the Way of Heaven. Thus they directly embodied its intention to provide unseen protection and benevolent care, and completed its work on its behalf. Above, they accorded with Heaven’s heart; below, they harmonized with the people’s hearts. The governance of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties remains illustrious to this day. By the Spring and Autumn period, rulers’ virtue had gradually declined. Solar eclipses, falling stars, hailstorms, earthquakes, and the like conveyed unmistakable warnings, yet we hear of no genuine efforts at self-cultivation and reflection. King Zhuang of Chu alone took Heaven’s failure to send calamities or anomalies to mean, “Heaven is about to forget me.” This might seem sufficient to qualify him to discuss the relationship between Heaven and humanity. Yet scarcely a day passed without his cruelly exploiting his people. How could he have understood the way to serve Heaven?
In the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties, some rulers donned plain robes and withdrew from their main halls, deliberating on relief and remitting taxes. Some, when signs of Heaven’s censure appeared in the sun and moon, halted military operations and suspended undertakings. Some stopped musical performances and reduced their meals, dispatching envoys to encourage agriculture. Some, when a comet appeared in the Yingshi lunar mansion, solicited frank counsel and released prisoners. These were all enlightened rulers and righteous sovereigns exerting themselves to achieve good government. Such measures were indeed sufficient to avert Heaven’s portents and secure the people and the state. Regrettably, however, their heavenly virtue was not yet pure, and they had not fully realized the Kingly Way. Though they could practice these measures for a time, they could not sustain them indefinitely. Commentators say that they did good in hopes of obtaining blessings and refrained from evil for fear of disaster. Measured against the sincere hearts and upright conduct of the sage emperors and kings, they had, on the whole, attained no real understanding.
We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao, endowed by Heaven with the qualities of a sage, undertook the responsibility of rescuing those drowning in distress and bringing deliverance from hardship. His plans to bequeath peace to his descendants and inaugurate tranquility for ten thousand generations were far-reaching indeed. He was especially diligent in these two matters: revering Heaven and laboring for the people. Thus he spoke to the Erudite Xu Cunren about the responses manifested in the various signs described in the “Great Plan” (Hongfan), and to District Magistrate Xu Haowen about the way to pray to Heaven for an enduring mandate. translation_en:
…cold, he thought of the soldiers guarding the frontier; when spring brought mild weather, he felt compassion for those confined in prison. Such were his ordinary concerns and plans. During severe drought, when he reduced his meals, everyone in the palace did likewise; when prolonged rains would not cease, he provided relief, distributed aid, and extended loans. His hardships in wearing straw sandals and sleeping on the ground went beyond mere frugality in his quarters and personal provisions. The Empress and the consorts tended the cooking fires, remembering the work of their former farming households. Such, too, were his efforts to turn matters around when calamities occurred. He thus made Heaven’s heart his own heart and took the people’s cares as his own. For one hundred and eighty years, Heaven’s blessings have arrived in increasing abundance, and the people’s allegiance has become firmly united. The flourishing of government and moral transformation has directly rivaled high antiquity: one cannot deny that this resulted from the nurturing efforts of the sagely founder. Confucian ministers of that time, such as Song Lian and Liu Ji, praised either his cultivation of virtue and examination of his faults or his wholehearted love for the people. Their praises and widely proclaimed encomiums were certainly no exaggeration. His example truly deserves to be transmitted through all ages as a standard for those who rule the world.
The successive sagely emperors arose in turn, further magnifying the work of carrying on his legacy. Their filial devotion in serving Heaven and their benevolence extending to those below were handed down in succession; predecessors and successors followed a single Way. How magnificent were their achievements in bringing the blessings of those above and below into harmony and fostering an age of prosperity and concord!
Thus our present Emperor’s achievements rank alongside the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humankind—and his Way brings aid to all living beings. There is a song on the Great Requital and an ode on Revering Heaven: these are like Shang Tang’s prayer in the Mulberry Grove. There is a composition on the Spirit of Grain and a rhapsody on the Silkworm Altar…

text:
虞帝南風之奏也寅奉欽若之誠惠鮮計安
之念存之於中而發之為文本之於心而敷
之為政其敬
天勤民無所不用其極是以嘉祥屢臻方内乂寧
天人交應信不誣矣而
聖諭復以水旱饑荒苗狄弗靖民生未遂治化未
孚為憂者此固
陛下望治無窮之心謙冲自牧之志也然臣竊觀
天下之勢不免有如
聖制所云者此其故何也臣愚以為
===
陛下心足以格天而奉天之政容有未備德足以
化民而子民之政容有未周
陛下精誠昭事非不加意於奉天之政也然而祗
承於下者能無或失其意乎
陛下仁愛洽浹非不加意於子民之政也然而宣
力於位者能無或鮮其良乎是故水旱饑荒
賑貸之令不可不行也今漂沒之患萬頃為
淤亢魃之災千畝盡赤展轉流離之苦不可
勝言而守令未聞拯濟之方求其撫字心勞
催科政拙者盖不多見矣苗狄未靖撻伐之

…these are like Emperor Shun’s performance of the South Wind song. Your reverent sincerity in serving and following Heaven, and your concern to favor the needy and plan for their security, are held within and expressed in writing, rooted in the heart and extended into government. In revering Heaven and diligently caring for the people, you exert yourself to the utmost. Thus auspicious signs have repeatedly appeared, and peace and order prevail throughout the realm. That Heaven and humanity respond to one another is indeed no empty claim. Yet your sagely instructions again express anxiety over floods, droughts, and famine; the unrest among the Miao and Di peoples; the people’s unfulfilled livelihoods; and the failure of transforming government to win their trust. This surely reflects Your Majesty’s boundless aspiration for good government and your resolve to cultivate yourself with humility. Yet, as your servant privately observes conditions throughout the realm, there are indeed circumstances such as those described in your imperial composition. Why is this so? In my humble view, Your Majesty’s heart is sufficient to move Heaven, yet the measures of government through which you serve Heaven may still be incomplete; your virtue is sufficient to transform the people, yet the measures through which you nurture them as your children may still fall short.
Your Majesty serves Heaven with perfect sincerity and manifest reverence: it is certainly not that you neglect the measures for serving Heaven. Yet can those below who reverently carry them out always avoid missing your intent? Your Majesty’s benevolent love reaches everywhere: it is certainly not that you neglect the measures for nurturing the people. Yet among those exerting themselves in office, might there not be some deficient in goodness? Thus, when floods, droughts, and famine occur, orders for relief grants and loans must be implemented. 寇疆侵軼無忌桀驁倡獗之勢不可漸長而
將帥未成擒撲之功求其匈奴未滅何以家
為者盖不多見矣夫人臣之職所以宣上德
達下情翊贊皇猷弼成至治者也今貪殘玩

上則民生之弗遂治化之未孚無怪其然也
何以仰副
上天仁愛之心少紓
陛下宵旰之慮哉此臣所深懼而皇皇然欲一言

…the might of punitive warfare must be displayed. Now the southern barbarians gather in bands, and their attacks and conquests penetrate ever deeper; the northern barbarians raid our borders and make incursions without restraint. Their defiant, rampant [?] power must not be allowed to grow, yet our commanders have accomplished no feats of capture and suppression. Few among them, indeed, can be found who hold that “Until the Xiongnu are destroyed, what need have I of a home?”

The duty of a minister is to spread the sovereign’s virtue, convey the circumstances of those below, assist imperial plans, and help bring perfect government to fruition. Now the evils of greed, cruelty, negligence, and idle delay increase daily below, while the authority to reward and punish, dismiss and promote, has not been made manifest above. It is therefore no wonder that the people’s livelihoods fail to flourish and the transforming influence of government has yet to win their confidence. How can this accord with High Heaven’s benevolent concern and somewhat ease Your Majesty’s anxieties, which keep you occupied before dawn and late into the evening? This is what your servant deeply fears, and why, in my disquiet, I wish to offer a word to give expression to my anxieties, like those of the man of Qi who feared the sky would fall. Now, fortunately, I have reached an occasion on which I may speak. How dare I fail to lay before Your Majesty all the humble thoughts of a mere gatherer of grass and firewood?

The disposition of the realm comprises, within, the prefectures and counties: when these obtain suitable men, the foundation of the state is secure. Without are the frontiers: when these obtain suitable men, the state’s might is invigorated. Thus, in securing peace within, nothing takes precedence over selecting prefects and county magistrates. That prefects and magistrates lack worth is not because officials’ habits cannot be changed, but simply because the means of encouraging and disciplining them have not been fully employed. …while the four seasons, cold and heat, each keep their appointed order.” This is surely the judgment of one who understands governance. This is what befits the great ruler; through it, all the substantive duties of revering Heaven and diligently caring for the people will likewise be fulfilled.

Yet your servant has also heard this: the court is the guiding pole of the four quarters, and the ruler’s person is the source of all transformation. “If the sovereign can be sage, his ministers will carry out his will without being commanded.” Assisting and supporting the ruler in bringing his work to completion is certainly the duty of his ministers; but setting the example and taking the lead are responsibilities Your Majesty must personally fulfill. Foolish, rash, and unenlightened as I am, I venture further to speak of the ultimate foundation: Your Majesty’s sagely virtue is pure, yet the work of self-examination must especially not be delayed. The Book of Changes says: “Examine your conduct and assess its auspices; on completing the cycle, there is supreme good fortune.” It also says: “‘Returning with steadfast sincerity brings no regret’: this means examining oneself through the mean.”

Your servant wishes that Your Majesty would test this in your own experience in the secluded depths of the palace, exercise discerning awareness during times of recreation and peaceful repose, distinguish the workings of impulse at their first stirrings, and investigate matters fully after actions have become manifest. Only when there is truly not a single thought or deed that fails to accord with Heaven will reverence for Heaven reach its utmost and your responsibility as the principal heir be fulfilled. Only when there is truly not a single thought or deed that fails to show concern for the people will diligent care for them reach its utmost and your responsibility as their parent be fulfilled. This is precisely the method of turning one’s scrutiny inward and the essential practice of vigilance when alone. What Zhou Dunyi called reflection and what Zhu Xi called careful examination both refer to this way. If you embody and practice it, your heavenly virtue will grow ever purer and the kingly way ever more refined. None among the many officials and offices will dare fail to purify themselves wholeheartedly in receiving your beneficent rule. translation_en:
…pervades all things, and supreme harmony responds abundantly. The sun, moon, and stars follow their proper courses; the four seasons proceed in order; the eight Man peoples offer tribute, and the nine Yi peoples submit. All things bearing blessings and all auspicious signs that can be brought forth gather in profusion. What the Book of Odes describes as “Heaven protects and establishes you, with the utmost firmness”; what the Book of Documents describes as “the hundred grains thereby ripen, and worthy men thereby become distinguished”; and what the “Evolution of Rites” chapter of the Book of Rites describes as “Heaven does not withhold its Way, earth does not withhold its treasures, and people do not withhold their true feelings”—all are borne out today. How could the highest state of good government be unattainable?

These words are like humble turnips and radishes: if Your Majesty will gather what is useful in them without rejecting them for their lowly roots, the realm will be most fortunate, and your foolish servant most fortunate indeed! Having presumed to offend Your Majesty’s heavenly dignity, your servant trembles in utmost fear, as though about to fall and perish. Your servant respectfully submits this reply.

title: 嘉靖二十九年進士登科錄
text:
臣姜金和
臣對臣聞帝王之治天下善事乎天而天心
無不眷者推此心之孝也善體乎民而民生
無不遂者推此心之仁也夫天以參贊之責
付之人不欽翼以事之則褻褻則違乎天矣
唯能推此心之孝斯足以格天而無不默相
之者焉民以輯寧之治望之君不懷保以體
之則慢慢則拂乎民矣唯能推此心之仁斯
足以感民而無不丕應之者焉蓋天人一理
也人君事天猶父而與天默契則天之道在
===
我矣由是以心之天格天之天天何有於違
也上下一情也人君視民猶子而與民無間
則民之情在我矣由是以己之心感民之心
民何有於違也蓋惟辟奉天惟天眷德有抑
畏之心者致仁愛之祐盡人而天自合也惟
上作德惟民從乂有勵精之心者成和平之
化脩己而民自安也人君不患天之不可格
而患己不能盡其孝不患民之不能治而患
己不能盡其仁以孝事天則事之無不至以
仁育民則育之無不盡自古帝王之治天下

臣姜金和。

臣對：臣聞帝王之治天下，善事乎天而天心無不眷者，推此心之孝也；善體乎民而民生無不遂者，推此心之仁也。夫天以參贊之責付之人，不欽翼以事之則褻，褻則違乎天矣。唯能推此心之孝，斯足以格天，而無不默相之者焉。民以輯寧之治望之君，不懷保以體之則慢，慢則拂乎民矣。唯能推此心之仁，斯足以感民，而無不丕應之者焉。蓋天人一理也，人君事天猶父，而與天默契，則天之道在我矣。由是以心之天格天之天，天何有於違也？上下一情也，人君視民猶子，而與民無間，則民之情在我矣。由是以己之心感民之心，民何有於違也？蓋惟辟奉天，惟天眷德，有抑畏之心者致仁愛之祐，盡人而天自合也。惟上作德，惟民從乂，有勵精之心者成和平之化，脩己而民自安也。人君不患天之不可格，而患己不能盡其孝；不患民之不能治，而患己不能盡其仁。以孝事天，則事之無不至；以仁育民，則育之無不盡。自古帝王之治天下
translation_en:
Your servant Jiang Jinhe.

Your servant replies: I have heard that when emperors and kings govern All under Heaven, those who serve Heaven well and invariably enjoy its favor do so by extending the filial devotion within their hearts; those who attend well to the people and enable all to prosper in their livelihoods do so by extending the benevolence within their hearts. Heaven entrusts human beings with responsibility for assisting its transforming and nourishing work. To serve it without reverence and care is irreverence, and irreverence runs counter to Heaven. Only by extending the filial devotion within one's heart can one move Heaven and invariably receive its unseen assistance. The people look to their ruler for government that brings harmony and peace. To attend to them without cherishing and protecting them is negligence, and negligence runs counter to the people's wishes. Only by extending the benevolence within one's heart can one move the people and invariably elicit their full response.

Heaven and humanity share a single principle. When the ruler serves Heaven as a father and is in tacit accord with it, Heaven's Way resides within him. Thus, through the Heaven within his heart, he moves Heaven above: how could Heaven oppose him? Those above and those below share the same feelings. When the ruler regards the people as his children and no estrangement separates him from them, their feelings reside within him. Thus, through his own heart, he moves the hearts of the people: how could the people oppose him?

The sovereign reverently serves Heaven, and Heaven cherishes virtue. One whose heart is humble and reverent obtains the blessings of Heaven's benevolent love: by fulfilling one's human duties, one naturally comes into accord with Heaven. Those above cultivate virtue, and the people follow in good order. One whose heart is intent on diligent endeavor achieves a transformation toward harmony and peace: by cultivating oneself, one naturally brings peace to the people. The ruler should worry not that Heaven cannot be moved, but that he himself cannot fully realize his filial devotion; not that the people cannot be governed, but that he himself cannot fully realize his benevolence. If he serves Heaven with filial devotion, his service will be complete in every respect; if he nurtures the people with benevolence, his care will leave nothing undone. From antiquity, when emperors and kings governed All under Heaven…

translation_en:
…The heart they preserved was invariably one of revering Heaven and diligently caring for the people; the government they extended was invariably one of taking Heaven as their model and protecting the people. This is how government reaches its greatest flourishing. That our dynasty equals the glory of high antiquity and surpasses anything the Han, Tang, or Song could attain rests precisely on this.

…the most spiritually endowed. The truly intelligent becomes the sovereign; the sovereign becomes the father and mother of the people.” Thus, although Heaven and humanity differ in their stations, their principle is one; although ruler and people are separated by their positions, their feelings communicate. The ruler is Heaven’s principal heir and the father and mother of the people. These roles originate in a single principle and cannot be regarded as separate.

I reverently reflect that Your Majesty has grandly received Heaven’s Mandate and assumed the responsibility of cherishing and bringing peace to the people. You have held dominion over the realm and been lord of its countless subjects for twenty-nine years now. Throughout the utmost reaches of Heaven and Earth, your reverent virtue has silently won trust, and your benevolent bounty has spread abundantly. Yet you still desire reverently to serve Heaven, so that the Lord on High may duly accept your offerings, and diligently to care for the people, so that those below may reverently live in harmony. Thus you investigate distant antiquity to seek the foundations for promoting the Way and achieving good government; and you take your more recent ancestors as models, inquiring into the way to establish the supreme standard and bequeath enduring rules. How could your ignorant servant be adequate to range through past and present and expound □□ [?]? Nevertheless, I dare not withhold anything I have heard in making my reply.

Examining high antiquity, we find Yao reverently following August Heaven, Shun diligently attending to Heaven’s commands, Yu reverently receiving the commands of the Lord on High, Tang reverently honoring Heaven’s Way, King Wen regarding Heaven as both watching over and protecting him, and King Wu neither growing lax nor forgetting. Their ways of revering Heaven differed, but all converged upon filial devotion. Yao’s benevolence was like Heaven; Shun’s virtue cherished life; Yu’s thoughts were untiring; Tang was tolerant and benevolent; King Wen cherished and protected the common people; and King Wu bestowed great gifts throughout the Four Seas. title: 嘉靖二十九年進士登科錄
text:
治發之為禮樂教化著之為典章文物雖不
可以盡述莫非敬天勤民之心以基之矣嗣
是而下若高祖之於漢櫟陽方還即舉天地
四方之祀中原甫定遂下約法弛民之詔是
亦敬天勤民之心也故能成創造之功太宗
之於唐欲合天意而持兢兢業業之心推心
惻物欲收濟世安民之績是亦敬天勤民之
心也故能成貞觀之治太祖之于宋信宿禱
天弭天災之流行日夜焦勞念霖雨之不止
亦敬天之心也仁厚立國嘉治世愛民之言
===
夙夜畏懼求以德化民之義亦勤民之心也
故不勞而集一統之業之三君者雖不能如
帝王仁孝之純亦可以當天人順應之歸矣
又降是而躬脩玄默勸趣農桑者漢之文帝
亦可謂用心于敬天勤民矣而刑措之風成
焉不事佚樂勵精政事唐之玄宗亦可謂用
心于敬天勤民矣而開元之治臻焉聞雷露
立禁中夜禱却獻瑞事儉約宋之仁宗亦可
謂敬天勤民者矣故社稷長遠終必賴之若
此者雖未及乎創業之諸君亦可謂守成之

治，發之為禮樂教化，著之為典章文物，雖不可以盡述，莫非敬天勤民之心以基之矣。嗣是而下，若高祖之於漢，櫟陽方還，即舉天地四方之祀；中原甫定，遂下約法弛民之詔，是亦敬天勤民之心也，故能成創造之功。太宗之於唐，欲合天意，而持兢兢業業之心；推心惻物，欲收濟世安民之績，是亦敬天勤民之心也，故能成貞觀之治。太祖之于宋，信宿禱天，弭天災之流行；日夜焦勞，念霖雨之不止，亦敬天之心也。仁厚立國，嘉治世愛民之言；夙夜畏懼，求以德化民之義，亦勤民之心也，故不勞而集一統之業。之三君者，雖不能如帝王仁孝之純，亦可以當天人順應之歸矣。

又降是而躬脩玄默，勸趣農桑者，漢之文帝，亦可謂用心于敬天勤民矣，而刑措之風成焉。不事佚樂，勵精政事，唐之玄宗，亦可謂用心于敬天勤民矣，而開元之治臻焉。聞雷露立，禁中夜禱，却獻瑞，事儉約，宋之仁宗，亦可謂敬天勤民者矣，故社稷長遠，終必賴之。若此者，雖未及乎創業之諸君，亦可謂守成之
translation_en:
…good government, giving it expression in rites, music, teaching, and moral transformation, and embodying it in institutions, regulations, and the forms of civilized culture. Though these cannot all be recounted, none lacked a foundation in a heart that revered Heaven and labored for the people. Among those who followed, Gaozu of the Han, for example, had only just returned to Yueyang when he instituted sacrifices to Heaven, Earth, and the four quarters. As soon as the Central Plain was pacified, he issued an edict simplifying the laws and easing the people's burdens. This, too, expressed a heart that revered Heaven and labored for the people; thus he accomplished the founding of his dynasty. Taizong of the Tang wished to accord with Heaven's will and maintained a vigilant and conscientious heart. Extending his heartfelt compassion to others, he sought to aid the world and bring peace to the people. This, too, expressed a heart that revered Heaven and labored for the people; thus he achieved the good government of the Zhenguan era. Taizu of the Song prayed to Heaven for two nights to halt the spread of heavenly calamities. Anxious and weary day and night, he worried that the prolonged rains would not cease: this, too, was a heart that revered Heaven. He founded his state upon benevolence and generosity, commending words about governing the world and loving the people. Fearful and vigilant morning and night, he sought the principles of transforming the people through virtue: this, too, was a heart that labored for the people. Thus, without toil, he accomplished the work of unification. Although these three rulers could not equal the ancient emperors and kings in the purity of their benevolence and filial devotion, they could nevertheless merit the favorable response of Heaven and the allegiance of the people.

Further down the succession, Emperor Wen of the Han personally cultivated profound quietude and encouraged farming and sericulture. He, too, may be said to have devoted his heart to revering Heaven and laboring for the people; thus a state of affairs in which punishments could be set aside came into being. Xuanzong of the Tang shunned idle pleasures and applied himself energetically to affairs of government. He, too, may be said to have devoted his heart to revering Heaven and laboring for the people; thus the good government of the Kaiyuan era was attained. Renzong of the Song stood in the open when he heard thunder, prayed at night within the palace, rejected offerings of auspicious marvels, and practiced frugality. He, too, may be called one who revered Heaven and labored for the people. Thus the enduring survival of the dynasty ultimately depended upon him. Such rulers, although they did not equal the founders of dynasties, may nevertheless be counted among those who preserved an established inheritance …

title: 嘉靖二十九年進士登科錄
text:
令主矣蓋自古帝王真有見於天道雖遠而
實邇民心雖愚而至神故於天而敬之神明
其德一內聖之心法也於民而勤之恪恭厥
政一外王之治法也然敬非倖福於天所以
盡已之心爾人君之心天下仰之以為天者
喜怒之形即天道慘舒之運仁義之用即天
道生殺之權一毫不敢或有不能順天之命
者故盡已之心即所以敬天也勤非要譽於
民所以推已之心爾人君之心天下倚之以
為治者勞逸不同四海之安危係之勤惰不
===
同天下之休戚因之一息少懈或有不能奠
民之生者故推已之心即所以勤民也苟不
求敬於心而徒減膳徹樂素服避殿從事封
禪者豈所以為敬天之孝哉觀於昭于天之
詩而敬天之道不能外矣苟不求勤于心而
徒衡石程書衛士傳餐下行尚書事者豈所
以為勤民之仁哉觀所其無逸之書而勤民
之道不能外矣仰惟我
太祖高皇帝有見於此故于草創之始恒諭羣雄
曰毋違天毋虐民其得天下之初已知二者

令主矣。蓋自古帝王，真有見於天道雖遠而實邇，民心雖愚而至神，故於天而敬之，神明其德，一內聖之心法也；於民而勤之，恪恭厥政，一外王之治法也。然敬非倖福於天，所以盡已之心爾。人君之心，天下仰之以為天者，喜怒之形，即天道慘舒之運；仁義之用，即天道生殺之權。一毫不敢，或有不能順天之命者，故盡已之心，即所以敬天也。勤非要譽於民，所以推已之心爾。人君之心，天下倚之以為治者，勞逸不同，四海之安危係之；勤惰不同，天下之休戚因之。一息少懈，或有不能奠民之生者，故推已之心，即所以勤民也。苟不求敬於心，而徒減膳徹樂、素服避殿、從事封禪者，豈所以為敬天之孝哉？觀於「昭于天」之詩，而敬天之道不能外矣。苟不求勤于心，而徒衡石程書、衛士傳餐、下行尚書事者，豈所以為勤民之仁哉？觀「所其無逸」之書，而勤民之道不能外矣。
仰惟我太祖高皇帝有見於此，故于草創之始，恒諭羣雄曰：「毋違天，毋虐民。」其得天下之初，已知二者

…worthy rulers who preserved the achievements of their predecessors. From antiquity, emperors and kings truly understood that although the Way of Heaven is distant, it is in fact near, and that although the people's hearts are simple, they possess the utmost spiritual discernment. Thus, revering Heaven and making their virtue spiritually luminous constitute the discipline of the mind for inward sagehood; diligently serving the people and administering government with reverent care constitute the method of government for outward kingship. Yet reverence is not a means of seeking blessings from Heaven: it is simply how one fully realizes one's own heart. The ruler's heart is what all under Heaven look up to as Heaven itself. His expressions of joy and anger are the workings of severity and gentleness in the Way of Heaven; his exercise of benevolence and righteousness is its authority to give life and bring death. He dares not lapse in the slightest, lest he fail to follow Heaven's mandate. Thus, fully realizing his own heart is precisely how he reveres Heaven. Diligence is not a means of seeking praise from the people: it is simply how one extends one's own heart to others. The ruler's heart is what all under Heaven rely upon for good government. Whether he labors or takes his ease determines the security or peril of all within the Four Seas; whether he is diligent or indolent determines the well-being or suffering of all under Heaven. If he relaxes his efforts even for a moment, he may fail to secure the people's livelihood. Thus, extending his own heart to others is precisely how he diligently serves the people. If he does not seek reverence within his heart, but merely reduces his meals, suspends music, wears plain garments, withdraws from the main hall, and undertakes the feng and shan sacrifices, how can this constitute the filial devotion of revering Heaven? Consider the poem containing the words “illustrious in Heaven”: the way of revering Heaven cannot extend beyond its teaching. If he does not seek diligence within his heart, but merely weighs documents to set his daily quota, has guards pass in his meals, and lowers himself to perform the duties of a Master of Writing, how can this constitute the benevolence of diligently serving the people? Consider the passage in the Book of Documents that enjoins one to “make one's abode in freedom from ease”: the way of diligently serving the people cannot extend beyond its teaching.

text:
為天下之大端觀其與博士許存仁講洪範
曰天道微妙難知人事感通易見君能脩德
則七政順度雨暘應期災害不生不能脩德
則三辰失行旱潦不時災異迭見又期之以
上下交脩斯為格天之本其敬天何如也至
于欽天有監
大祀有文精誠之錄存心之篇凡所以極其誠敬
以對越
上帝者真能體乾父坤母之心無忝于宗子之責
者矣又曰得天下者得民心也老者民之父
===
母幼者民之子弟恤其老則天下之為子弟
者悅恤其幼則天下之為父母者悅老幼咸
悅其心其不歸者寡矣繼又云今日之務此
最為先宜速行之其勤民何如也至于
恤民有諭寬租有詔勸耕而躬禱雨而露凡所
以竭其仁愛以勤恤民隱者真能擴民胞物
與之念無歉于父母之任者矣是誠見於
上帝之眷根于廼心下民之懷本于有德故
貽謀之善
垂訓之勤合千古帝王而一之

為天下之大端。觀其與博士許存仁講《洪範》，曰：「天道微妙難知，人事感通易見。君能脩德，則七政順度，雨暘應期，災害不生；不能脩德，則三辰失行，旱潦不時，災異迭見。」又期之以上下交脩，斯為格天之本，其敬天何如也！至于欽天有監，大祀有文，精誠之錄，存心之篇，凡所以極其誠敬以對越上帝者，真能體乾父坤母之心，無忝于宗子之責者矣。
又曰：「得天下者，得民心也。老者，民之父母；幼者，民之子弟。恤其老，則天下之為子弟者悅；恤其幼，則天下之為父母者悅。老幼咸悅，其心其不歸者寡矣。」繼又云：「今日之務，此最為先，宜速行之。」其勤民何如也！至于恤民有諭，寬租有詔，勸耕而躬，禱雨而露，凡所以竭其仁愛以勤恤民隱者，真能擴民胞物與之念，無歉于父母之任者矣。是誠見於上帝之眷根于廼心，下民之懷本于有德，故貽謀之善，垂訓之勤，合千古帝王而一之。
translation_en:
…were the great essentials of governing the realm. Consider how, when discussing the “Great Plan” (Hongfan) with the Erudite Xu Cunren, he said: “The Way of Heaven is subtle and difficult to know; its response to human affairs is readily apparent. If the ruler cultivates virtue, the seven celestial regulators follow their proper courses, rain and sunshine arrive in season, and calamities do not arise. If he fails to cultivate virtue, the three celestial luminaries stray from their courses, droughts and floods occur out of season, and calamities and anomalies appear one after another.” He further urged mutual cultivation by those above and below as the foundation for moving Heaven. How great was his reverence for Heaven! Moreover, he established the Directorate of Astronomy to show reverence for Heaven and composed texts for the great sacrifices, along with records of utmost sincerity and writings on preserving the mind. In all these means of bringing his sincerity and reverence to the utmost in serving the Lord on High, he truly embodied the understanding that Heaven is father and Earth is mother, and brought no dishonor upon his responsibility as their principal heir.
He also said: “To gain the realm is to gain the hearts of the people. The elderly are the people’s fathers and mothers; the young are their sons and younger brothers. Care for the elderly, and all the sons and younger brothers in the realm will rejoice; care for the young, and all the fathers and mothers in the realm will rejoice. When old and young alike rejoice, few will fail to give their allegiance.” He then added: “Among today’s tasks, this takes precedence over all others; it should be carried out promptly.” How diligent was his care for the people! Moreover, he issued instructions for relieving the people and edicts for reducing land taxes; he personally encouraged cultivation and exposed himself to the elements when praying for rain [?]. In all these means of exhausting his benevolence and love in diligently attending to the people’s hidden sufferings, he truly extended the conviction that the people are his siblings and all things his companions, fully discharging his responsibility as their parent. He truly understood that the favor of the Lord on High is rooted in one’s own heart, and that the allegiance of the people below rests upon possessing virtue. Thus, in the excellence of the plans he bequeathed and the diligence with which he handed down instruction, he united in himself the virtues of the emperors and kings of all ages.

title: 嘉靖二十九年進士登科錄
text:
列聖相承莫不體其心而效其法敬其所尊事天
以盡孝也愛其所親治民以盡仁也是以天
眷隆而民志定重熈累洽之治深仁厚澤之
化遠而不禦久而彌彰
太祖肇造之心開先之德至今益有以擴而大之
培而厚之濬而深之矣逮我
陛下繼帝王
祖宗之統為
天地民物之主所以奉
天子民者無所不用其誠定
===
郊祀之典脩農桑之政
欽天有記慰民有詔至于齋戒祗畏之心寬宥勤
恤之治不能悉舉天下咸囿于
陛下之仁咸感于
陛下之孝而不自知矣
聖制則曰朕寅奉
上玄欽若天道凡惠恤計安乎斯民者未嘗少懈
其念此
陛下之所自信亦天下之所仰戴而嚮應者也由
是荷

陛下之所自信亦天下之所仰戴而嚮應者也由
是筍
punctuated:
列聖相承，莫不體其心而效其法，敬其所尊，事天以盡孝也；愛其所親，治民以盡仁也。是以天眷隆而民志定，重熈累洽之治、深仁厚澤之化，遠而不禦，久而彌彰。太祖肇造之心、開先之德，至今益有以擴而大之，培而厚之，濬而深之矣。
逮我陛下繼帝王祖宗之統，為天地民物之主，所以奉天子民者，無所不用其誠。定郊祀之典，脩農桑之政，欽天有記，慰民有詔。至于齋戒祗畏之心、寬宥勤恤之治，不能悉舉。天下咸囿于陛下之仁，咸感于陛下之孝，而不自知矣。
聖制則曰：「朕寅奉上玄，欽若天道，凡惠恤計安乎斯民者，未嘗少懈其念。」此陛下之所自信，亦天下之所仰戴而嚮應者也。由是荷
translation_en:
The successive sage emperors all embodied his intentions and emulated his methods. Revering what he revered, they served Heaven to fulfill their filial devotion; loving those he held dear, they governed the people to fulfill their benevolence. Thus Heaven’s favor abounded and the people’s hearts were settled. Their government, marked by successive ages of prosperity and peace, and their transforming influence, marked by profound benevolence and generous beneficence, reached far without obstruction and grew ever more manifest with time. Taizu’s founding intentions and pioneering virtue have, down to the present, been further extended and enlarged, cultivated and strengthened, dredged and deepened.
Now Your Majesty has inherited the succession of the emperors and royal ancestors and become sovereign over all people and things between Heaven and Earth. In serving Heaven and nurturing the people as your children, you employ the utmost sincerity in everything. You have established the rites of the suburban sacrifices and improved the administration of agriculture and sericulture. There is a written record of your reverence for Heaven and an edict comforting the people. As for your disposition toward ritual fasting, purification, reverence, and awe, and your government’s clemency and diligent care, these cannot all be enumerated. All under Heaven dwell within Your Majesty’s benevolence and are moved by Your Majesty’s filial devotion, without even being conscious of it.
The Emperor’s decree reads: “I reverently serve Heaven on high and respectfully follow the Way of Heaven. In all matters concerning kindness and relief for these people and plans for their security, I have never relaxed my concern in the slightest.” This is what Your Majesty knows with confidence about yourself, and also what all under Heaven look up to, uphold, and respond to. Thus, receiving …

title: 嘉靖二十九年進士登科錄
text:
□下參贊之誠稽宰輔調燮之功比年以来嘉祥
屢臻天不愛道而卿雲甘露降于上地不愛
寶而河清醴泉見於下凡諸福之物可致之
祥莫不畢至不可以厯紀者故方內見其乂
安矣綱舉目張文治隆而武備脩德盛化神
天地位而萬物育海宇翕然丕冒於休養生
息之中沾濡乎二帝三王之澤矣敬天勤民
之脩而天人交感之效其不可誣有如此者
欽惟
陛下以孝治天下而維則之思四方效之故所以
===
===
事
天者真有如事親者矣
陛下以仁育天下而恫瘝之念萬民賴之故所以
體民者真有如愛子者矣是故天之祐助宜
無不至民之懷保宜無不周焉夫何邇年以
来水旱相仍饉荒不免而南北之鄙苗狄未
靖太平極盛之時亦有流離無告之民王化
大行之際間有滲漏未洽之地民生未遂治
化未孚誠有如
聖問之所及

之餘而天人交感之效其不可誣有如此者
欽惟
陛下以孝治天下而維則之思四方效之故所以
===
事

陛下以仁育天下而恫瘝之念萬民賴之故所以
體民者真有如愛子者矣是故天之祐助宜
無不至民之懷保宜無不周焉夫何邇年以

靖太平極盛之時亦有流離無告之民王化
大行之際間有滲漏未洽之地民生未遂治
化未孚誠有如
聖問之所及
punctuated:
□下參贊之誠，稽宰輔調燮之功，比年以来，嘉祥屢臻。天不愛道，而卿雲甘露降于上；地不愛寶，而河清醴泉見於下。凡諸福之物、可致之祥，莫不畢至，不可以厯紀者。故方內見其乂安矣，綱舉目張，文治隆而武備脩，德盛化神，天地位而萬物育。海宇翕然，丕冒於休養生息之中，沾濡乎二帝三王之澤矣。敬天勤民之脩，而天人交感之效，其不可誣有如此者。
欽惟陛下以孝治天下，而維則之思，四方效之，故所以事天者，真有如事親者矣。陛下以仁育天下，而恫瘝之念，萬民賴之，故所以體民者，真有如愛子者矣。是故天之祐助，宜無不至；民之懷保，宜無不周焉。夫何邇年以来，水旱相仍，饉荒不免，而南北之鄙，苗狄未靖？太平極盛之時，亦有流離無告之民；王化大行之際，間有滲漏未洽之地。民生未遂，治化未孚，誠有如聖問之所及
translation_en:
…Your Majesty’s [?] sincerity in assisting the transforming and nourishing work of Heaven and Earth, and considering the achievements of the chief ministers in harmonizing their forces, auspicious signs have repeatedly appeared in recent years. Heaven does not withhold its Way [?], and auspicious clouds and sweet dew descend from above; Earth does not withhold its treasures, and the Yellow River runs clear and springs of sweet water appear below. Every object betokening good fortune and every auspicious sign that can be called forth has arrived, too numerous to record individually. Thus all within the realm enjoys order and peace. With the main cord raised, every mesh of the net opens: civil governance flourishes and military preparations are maintained. Virtue abounds and its transforming influence is wondrous; Heaven and Earth occupy their proper places, and all things flourish. The whole realm, united in harmony, enjoys ample respite and the opportunity to sustain and replenish its people, steeped in blessings like those bestowed by the Two Emperors and Three Kings. Such are the undeniable results of cultivating reverence for Heaven and diligence toward the people, and of the mutual response between Heaven and humankind.
I respectfully consider that Your Majesty governs all under Heaven through filial piety, and the four quarters emulate your resolve to provide a model. Thus your service to Heaven truly resembles service to your parents. Your Majesty nurtures all under Heaven through benevolence, and the myriad people depend upon your concern for their suffering. Thus your sympathetic care for the people truly resembles love for your children. Accordingly, Heaven’s assistance should reach everywhere, and your cherishing and protection of the people should embrace everyone. Why, then, have floods and droughts followed one another in recent years, with famine unavoidable, while the Miao and Di on the southern and northern frontiers remain unpacified? Even at the height of peace and prosperity, there are people displaced and wandering, with no one to whom they can appeal; even as kingly transformation spreads widely, there are places it has missed, where its influence has not fully penetrated. The people’s livelihoods remain unfulfilled, and the transforming influence of government has yet to win their confidence, just as Your Majesty’s august question has indicated…

title: 嘉靖二十九年進士登科錄
text:
聖心之所憂者也雖然仁孝克全而無慊于心天
人協應而不違乎理則
陛下亦自盡乎道自信諸心而已矣至於九年之
水七年之旱有苗之未格獫狁之未靖黎民
之阻饑博施濟衆之猶病雖二帝三王之盛
亦所不免爾又何足為
聖德王業之累哉
聖制則曰豈朕誠之有未盡者是則
陛下求諸巳而不求諸外貴以實而不貴以文之
盛心也盖惟天聰明本不容偽民心至靈亦
===
不可欺果能誠于敬
天而肅雝之念無間于宮廟戒懼之功無異於隱
顯不徒為祗畏之彌文而已誠于勤民而竭
精研慮無忽於心宵衣旰食不怠於政不徒
為勤恤之徒說而已則天必久而自定民必
久而自安又何必望助於近責效於速哉至
於任事之臣親民之吏不能體
陛下勤恤之心而玩愒貪殘罔以斯民為念者間
亦有之誠不能逃
陛下天縱之聰者夫辨臧否慎黜陟崇教化廣儲

陛下天縱之聰者夫辯誠否慎黜陟崇教化廣儲
punctuated:
聖心之所憂者也。雖然，仁孝克全而無慊于心，天人協應而不違乎理，則陛下亦自盡乎道、自信諸心而已矣。至於九年之水、七年之旱、有苗之未格、獫狁之未靖、黎民之阻饑、博施濟衆之猶病，雖二帝三王之盛，亦所不免爾，又何足為聖德王業之累哉？
聖制則曰：「豈朕誠之有未盡者？」是則陛下求諸巳而不求諸外，貴以實而不貴以文之盛心也。盖惟天聰明，本不容偽；民心至靈，亦不可欺。果能誠于敬天，而肅雝之念無間于宮廟，戒懼之功無異於隱顯，不徒為祗畏之彌文而已；誠于勤民，而竭精研慮，無忽於心，宵衣旰食，不怠於政，不徒為勤恤之徒說而已；則天必久而自定，民必久而自安，又何必望助於近、責效於速哉？至於任事之臣、親民之吏，不能體陛下勤恤之心，而玩愒貪殘，罔以斯民為念者，間亦有之，誠不能逃陛下天縱之聰者。夫辨臧否、慎黜陟、崇教化、廣儲
translation_en:
…and are matters that trouble Your Majesty’s sagely heart. Nevertheless, if benevolence and filial piety are fully realized, leaving no dissatisfaction in your heart, and Heaven and humanity respond in harmony without departing from principle, Your Majesty need only fulfill the Way to the utmost and remain confident in your own heart. As for the nine years of flooding, the seven years of drought, the Youmiao’s failure to submit, the Xianyun’s remaining unpacified, the common people’s suffering from hunger, and the difficulty even sages found in bestowing benefits widely and bringing relief to all—even the flourishing reigns of the Two Emperors and Three Kings could not avoid these things. How, then, could they detract from your sagely virtue and royal achievement?
The Emperor’s decree reads: “Could there be some respect in which my sincerity has not been fully realized?” This expresses Your Majesty’s noble resolve to seek the cause within yourself rather than outside, and to value substance rather than outward form. Heaven’s keen perception admits no falsehood; the people’s hearts are supremely discerning and likewise cannot be deceived. If you are truly sincere in revering Heaven, maintaining an unbroken spirit of solemn harmony in the palace and ancestral temples, exercising the same vigilance and apprehension in private as in public, rather than merely multiplying formal displays of reverence and awe; and if you are sincere in laboring for the people, exhausting your energies in careful deliberation without any inward negligence, dressing before dawn and eating late, remaining tireless in government rather than merely uttering empty words about diligence and compassion—then Heaven will assuredly become settled in time, and the people will assuredly find peace in time. Why, then, must you expect assistance in the near term or demand swift results? As for ministers entrusted with affairs and officials who govern the people directly, there are indeed some who fail to embody Your Majesty’s diligent and compassionate concern, but instead idle away their time, behave greedily and cruelly, and give no thought to the people. They surely cannot escape Your Majesty’s Heaven-endowed discernment. Now, distinguishing the worthy from the unworthy, exercising care in demotions and promotions, promoting moral instruction, and expanding reserves…

title: 嘉靖二十九年進士登科錄
text:
蓄脩兵刑奠萬物者六卿之職也必德足以
稱位如禹稷夔龍之徒斯可矣協謀慮立威
信除戎器勤訓練精竒正慎攻守者將帥之
職也必才足以集事如吉甫方叔之輩斯可
也貞僚肅度明目達聰闢賢路通民情者臺
諫之職也其敢言直諫能如漢之汲黯唐之
魏徵斯可也均財賦清刑獄植斯民之命定
天下之平者藩臬之職也果能承流宣化激
濁揚清否乎善催科勤撫字保乂元元安集
邦本者守令之職也果能政平訟理吏稱民
===
安否乎或兼理庶務之煩或分牧兆民之眾
能效法乎先哲宣布乎
德意者固未嘗乏才但任之者眾不必盡忠且
賢矣稱恬靜者虛度歲月無所建立於時稱
練達者貪婪自用罔知盡心於國有弗畏於
天弗念於民戾乎
憲章違乎官箴者是則臣工之罪亦君上所當
慎簡任而嚴罰黜者也天命難諶民心罔常
抑可不為之所乎
聖制又曰朕欲俾休徵時若邊警不聞百工允釐

蓄、脩兵刑、奠萬物者，六卿之職也。必德足以稱位，如禹、稷、夔、龍之徒，斯可矣。協謀慮、立威信、除戎器、勤訓練、精竒正、慎攻守者，將帥之職也。必才足以集事，如吉甫、方叔之輩，斯可也。貞僚肅度、明目達聰、闢賢路、通民情者，臺諫之職也。其敢言直諫，能如漢之汲黯、唐之魏徵，斯可也。均財賦、清刑獄、植斯民之命、定天下之平者，藩臬之職也。果能承流宣化、激濁揚清否乎？善催科、勤撫字、保乂元元、安集邦本者，守令之職也。果能政平訟理、吏稱民安否乎？或兼理庶務之煩，或分牧兆民之眾，能效法乎先哲、宣布乎德意者，固未嘗乏才。但任之者眾，不必盡忠且賢矣。稱恬靜者，虛度歲月，無所建立於時；稱練達者，貪婪自用，罔知盡心於國。有弗畏於天、弗念於民、戾乎憲章、違乎官箴者，是則臣工之罪，亦君上所當慎簡任而嚴罰黜者也。天命難諶，民心罔常，抑可不為之所乎？
聖制又曰：「朕欲俾休徵時若，邊警不聞，百工允釐……」
translation_en:
…reserves, attending to military affairs and punishments, and securing all things—these are the duties of the Six Ministers. Their virtue must suffice for their positions: men such as Yu, Ji, Kui, and Long will meet this requirement. Coordinating plans, establishing authority and trust, putting weapons in order, diligently conducting training, mastering unconventional and conventional tactics, and exercising care in attack and defense—these are the duties of commanders. Their abilities must suffice to accomplish their tasks: men such as Jifu and Fang Shu will meet this requirement. Rectifying their colleagues and enforcing standards, ensuring that the ruler sees clearly and hears fully, opening avenues for worthy men, and communicating the people's circumstances—these are the duties of censorial and remonstrance officials. They must dare to speak and remonstrate frankly, like Ji An of the Han and Wei Zheng of the Tang. Equalizing revenues and levies, ensuring justice in penal cases, sustaining the people's lives, and establishing peace throughout the realm—these are the duties of Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissioners. Can they truly carry forward imperial influence and spread its transforming effects, curb the corrupt, and promote the upright? Managing tax collection well, diligently nurturing the people, protecting and governing the common folk, and bringing security and stability to the foundation of the state—these are the duties of prefects and magistrates. Can they truly administer equitably and settle lawsuits properly, so that officials discharge their duties creditably and the people live in peace? Whether charged with overseeing the complexities of numerous affairs or assigned to govern a portion of the vast populace, there has certainly been no lack of capable men who can emulate the sages of old and promulgate Your Majesty's benevolent intentions. Yet those appointed are many, and they are not necessarily all loyal and worthy. Those praised as tranquil and restrained idly let the years pass, accomplishing nothing in their time; those praised as experienced and capable are greedy and self-willed, never thinking to devote themselves fully to the state. Some neither fear Heaven nor care for the people, contravening established statutes and violating the precepts of office. These are the faults of the officials, but they are also matters requiring the sovereign to select and appoint carefully, and to punish and dismiss rigorously. Heaven's mandate is difficult to rely upon, and the people's allegiance is not constant. Can one possibly fail to make provision for this?
The Emperor's decree further reads: “I wish to bring about the timely appearance of auspicious signs, to hear no alarms from the frontiers, and to have all officials faithfully discharge their responsibilities…”

title: 嘉靖二十九年進士登科錄
text:
庶績咸熈不令一夫失其所朕志也是志也善
繼
天之志者也善繼
祖之志者也果能實有是心而言行相顧父於其
道而始終不渝必欲先天而不違後天而奉
時而孝之存乎心者純通天下為一家合中
國為一人而仁之及于物者溥殆見和氣致
祥休徵無不應也公孫弘所謂心和則氣和
氣和則形和形和則天地之和應之者是矣
内治既脩邊警自不聞也朱熹所謂其本不
===
在威強而在德業其任不在邊境而在朝廷
其具不在兵食而在紀綱者是也統治於上
者奉天子民盡其心則輔治於下者愛君憂
國殫其慮百工無不允釐也庶績無不咸熈
也董仲舒所謂正心以正朝廷正朝廷以正
百官正百官以正萬民遠近莫不一于正者
是也自古謀國之臣其言莫不本於人君之
心人君之心果能本之學而益加涵養之功
求之人而益弘維持之助懋精一之訓以培
道心之微體綏猷之義以全所降之衷本皇

translation_en:
…that all undertakings flourish, and that not a single person be deprived of his proper place: this is my aspiration.” This aspiration worthily continues the will of Heaven and worthily continues the will of the ancestors. If Your Majesty can truly hold this intention, make your words and deeds accord, adhere to the Way [?], and remain constant from beginning to end, you will surely seek, when acting before Heaven, not to contravene it, and, when acting after Heaven, to follow its seasons. Thus the filial devotion within your heart will be pure. You will unite all under Heaven as one family and bring the Central Kingdom together as one person, so that your benevolence extends broadly to all beings. Then we may expect harmonious vital energies to bring auspicious blessings, with every favorable portent appearing in response. This is what Gongsun Hong meant when he said: “When the heart is harmonious, the vital energies are harmonious; when the vital energies are harmonious, the bodily form is harmonious; when the bodily form is harmonious, the harmony of Heaven and Earth responds to it.” Once internal government is well ordered, alarms from the frontiers will naturally cease to be heard. This is what Zhu Xi meant when he said: “Its foundation lies not in coercive strength but in virtuous achievement; responsibility for it lies not at the frontiers but at court; its instruments lie not in troops and provisions but in governing principles and discipline.” If the ruler above serves Heaven, treats the people as his children, and devotes his whole heart to this, those assisting government below will love their sovereign, be concerned for the state, and devote their utmost thought to their duties. All officials will properly discharge their responsibilities, and all undertakings will flourish. This is what Dong Zhongshu meant when he said: “Rectify the heart in order to rectify the court; rectify the court in order to rectify the hundred officials; rectify the hundred officials in order to rectify the myriad people. Near and far, none will fail to be united in rectitude.”

Since antiquity, ministers who have deliberated on affairs of state have invariably grounded their counsel in the ruler’s heart. If the ruler can truly ground his heart in learning and further strengthen the work of nurturing it; seek support from others and further enlarge the assistance that sustains it; diligently uphold the injunction to be discerning and single-minded, thereby nurturing the subtle moral mind; embody the meaning of bringing peace through the Way, thereby preserving intact the inner nature bestowed by Heaven; and take as his foundation the August…

title: 嘉靖二十九年進士登科錄
text:
極之訓於洪範而不流於偏陂求敬義之教
於丹書而不溺於怠欲則吾之一心上有以
孚於天下有以通於民矣治天下之道謂不
在于是耶臣願
陛下之於事天也念付寄之重為永命之圖求其
端而不忽順其命而不違辨災眚禎祥之異
而致脩省之功妙弛張緩急之宜以時順承
之道出入起居莫非天理動靜語默罔非天
則由是天鑒其誠保祐益至矣外此而有所
謂敬者非敬也
===
陛下之於治民也念萬幾之難總四海之難一西
北之民憊於力役則思所以逸之東南之民
竭於征求則思所以蘇之又必慎循良之選
以廣其惠汰貪酷之吏以去其害則民得其
所感仰益深矣外此而有所謂勤者非勤也
是敬天勤民之道皆不必外有所慕亦惟求
之此心而已然有外之心不足以合天心必
求合乎天心然後謂之孝有我之心不足以
當民心必求當乎民心然後謂之仁是故天
命有善而無惡人心好善而惡惡能培吾心

punctuated:
極之訓於洪範，而不流於偏陂；求敬義之教於丹書，而不溺於怠欲，則吾之一心，上有以孚於天，下有以通於民矣。治天下之道，謂不在于是耶？臣願陛下之於事天也，念付寄之重，為永命之圖，求其端而不忽，順其命而不違，辨災眚禎祥之異而致脩省之功，妙弛張緩急之宜以時順承之道。出入起居，莫非天理；動靜語默，罔非天則。由是天鑒其誠，保祐益至矣。外此而有所謂敬者，非敬也。
陛下之於治民也，念萬幾之難總、四海之難一。西北之民憊於力役，則思所以逸之；東南之民竭於征求，則思所以蘇之。又必慎循良之選，以廣其惠；汰貪酷之吏，以去其害。則民得其所，感仰益深矣。外此而有所謂勤者，非勤也。是敬天勤民之道，皆不必外有所慕，亦惟求之此心而已。然有外之心，不足以合天心，必求合乎天心，然後謂之孝；有我之心，不足以當民心，必求當乎民心，然後謂之仁。是故天命有善而無惡，人心好善而惡惡。能培吾心
translation_en:
…ground oneself in the teaching of the Sovereign Ultimate in the Great Plan, without straying into partiality; seek the teaching of reverence and righteousness in the Cinnabar Writing, without sinking into indolence and desire. Then this single heart of mine can win Heaven’s trust above and communicate with the people below. Can it be said that the way to govern all under Heaven does not lie here? Your servant wishes that Your Majesty, in serving Heaven, would remember the weight of the charge entrusted to you and plan to perpetuate the mandate: seek its beginnings without neglect, obey its commands without deviation, distinguish the significance of calamities and misfortunes from auspicious signs, and devote yourself fully to self-cultivation and examination. Judge with subtle discernment when to relax or tighten, when to proceed slowly or urgently, so as to accord with Heaven at the proper time. In going out and coming in, rising and resting, let nothing depart from heavenly principle; in movement and stillness, speech and silence, let nothing depart from Heaven’s rule. Heaven will then perceive your sincerity, and its protection and aid will become ever more abundant. Anything called reverence apart from this is no true reverence.
In governing the people, may Your Majesty remember how difficult it is to oversee the myriad affairs of state and to unite all within the Four Seas. When the people of the northwest are exhausted by labor service, consider how to give them respite; when the people of the southeast are drained by levies and exactions, consider how to revive their livelihoods. You must also carefully select upright and capable officials to extend your beneficence, and dismiss corrupt and cruel officials to remove the harm they cause. The people will then find their proper place, and their gratitude and admiration will deepen. Anything called diligence apart from this is no true diligence. Thus, the way to revere Heaven and labor diligently for the people requires no pursuit of anything external; it need only be sought within this heart. Yet a heart turned toward external things cannot accord with Heaven’s heart. Only when one seeks accord with Heaven’s heart can this be called filial piety. A heart preoccupied with oneself cannot answer to the people’s hearts. Only when one seeks to answer to the people’s hearts can this be called benevolence. Thus Heaven’s mandate contains goodness and no evil, while the human heart loves goodness and hates evil. If I can nurture my heart’s…

title: 嘉靖二十九年進士登科錄
text:
之善以来天下之善抑吾心之惡以止天下
之惡則所謂踐形惟肖者是矣易曰君子以
遏惡揚善順天休命其善事天者與天下有
不同之人而無不同之情果能公吾心之好
以遂天下之好公吾心之惡以遂天下之惡
則所謂父母孔邇者是矣傳曰民之所好好
之民之所惡惡之此之謂民之父母其善體
民之謂與然天人一理也仁孝一道也民心
得則天心亦無不得拂乎民則天亦因之書
曰天聰明自我民聰明天明畏自我民明威
===
達於上下敬哉有土可見民心所存即天理
之所在而吾心之敬又合天人而一之也是
天雖逺也吾心則近也民雖衆也吾心則約
也由近以達之逺守約以該乎博則天意回
而民困日紓民生遂而天眷自隆上下交感
之幾天人會合之理自不期而同者但不知
陛下之敬
天勤民果能極其誠而無一念之不誠否也竊聞
成湯嘗謂侍臣曰一夫有怨豈得謂仁一念不誠
豈能格天知用心之密如此則仁孝之道庶

punctuated: 之善以来天下之善，抑吾心之惡以止天下之惡，則所謂踐形惟肖者是矣。《易》曰：「君子以遏惡揚善，順天休命。」其善事天者與！天下有不同之人，而無不同之情。果能公吾心之好，以遂天下之好，公吾心之惡，以遂天下之惡，則所謂父母孔邇者是矣。傳曰：「民之所好好之，民之所惡惡之，此之謂民之父母。」其善體民之謂與！然天人一理也，仁孝一道也。民心得則天心亦無不得，拂乎民則天亦因之。《書》曰：「天聰明，自我民聰明；天明畏，自我民明威。達於上下，敬哉有土！」可見民心所存，即天理之所在，而吾心之敬又合天人而一之也。是天雖逺也，吾心則近也；民雖衆也，吾心則約也。由近以達之逺，守約以該乎博，則天意回而民困日紓，民生遂而天眷自隆。上下交感之幾，天人會合之理，自不期而同者。但不知陛下之敬天勤民，果能極其誠而無一念之不誠否也？竊聞成湯嘗謂侍臣曰：「一夫有怨，豈得謂仁？一念不誠，豈能格天？」知用心之密如此，則仁孝之道庶
translation_en:
…the goodness in my own heart so as to draw forth the goodness of all under Heaven, and suppress the evil in my own heart so as to halt the evil of all under Heaven: this is what is meant by fulfilling one’s bodily endowment and truly resembling Heaven. The Book of Changes says: “The gentleman curbs evil and promotes good, complying with Heaven’s beneficent mandate.” Is this not serving Heaven well? People throughout the world differ, yet their feelings do not differ. If I can truly make the likes of my own heart impartial, thereby fulfilling the likes of all under Heaven, and make the dislikes of my own heart impartial, thereby fulfilling the dislikes of all under Heaven, this is what is meant by being parents who are very near. The Commentary says: “To like what the people like and dislike what the people dislike: this is called being the parents of the people.” Does this not mean understanding the people well?

Yet Heaven and humanity share one principle, and benevolence and filial piety share one Way. If the people’s hearts are won, Heaven’s heart cannot fail to be won as well; if the people are affronted, Heaven responds accordingly. The Book of Documents says: “Heaven’s hearing and sight derive from the hearing and sight of our people; Heaven’s manifest awe derives from the manifest authority of our people. This reaches above and below. Be reverent, you who possess territory!” We can thus see that where the people’s hearts abide is precisely where Heaven’s principle resides, while the reverence in my own heart unites Heaven and humanity as one. Thus, although Heaven is distant, my own heart is near; although the people are many, my own heart offers a single focus. By proceeding from the near to reach the distant, and holding to the essential to encompass the vast, Heaven’s disposition will turn favorably and the people’s distress will ease daily; the people’s livelihood will flourish and Heaven’s favor will naturally grow abundant. The subtle workings of mutual response between above and below, and the principle by which Heaven and humanity come together, will spontaneously accord. Yet I do not know whether Your Majesty, in revering Heaven and diligently caring for the people, can indeed bring sincerity to its utmost, without a single insincere thought.

I have humbly heard that Cheng Tang once said to his attendant ministers: “If even one man has a grievance, how can I be called benevolent? If even one thought is insincere, how can I move Heaven?” If one understands that the application of the heart must be so meticulous, then the Way of benevolence and filial piety may be approached …

title: 嘉靖二十九年進士登科錄
text:
之而配乎天地溥之而橫乎四海天下不足
治矣又何帝王之治之不可及哉雖然有敬
天之心不可無憲天之治有愛民之念不可
無法祖之行故臯陶告舜曰人代傅說告高
宗曰時憲臣之望君未嘗不欲其求端於天
也伊尹之告太甲曰率攸行周公之告成王
曰脩厥德君臣之際未嘗不欲其無違乎祖
也夫天道不言莫非至教至德之施祖訓無
愆要皆盡倫盡制之道臣願
陛下體元居正法其自然之運善繼善述守其不
===
易之則
天之所以望我者何如而所以事
天者必有以慰之矣
祖宗之所以貽我者何如而所以法

易之則
天之所以望我者何如而所以事
天者必有以慰之矣
祖宗之所以貽我者何如而所以法
祖者必有以成之矣欲盡其道以臻致治之盛
有踰于此者哉敬孝所以事天亦所以法祖
仁所以勤民亦所以法天一以貫之皆本乎
心者也
陛下纘敵一之學成中興之治四海之永寧萬民
之咸服合二十九年如一日者然猶下詢□□
punctuated:
之而配乎天地，溥之而橫乎四海，天下不足治矣，又何帝王之治之不可及哉？雖然，有敬天之心，不可無憲天之治；有愛民之念，不可無法祖之行。故臯陶告舜曰：「人代。」傅說告高宗曰：「時憲。」臣之望君，未嘗不欲其求端於天也。伊尹之告太甲曰：「率攸行。」周公之告成王曰：「脩厥德。」君臣之際，未嘗不欲其無違乎祖也。夫天道不言，莫非至教至德之施；祖訓無愆，要皆盡倫盡制之道。臣願陛下體元居正，法其自然之運；善繼善述，守其不易之則。天之所以望我者何如，而所以事天者必有以慰之矣；祖宗之所以貽我者何如，而所以法祖者必有以成之矣。欲盡其道，以臻致治之盛，孰有踰于此者哉？故孝所以事天，亦所以法祖；仁所以勤民，亦所以法天。一以貫之，皆本于心者也。
陛下擴敬一之學，成中興之治，四海之永寧，萬民之咸服，合二十九年如一日者。然猶下詢蒭
translation_en:
…and bring it into accord with Heaven and Earth, spreading it across the Four Seas: governing All under Heaven would present no difficulty. How, then, could the government of the ancient emperors and kings be beyond reach? Nevertheless, a heart that reveres Heaven must be accompanied by government that takes Heaven as its model; concern that cherishes the people must be accompanied by conduct that follows the ancestors. Thus Gao Yao told Shun, “Human beings act on Heaven’s behalf,” and Fu Yue told Gaozong, “Take this as your model.” In their expectations of their rulers, ministers have always wished them to seek their guiding principle in Heaven. Yi Yin told Tai Jia, “Follow the course he pursued,” and the Duke of Zhou told King Cheng, “Cultivate his virtue.” In relations between ruler and minister, the wish has always been that the ruler should not depart from his ancestors’ example. Heaven’s Way does not speak, yet everything it does manifests the highest teaching and virtue. The ancestral instructions are without fault; in essence, all are ways of fulfilling human relationships and institutional requirements.
Your servant wishes Your Majesty to embody the primal creative power and occupy your proper position, modeling yourself on Heaven’s spontaneous workings; to carry forward and fulfill your ancestors’ purposes, preserving their unchanging standards. Consider what Heaven expects of us: our service to Heaven must surely provide the means to satisfy those expectations. Consider what the ancestors have bequeathed to us: our emulation of them must surely provide the means to bring their legacy to fulfillment. If one wishes to fulfill this Way completely and attain the height of good government, what could surpass this? Thus filial piety is the means of serving Heaven and also of following the ancestors; benevolence is the means of diligently caring for the people and also of modeling oneself on Heaven. One principle runs through them all, and all are rooted in the heart.
Your Majesty has expanded the learning of reverent single-mindedness and achieved the government of a dynastic restoration. Lasting peace throughout the Four Seas and the allegiance of all the people have continued for twenty-nine years as though for a single day. Yet you still stoop to seek counsel from grass-cutters…

text:
蕘之言焉是則以斯民為念求治若渴不自
足之極究也臣荷蒙
聖問復綴以法
祖之法
天之說于篇終者誠欲
聖德之隆合上下而同流通古今于一息則繁祉
之錫申重無窮德化之孚淪浹不替矣一得
之見如此若夫泛而不切于用隱而不盡于
言非臣之所敢事
陛下者也臣干瀆
===

punctuated: 蕘之言焉，是則以斯民為念，求治若渴，不自足之極究也。臣荷蒙聖問，復綴以法祖之法天之說于篇終者，誠欲聖德之隆，合上下而同流，通古今于一息，則繁祉之錫申重無窮，德化之孚淪浹不替矣。一得之見如此。若夫泛而不切于用，隱而不盡于言，非臣之所敢事陛下者也。臣干瀆宸嚴，無任戰兢隕越之至。臣謹對。
translation_en: …the words of humble woodcutters. This shows the utmost concern for the people, a thirst for good governance, and an unwillingness to rest content with one’s achievements. Having been honored with Your Majesty’s sagely inquiry, your servant has appended at the end of this essay an account of emulating the ancestors in their emulation of Heaven. My earnest wish is that Your Majesty’s exalted virtue may unite those above and below in a common flow and link past and present in a single breath. Then abundant blessings will be bestowed repeatedly without end, and the influence of moral transformation will penetrate everywhere without diminishing. Such is your servant’s modest insight. As for offering broad statements without practical application, or concealing thoughts rather than expressing them fully, these are ways in which your servant would never dare to serve Your Majesty. Your servant has presumptuously intruded upon Your Majesty’s august dignity and is overcome with trembling and dread of stumbling and falling. Your servant respectfully submits this reply.
